verses.text: In the beginning God created the heaven and the earth.
And the earth as ithout form, and void; and darkness \add as\add* upon the face of the deep: and the Spirit of God moved upon the face of the aters.
And God said, Let there be light: and there as light.
And God sa the light, that \add it as\add* good: and God divided the light from the darkness.
And God called the light Day, and the darkness he called Night: and the evening and the morning ere the first day.
And God said, Let there be a firmament in the midst of the aters, and let it divide the aters from the aters.
And God made the firmament; and divided the aters hich \add ere\add* under the firmament from the aters hich \add ere\add* above the firmament: and it as so.
And God called the firmament Heaven: and the evening and the morning ere the second day.
And God said, Let the aters under the heaven be gathered into one place, and let the dry \add land\add* appear: and it as so.
And God called the dry \add land\add* Earth, and the collection of aters he called Seas: and God sa that it \add as\add* good.
And God said, Let the earth bring forth grass, the herb yielding seed, \add and\add* the fruit-tree yielding fruit after its kind, hose seed \add is\add* in itself, upon the earth: and it as so.

And the earth brought forth grass, \add and\add* herb yielding seed after its kind, and the tree yielding fruit, hose seed \add as\add* in itself, after its kind: and God sa that it \add as\add* good.
And the evening and the morning ere the third day.
And God said, Let there be lights in the firmament of the heaven, to divide the day from the night: and let them be for signs, and for seasons, and for days, and years.
And let them be for lights in the firmament of the heaven, to give light upon the earth: and it as so.
And God made to great lights; the greater light to rule the day, and the lesser light to rule the night: \add he made\add* the stars also.
And God set them in the firmament of the heaven, to give light upon the earth.
And to rule over the day, and over the night, and to divide the light from the darkness: and God sa that it \add as\add* good.
And the evening and the morning ere the fourth day.
And God said, Let the aters bring forth abundantly the moving creature that hath life, and fol \add that\add* may fly above the earth in the open firmament of heaven.
And God created great hales, and every living creature that moveth, hich the aters brought forth abundantly after their kind, and every inged fol after his kind: and God sa that \add it as\add* good.
And God blessed them, saying, Be fruitful, and multiply, and fill the aters in the seas, and let fol multiply in the earth.
And the evening and the morning ere the fifth day.
And God said, Let the earth bring forth the living creature after his kind, cattle, and the creeping animal, and the beast of the earth after his kind: and it as so.
And God made the beast of the earth after his kind, and cattle after their kind, and every animal that creepeth upon the earth after his kind: and God sa that \add it as\add* good.

And God said, Let us make man in our image, after our likeness: and let them have dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the fol of the air, and over the cattle, and over all the earth, and over every creeping animal that creepeth upon the earth.
So God created man in his \add on\add* image, in the image of God created he him; male and female created he them.

And God blessed them, and God said to them, Be fruitful, and multiply, and replenish the earth, and subdue it: and have dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the fol of the air, and over every living animal that moveth upon the earth.

And God said, Behold, I have given you every herb bearing seed, hich \add is\add* upon the face of all the earth, and every tree, in hich \add is\add* the fruit of a tree yielding seed; to you it shall be for food.

And to every beast of the earth, and to every fol of the air, and to every animal that creepeth upon the earth, in hich \add is\add* life, \add I have given\add* every green herb for food: and it as so.
And God sa every thing that he had made, and behold, \add it as\add* very good. And the evening and the morning ere the sixth day.
Thus the heavens and the earth ere finished, and all the host of them.
And on the seventh day God ended his ork hich he had made; and he rested on the seventh day from all his ork hich he had made.
And God blessed the seventh day, and sanctified it: because that in it he had rested from all his ork hich God created and made.
These \add are\add* the generations of the heavens and of the earth hen they ere created, in the day that the LORD God made the earth and the heavens.

And every plant of the field before it as in the earth, and every herb of the field before it gre: for the LORD God had not caused it to rain on the earth, and \add there as\add* not a man to till the ground.
But there ent up a mist from the earth, and atered the hole face of the ground.
And the LORD God formed man \add of\add* the dust of the ground, and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life; and man became a living soul.
And the LORD God planted a garden eastard in Eden; and there he put the man hom he had formed.

And out of the ground made the LORD God to gro every tree that is pleasant to the sight, and good for food; the tree of life also in the midst of the garden, and the tree of knoledge of good and evil.
And a river ent out of Eden to ater the garden: and from thence it as parted, and became into four heads.
The name of the first \add is\add* Pison, hich compasseth the hole land of Havilah, here \add there is\add* gold;
And the gold of that land \add is\add* good: there \add is\add* bdellium and the onyx-stone.
And the name of the second river \add is\add* Gihon: the same that compasseth the hole land of Cush.
And the name of the third river \add is\add* Hiddekel: hich floeth toard the east of Assyria. And the fourth river \add is\add* Euphrates.
And the LORD God took the man, and put him into the garden of Eden, to dress it, and to keep it.
And the LORD God commanded the man, saying, Of every tree of the garden thou mayest freely eat:
But of the tree of the knoledge of good and evil, thou shalt not eat of it: for in the day that thou eatest of it thou shalt surely die.
And the LORD God said, \add It is\add* not good that the man should be alone: I ill make him a help meet for him.

And out of the ground the LORD God formed every beast of the field, and every fol of the air, and brought \add them\add* to Adam to see hat he ould call them; and hatsoever Adam called every living creature, that \add as\add* its name.
And Adam gave names to all cattle, and to the fols of the air, and to every beast of the field: but for Adam there as not found a help meet for him.
And the LORD God caused a deep sleep to fall upon Adam, and he slept; and he took one of his ribs, and closed up the flesh in its place.
And the rib, hich the LORD God had taken from man, he made oman, and brought her to the man.
And Adam said, This \add is\add* no bone of my bones, and flesh of my flesh: she shall be called Woman, because she as taken out of man.
Therefore shall a man leave his father and his mother, and shall cleave to his ife: and they shall be one flesh.
And they ere both naked, the man and his ife, and ere not ashamed.
No the serpent as more subtil than any beast of the field hich the LORD God had made: and he said to the oman, Yea, hath God said, Ye shall not eat of every tree of the garden?
And the oman said to the serpent, We may eat of the fruit of the trees of the garden:
But of the fruit of the tree hich \add is\add* in the midst of the garden, God hath said, Ye shall not eat of it, neither shall ye touch it, lest ye die.
And the serpent said to the oman, Ye shall not surely die:
For God doth kno, that in the day ye eat of it, then your eyes shall be opened: and ye shall be as gods, knoing good and evil.

And hen the oman sa that the tree \add as\add* good for food, and that it \add as\add* pleasant to the eyes, and a tree to be desired to make \add one\add* ise; she took of its fruit, and ate, and gave also to her husband ith her, and he ate.
And the eyes of them both ere opened, and they kne that they \add ere\add* naked: and they seed fig-leaves together, and made for themselves aprons.
And they heard the voice of the LORD God alking in the garden in the cool of the day: and Adam and his ife hid themselves from the presence of the LORD God amongst the trees of the garden.
And the LORD God called to Adam, and said to him, Where \add art\add* thou?
And he said, I heard thy voice in the garden: and I as afraid, because I \add as\add* naked; and I hid myself.
And he said, Who told thee that thou \add ast\add* naked? Hast thou eaten of the tree of hich I commanded thee, that thou shouldest not eat?
And the man said, The oman, hom thou gavest \add to be\add* ith me, she gave me of the tree, and I ate.
And the LORD God said to the oman, What \add is\add* this \add that\add* thou hast done? And the oman said, The serpent beguiled me, and I ate.

And the LORD God said to the serpent, Because thou hast done this, thou \add art\add* cursed above all cattle, and above every beast of the field: upon thy belly shalt thou go, and dust shalt thou eat all the days of thy life:
And I ill put enmity beteen thee and the oman, and beteen thy seed and her seed: it shall bruise thy head, and thou shalt bruise his heel.
To the oman he said, I ill greatly multiply thy sorro and thy conception; in sorro thou shalt bring forth children: and thy desire \add shall be\add* to thy husband, and he shall rule over thee.

And to Adam he said, Because thou hast hearkened to the voice of thy ife, and hast eaten of the tree of hich I commanded thee, saying, Thou shalt not eat of it: cursed \add is\add* the ground for thy sake; in sorro shalt thou eat \add of\add* it all the days of thy life;
Thorns also and thistles shall it bring forth to thee; and thou shalt eat the herb of the field;
In the seat of thy face shalt thou eat bread, till thou shalt return to the ground; for out of it ast thou taken: for dust thou \add art\add*, and to dust shalt thou return.
And Adam called his ife’s name Eve, because she as the mother of all living.
For Adam also and for his ife the LORD God made coats of skins, and clothed them.
And the LORD God said, Behold, the man hath become as one of us, to kno good and evil. And no, lest he should put forth his hand, and take also of the tree of life, and eat, and live for ever:
Therefore the LORD God sent him forth from the garden of Eden, to till the ground from hich he as taken.
So he drove out the man: and he placed at the east of the garden of Eden Cherubim, and a flaming sord hich turned every ay, to keep the ay of the tree of life.
And Adam kne Eve his ife; and she conceived, and bore Cain, and said, I have gotten a man from the LORD.
And she again bore his brother Abel. And Abel as a keeper of sheep, but Cain as a tiller of the ground.
And in process of time it came to pass, that Cain brought of the fruit of the ground an offering to the LORD.
And Abel, he also brought of the firstlings of his flock, and of the fat thereof. And the LORD had respect to Abel, and to his offering:
But to Cain and to his offering he had not respect. And Cain as very roth, and his countenance fell.
And the LORD said to Cain, Why art thou roth? and hy is thy countenance fallen?
If thou doest ell, shalt thou not be accepted? and if thou doest not ell, sin lieth at the door. And to thee \add shall be\add* his desire, and thou shalt rule over him.
And Cain talked ith Abel his brother: and it came to pass hen they ere in the field, that Cain rose up against Abel his brother, and sle him.
And the LORD said to Cain, Where \add is\add* Abel thy brother? And he said, I kno not: \add Am\add* I my brother’s keeper?
And he said, What hast thou done? the voice of thy brother’s blood crieth to me from the ground.
And no \add art\add* thou cursed from the earth, hich hath opened her mouth to receive thy brother’s blood from thy hand;
When thou tillest the ground, it shall not henceforth yield to thee its strength: A fugitive and a vagabond shalt thou be in the earth.
And Cain said to the LORD, My punishment \add is\add* greater than I can bear.

Behold, thou hast driven me this day from the face of the earth; and from thy face shall I be hid; and I shall be a fugitive and a vagabond in the earth; and it ill come to pass, \add that\add* every one that findeth me ill slay me.
And the LORD said to him, Therefore hoever slayeth Cain, vengeance shall be taken on him seven-fold. And the lord set a mark upon Cain, lest any finding him should kill him.
And Cain ent out from the presence of the LORD, and delt in the land of Nod, on the east of Eden.
And Cain kne his ife, and she conceived, and bore Enoch: and he built a city, and called the name of the city, after the name of his son Enoch.
And to Enoch as born Irad: and Irad begat Mehujael: and Mehujael begat Methusael: and Methusael begat Lamech.
And Lamech took to him to ives: the name of the one \add as\add* Adah, and the name of the other Zillah.
And Adah bore Jabal: he as the father of such as dell in tents, and \add of such as have\add* cattle.
And his brother’s name \add as\add* Jubal: he as the father of all such as handle the harp and organ.
And Zillah, she also bore Tubalcain, an instructor of every artificer in brass and iron: and the sister of Tubalcain \add as\add* Naamah.
And Lamech said to his ives, Adah and Zillah, Hear my voice, ye ives of Lamech, hearken to my speech: for I have slain a man to my ounding, and a young man to my hurt.
If Cain shall be avenged seven-fold, truly Lamech seventy and seven-fold.
And Adam kne his ife again, and she bore a son, and called his name Seth: For God, \add said she\add*, hath appointed me another seed instead of Abel, hom Cain sle.
And to Seth, to him also there as born a son; and he called his name Enos: then began men to call upon the name of the LORD.
This \add is\add* the book of the generations of Adam: In the day that God created man, in the likeness of God made he him:
Male and female created he them; and blessed them, and called their name Adam, in the day hen they ere created.
And Adam lived a hundred and thirty years, and begat \add a son\add* in his on likeness, after his image; and called his name Seth:
And the days of Adam after he had begotten Seth ere eight hundred years: and he begat sons and daughters:
And all the days that Adam lived ere nine hundred and thirty years: and he died.
And Seth lived a hundred and five years, and begat Enos:
And Seth lived after he begat Enos eight hundred and seven years, and begat sons and daughters:
And all the days of Seth ere nine hundred and telve years; and he died.
And Enos lived ninety years, and begat Cainan.
And Enos lived after he begat Cainan eight hundred and fifteen years, and begat sons and daughters:
And all the days of Enos ere nine hundred and five years; and he died.
And Cainan lived seventy years, and begat Mahalaleel:
And Cainan lived after he begat Mahalaleel eight hundred and forty years, and begat sons and daughters:
And all the days of Cainan ere nine hundred and ten years; and he died.
And Mahalaleel lived sixty and five years, and begat Jared:
And Mahalaleel lived after he begat Jared eight hundred and thirty years, and begat sons and daughters:
And all the days of Mahalaleel ere eight hundred ninety and five years; and he died.
And Jared lived a hundred sixty and to years, and he begat Enoch:
And Jared lived after he begat Enoch eight hundred years, and begat sons and daughters:
And all the days of Jared ere nine hundred sixty and to years; and he died.
And Enoch lived sixty and five years, and begat Methuselah:
And Enoch alked ith God after he begat Methuselah three hundred years, and begat sons and daughters:
And all the days of Enoch ere three hundred sixty and five years:
And Enoch alked ith God, and he \add as\add* not: for God took him.
And Methuselah lived a hundred eighty and seven years, and begat Lamech:
And Methuselah lived after he begat Lamech seven hundred eighty and to years, and begat sons and daughters:
And all the days of Methuselah ere nine hundred sixty and nine years; and he died.
And Lamech lived a hundred eighty and to years; and begat a son:
And he called his name Noah, saying, This \add same\add* shall comfort us concerning our ork and toil of our hands, because of the ground hich the LORD hath cursed.
And Lamech lived after he begat Noah five hundred ninety and five years, and begat sons and daughters:
And all the days of Lamech ere seven hundred seventy and seven years; and he died.
And Noah as five hundred years old: and Noah begat Shem, Ham, and Japheth.
And it came to pass, hen men began to multiply on the face of the earth, and daughters ere born to them,
That the sons of God sa the daughters of men that they \add ere\add* fair; and they took them ives of all hom they chose.
And the LORD said, My spirit shall not alays strive ith man, for that he also \add is\add* flesh: yet his days shall be a hundred and tenty years.

There ere giants in the earth in those days; and also after that, hen the sons of God came in to the daughters of men, and they bore \add children\add* to them: the same \add became\add* mighty men, ho \add ere\add* of old, men of renon.
And God sa that the ickedness of man \add as\add* great in the earth, and \add that\add* every imagination of the thoughts of his heart \add as\add* only evil continually.
And the LORD repented that he had made man on the earth, and it grieved him at his heart.
And the LORD said, I ill destroy man hom I have created, from the face of the earth, both man and beast, and the creeping animal, and the fols of the air; for I repent that I have made them.
But Noah found grace in the eyes of the LORD.
These \add are\add* the generations of Noah: Noah as a just man, \add and\add* perfect in his generations, \add and\add* Noah alked ith God.
And Noah begat three sons, Shem, Ham, and Japheth.
The earth also as corrupt before God; and the earth as filled ith violence.
And God looked upon the earth, and behold, it as corrupt: for all flesh had corrupted his ay upon the earth.
And God said to Noah, The end of all flesh is come before me; for the earth is filled ith violence through them: and behold, I ill destroy them ith the earth.
Make thee an ark of gopher-ood: rooms shalt thou make in the ark, and shalt pitch it ithin and ithout ith pitch.
And this \add is the fashion\add* in hich thou shalt make it: the length of the ark \add shall be\add* three hundred cubits, the breadth of it fifty cubits, and the height of it thirty cubits.

A indo shalt thou make to the ark, and in a cubit shalt thou finish it above; and the door of the ark shalt thou set in its side: \add ith\add* loer, second, and third \add stories\add* shalt thou make it.

And behold, I, even I do bring a flood of aters upon the earth, to destroy all flesh, in hich \add is\add* the breath of life, from under heaven: \add and\add* every thing that \add is\add* on the earth shall die.
But ith thee ill I establish my covenant: and thou shalt come into the ark, thou, and thy sons, and thy ife, and thy sons’ ives ith thee.
And of every living thing of all flesh, to of every \add sort\add* shalt thou bring into the ark, to keep \add them\add* alive ith thee: they shall be male and female.
Of fols after their kind, and of cattle after their kind, of every creeping animal of the earth after its kind, to of every \add sort\add* shall come to thee, to keep \add them\add* alive.
And take thou to thee of all food that is eaten, and thou shalt gather \add it\add* to thee; and it shall be for food for thee, and for them.
Thus did Noah; according to all that God commanded him, so did he.
And the LORD said to Noah, Come thou and all thy house into the ark: for thee have I seen righteous before me in this generation.
Of every clean beast thou shalt take to thee by sevens, the male and his female: and of beasts that \add are\add* not clean by to, the male and his female.
Of fols of the air also by sevens, the male and the female; to keep seed alive on the face of all the earth.
For yet seven days, and I ill cause it to rain upon the earth forty days and forty nights: and every living substance that I have made ill I destroy from the face of the earth.
And Noah did according to all that the LORD commanded him.
And Noah \add as\add* six hundred years old hen the flood of aters as on the earth.
And Noah ent in, and his sons, and his ife, and his sons’ ives ith him, into the ark, because of the aters of the flood.
Of clean beasts, and of beasts that \add are\add* not clean, and of fols, and of every animal that creepeth upon the earth;
There ent in to and to to Noah into the ark, the male and the female, as God had commanded Noah.
And it came to pass after seven days, that the aters of the flood ere upon the earth.
In the six hundredth year of Noah’s life, in the second month, the seventeenth day of the month, the same day ere all the fountains of the great deep broken up, and the indos of heaven ere opened.
And the rain as upon the earth forty days and forty nights.
In the same day entered Noah, and Shem, and Ham, and Japheth, the sons of Noah, and Noah’s ife, and the three ives of his sons ith them, into the ark.

They, and every beast after his kind, and all the cattle after their kind, and every creeping animal that creepeth upon the earth after his kind, and every fol after his kind, every bird of every sort.
And they ent in to Noah into the ark, to and to of all flesh, in hich \add is\add* the breath of life.
And they that entered, ent in male and female of all flesh, as God had commanded him: and the LORD shut him in.
And the flood as forty days upon the earth: and the aters increased, and bore up the ark, and it as lifted above the earth.
And the aters prevailed, and ere increased greatly upon the earth: and the ark moved upon the face of the aters.
And the aters prevailed exceedingly upon the earth; and all the high hills that \add ere\add* under the hole heaven ere covered.
Fifteen cubits upard did the aters prevail: and the mountains ere covered.
And all flesh died that moved upon the earth, both of fol, and of cattle, and of beast, and of every creeping animal that creepeth upon the earth, and every man:
All in hose nostrils \add as\add* the breath of life, of all that \add as\add* on the dry \add land\add*, died.

And every living substance as destroyed hich as upon the face of the ground, both man, and cattle, and the creeping animals, and the fol of heaven; and they ere destroyed from the earth; and Noah only remained \add alive\add*, and they that \add ere\add* ith him in the ark.
And the aters prevailed upon the earth a hundred and fifty days.
And God remembered Noah, and every living animal, and all the cattle that \add ere\add* ith him in the ark: and God made a ind to pass over the earth, and the aters ere checked.
The fountains also of the deep, and the indos of heaven ere stopped, and the rain from heaven as restrained;
And the aters returned from off the earth continually: and after the end of the hundred and fifty days the aters ere abated.
And the ark rested in the seventh month, on the seventeenth day of the month, upon the mountains of Ararat.
And the aters decreased continually, till the tenth month: in the tenth \add month\add*, on the first \add day\add* of the month, ere the tops of the mountains seen.
And it came to pass at the end of forty days, that Noah opened the indo of the ark hich he had made:
And he sent forth a raven, hich ent forth to and fro, till the aters ere dried from off the earth.
Also he sent forth a dove from him, to see if the aters ere abated from off the face of the ground;

But the dove found no rest for the sole of her foot, and she returned to him into the ark; for the aters \add ere\add* on the face of the hole earth. Then he put forth his hand, and took her, and pulled her in to him into the ark.
And he stayed yet other seven days, and again he sent forth the dove out of the ark;
And the dove came in to him in the evening, and lo, in her mouth \add as\add* an olive-leaf plucked off: So Noah kne that the aters ere abated from off the earth.
And he stayed yet other seven days, and sent forth the dove; hich returned not again to him any more.

And it came to pass in the six hundredth and first year, in the first \add month\add*, the first \add day\add* of the month, the aters ere dried from off the earth: and Noah removed the covering of the ark, and looked, and behold, the face of the ground as dry.
And in the second month, on the seven and tentieth day of the month, as the earth dried.
And God spoke to Noah, saying,
Go forth from the ark, thou, and thy ife, and thy sons, and thy sons’ ives ith thee.

Bring forth ith thee every living animal that \add is\add* ith thee, of all flesh, of fol, and of cattle, and of every creeping animal that creepeth upon the earth; that they may breed abundantly on the earth, and be fruitful, and multiply upon the earth.
And Noah ent forth, and his sons, and his ife, and his sons’ ives ith him:
Every beast, every creeping animal, and every fol, \add and\add* hatsoever creepeth upon the earth, after their kinds, ent out of the ark.
And Noah built an altar to the LORD, and took of every clean beast, and of every clean fol, and offered burnt-offerings on the altar.

And the LORD smelled a seet savor; and the LORD said in his heart, I ill not again curse the ground any more for man’s sake; for the imagination of man’s heart \add is\add* evil from his youth: neither ill I again smite any more every living animal as I have done.
While the earth remaineth, seed-time and harvest, and cold and heat, and summer and inter, and day and night shall not cease.
And God blessed Noah and his sons, and said to them, Be fruitful, and multiply, and replenish the earth.

And the fear of you and the dread of you shall be upon every beast of the earth, and upon every fol of the air, upon all that moveth \add on\add* the earth, and upon all the fishes of the sea; into your hand are they delivered.
Every moving thing that liveth shall be food for you; even as the green herb have I given you all things:
But flesh ith the life of it, \add hich is\add* its blood, shall ye not eat.
And surely your blood of your lives ill I require: at the hand of every beast ill I require it: and at the hand of man, at the hand of every man’s brother ill I require the life of man.
Whoever sheddeth man’s blood, by man shall his blood be shed: for in the image of God made he man.
And you, be ye fruitful, and multiply, bring forth abundantly in the earth, and multiply therein.
And God spoke to Noah, and to his sons ith him, saying,
And I, behold, I establish my covenant ith you, and ith your seed after you;
And ith every living creature that \add is\add* ith you, of the fol, of the cattle, and of every beast of the earth ith you, from all that go out of the ark, to every beast of the earth.
And I ill establish my covenant ith you; neither shall all flesh be cut off any more by the aters of a flood; neither shall there any more be a flood to destroy the earth.
And God said, This \add is\add* the token of the covenant hich I make beteen me and you and every living creature that \add is\add* ith you, for perpetual generations.
I do set my bo in the cloud, and it shall be for a token of a covenant beteen me and the earth.
And it shall come to pass, hen I bring a cloud over the earth, that the bo shall be seen in the cloud:
And I ill remember my covenant, hich \add is\add* beteen me and you and every living creature of all flesh; and the aters shall no more become a flood to destroy all flesh.
And the bo shall be in the cloud; and I ill look upon it, that I may remember the everlasting covenant beteen God and every living creature of all flesh that \add is\add* upon the earth.
And God said to Noah, This \add is\add* the token of the covenant hich I have established beteen me and all flesh that \add is\add* upon the earth.
And the sons of Noah that ent forth from the ark, ere Shem, and Ham, and Japheth: and Ham \add as\add* the father of Canaan.
These three \add ere\add* the sons of Noah: and from them as the hole earth overspread.
And Noah began \add to be\add* a husbandman, and he planted a vineyard:
And he drank of the ine, and as drunken, and he as uncovered ithin his tent.
And Ham, the father of Canaan, sa the nakedness of his father, and told his to brethren ithout.

And Shem and Japheth took a garment, and laid \add it\add* upon both their shoulders, and ent backard, and covered the nakedness of their father: and their faces \add ere\add* backard, and they sa not their father’s nakedness.

And there came to angels to Sodom at evening; and Lot sat in the gate of Sodom; and Lot seeing \add them\add*, rose to meet them; and he boed himself ith his face toards the ground;

And he said, Behold no, my lords, turn, I pray you, into your servant’s house, and tarry all night, and ash your feet, and ye shall rise early, and go on your ays. And they said, Nay; but e ill abide in the street all night.
And he urged them greatly; and they turned in to him, and entered into his house; and he made them a feast, and baked unleavened bread, and they ate.
But before they lay don, the men of the city, \add even\add* the men of Sodom, surrounded the house, both old and young, all the people from every quarter:
And they called to Lot, and said to him, Where \add are\add* the men ho came in to thee this night? bring them out to us, that e may kno them.
And Lot ent out at the door to them, and shut the door after him,
And said, I pray you, brethren, do not so ickedly.

Behold no, I have to daughters ho have not knon man; let me, I pray you, bring them out to you, and do ye to them as \add is\add* good in your eyes: only to these men do nothing; for therefore came they under the shado of my roof.

And they said, Stand back. And they said \add again\add*, This one \add man\add* came in to sojourn, and he ill needs be a judge: No ill e deal orse ith thee than ith them. And they pressed hard upon the man, Lot, and came near to break the door.
But the men put forth their hand, and pulled Lot into the house to them, and shut the door.
And they smote the men that \add ere\add* at the door of the house ith blindness, both small and great: so that they earied themselves to find the door.
And the men said to Lot, Hast thou here any besides? son-in-la, and thy sons, and thy daughters, and hatever thou hast in the city, bring \add them\add* out of this place:
For e ill destroy this place, because the cry of them has become great before the face of the LORD; and the LORD hath sent us to destroy it.
And Lot ent out and spoke to his sons-in-la, ho married his daughters, and said, Arise, depart from this place; for the LORD ill destroy this city: but he seemed to his sons-in-la as one that mocked.
And hen the morning arose, then the angels hastened Lot, saying, Arise, take thy ife, and thy to daughters ho are here; lest thou be consumed in the iniquity of the city.

And hile he lingered, the men laid hold upon his hand, and upon the hand of his ife, and upon the hand of his to daughters: the LORD being merciful to him: and they brought him forth, and set him ithout the city.

And it came to pass, hen they had brought them forth abroad, that he said, Escape for thy life: look not behind thee, neither stay thou in all the plain: escape to the mountain, lest thou be consumed.
And Lot said to them, Oh, not so, my Lord!

Behold no, thy servant hath found grace in thy sight, and thou hast magnified thy mercy, hich thou hast shon to me in saving my life: and I cannot escape to the mountain, lest some evil should take me, and I die:
Behold no, this city is near to flee to, and it \add is\add* a small one: Oh, let me escape thither! (\add Is\add* it not a small one?) and my soul shall live.
And he said to him, See, I have accepted thee concerning this thing also, that I ill not overthro this city, for hich thou hast spoken.
Haste thee, escape thither: for I cannot do any thing till thou hast come thither: therefore the name of the city as called Zoar.
The sun had risen upon the earth hen Lot entered into Zoar.
Then the LORD rained upon Sodom and upon Gomorrah brimstone and fire from the LORD out of heaven;
And he overthre those cities, and all the plain, and all the inhabitants of the cities, and that hich gre upon the ground.
But his ife looked back from behind him, and she became a pillar of salt.
And Abraham rose early in the morning, to the place ere he stood before the LORD:
And he looked toards Sodom and Gomorrah, and toards all the land of the plain, and beheld, and lo, the smoke of the country ent up as the smoke of a furnace.
And it came to pass, hen God destroyed the cities of the plain, that God remembered Abraham, and sent Lot out of the midst of the overthro, hen he overthre the cities in hich Lot delt.
And Lot ent up from Zoar, and delt in the mountain, and his to daughters ith him; for he feared to dell in Zoar: and he delt in a cave, he, and his to daughters.
And the first-born said to the younger, Our father \add is\add* old, and \add there is\add* not a man on the earth to come in to us after the manner of all the earth:
Come, let us make our father drink ine, and e ill lie ith him, that e may preserve seed of our father.
And they made their father drink ine that night: and the first-born ent in and lay ith her father; and he perceived not hen she lay don, nor hen she arose.

And it came to pass on the morro that the first born said to the younger, Behold, I lay yesternight ith my father; let us make him drink ine this night also; and go thou in, \add and\add* lie ith him, that e may preserve seed of our father.
And they made their father drink ine that night also: and the younger arose and lay ith him; and he perceived not hen she lay don, nor hen she arose.
Thus ere both the daughters of Lot ith child by their father.
And the first-born bore a son, and called his name Moab: the same \add is\add* the father of the Moabites to this day.
And the younger, she also bore a son, and called his name Ben-ammi: the same \add is\add* the father of the children of Ammon to this day.
And Abraham journeyed from thence toards the south country, and delt beteen Kadash and Shur, and sojourned in Gerar.
And Abraham said of Sarah his ife, she is my sister: And Abimelech king of Gerar sent and took Sarah.
But God came to Abimelech in a dream by night, and said to him, Behold, thou \add art but\add* a dead man, on account of the oman hom thou hast taken: for she \add is\add* a man’s ife.
But Abimelech had not come near her: and he said, LORD, ilt thou also slay a righteous nation?
Said he not to me, She \add is\add* my sister? and she, even she herself said, He \add is\add* my brother: in the integrity of my heart, and innocence of my hands have I done this.
And God said to him in a dream, Yea, I kno that thou didst this in the integrity of thy heart; for I also ithheld thee from sinning against me: therefore I suffered thee not to touch her.

No therefore restore to the man \add his\add* ife, for he \add is\add* a prophet, and he shall pray for thee, and thou shalt live: and if thou shalt not restore \add her\add*, kno thou that thou shalt surely die, thou and all that \add are\add* thine.
Therefore Abimelech rose early in the morning, and called all his servants, and told all these things in their ears: and the men ere greatly afraid.

Then Abimelech called Abraham, and said to him, What has thou done to us? and in hat have I offended thee, that thou hast brought on me and on my kingdom a great sin? thou hast done deeds to me that ought not to be done.
And Abimelech said to Abraham, What saest thou, that thou hast done this thing?
And Abraham said, Because I thought, surely the fear of God \add is\add* not in this place; and they ill slay me for my ife’s sake.
And yet indeed \add she is\add* my sister: she \add is\add* the daughter of my father, but not the daughter of my mother; and she became my ife.

And it came to pass, hen God caused me to ander from my father’s house, that I said to her, This \add is\add* thy kindness hich thou shalt sho to me; At every place hither e shall come, say of me, He \add is\add* my brother.
And Abimelech took sheep, and oxen, and men-servants, and omen-servants, and gave \add them\add* to Abraham, and restored to him Sarah his ife.
And Abimelech said, Behold, my land \add is\add* before thee: dell here it pleaseth thee.

And to Sarah he said, Behold, I have given thy brother a thousand \add pieces\add* of silver: behold, he \add is\add* to thee a covering of the eyes, to all that \add are\add* ith thee, and ith all \add other\add*: thus she as reproved.
So Abraham prayed to God: and God healed Abimelech, and his ife, and his maid-servants, and they bore \add children\add*.
For the LORD had made barren all the females of the house of Abimelech, because of Sarah, Abraham’s ife.
And the LORD visited Sarah as he had said, and the LORD did to Sarah as he had spoken.
For Sarah conceived and bore Abraham a son in his old age, at the set time of hich God had spoken to him.
And Abraham called the name of his son that as born to him, hom Sarah bore to him, Isaac.
And Abraham circumcised his son Isaac, being eight days old, as God had commanded him.
And Abraham as a hundred years old, hen his son Isaac as born to him.
And Sarah said, God hath made me to laugh, \add so that\add* all that hear ill laugh ith me.
And she said, Who ould have said to Abraham, that Sarah shall nurse children? for I have borne him a son in his old age.
And the child gre, and as eaned: and Abraham made a great feast the day that Isaac as eaned.
And Sarah sa the son of Hagar the Egyptian, hich she had borne to Abraham, mocking.
Wherefore, she said to Abraham, Cast out this bond-oman, and her son: for the son of this bond-oman shall not be heir ith my son, \add even\add* ith Isaac.
And the thing as very grievous in Abraham’s sight, because of his son.

And God said to Abraham, Let it not be grievous in thy sight, because of the lad, and because of thy bond-oman; in all that Sarah hath said to thee, hearken to her voice: for in Isaac shall thy seed be called.
And also of the son of the bond-oman ill I make a nation, because he \add is\add* thy seed.

And Abraham rose early in the morning, and took bread, and a bottle of ater, and gave \add it\add* to Hagar (putting \add it\add* on her shoulder) and the child, and sent her aay; and she departed, and andered in the ilderness of Beer-sheba.
And the ater as spent in the bottle, and she cast the child under one of the shrubs.

And she ent, and sat her don over against \add him\add*, a good ay off, as it ere a bo-shot: for she said, Let me not see the death of the child. And she sat over against \add him\add*, and raised her voice, and ept.

And God heard the voice of the lad: and the angel of God called to Hagar out of heaven, and said to her, What aileth thee, Hagar? fear not; for God hath heard the voice of the lad here he \add is\add*.
Arise, lift up the lad, and hold him in thy hand: for I ill make him a great nation.
And God opened her eyes, and she sa a ell of ater: and she ent, and filled the bottle ith ater, and gave the lad drink.
And God as ith the lad; and he gre, and delt in the ilderness, and became an archer.
And he delt in the ilderness of Paran: and his mother took for him a ife out of the land of Egypt.
And it came to pass at that time, that Abimelech, and Phichol the chief captain of his host, spoke to Abraham, saying, God \add is\add* ith thee in all that thou doest:

No therefore sear to me here by God, that thou ilt not deal falsely ith me, nor ith my son, nor ith my son’s son: \add but\add* according to the kindness that I have done to thee, thou shalt do to me, and to the land in hich thou hast sojourned.
And Abraham said, I ill sear.
And Abraham reproved Abimelech, because of a ell of ater, hich Abimelech’s servants had violently taken aay.
And Abimelech said, I kno not ho hath done this thing: neither didst thou tell me, neither yet have I heard \add of it\add*, but to-day.
And Abraham took sheep and oxen, and gave them to Abimelech: and both of them made a covenant.
And Abraham set seven ee-lambs of the flock by themselves.
And Abimelech said to Abraham, What \add mean\add* these seven ee-lambs, hich thou hast set by themselves?
And he said, For \add these\add* seven ee-lambs shalt thou take from my hand, that they may be a itness to me, that I have digged this ell.
Wherefore he called that place Beer-sheba: because there they sore both of them.
Thus they made a covenant at Beer-sheba: Then Abimelech arose, and Phichol the chief captain of his host, and they returned into the land of the Philistines.
And \add Abraham\add* planted a grove in Beer-sheba, and called there on the name of the LORD, the everlasting God.
And Abraham sojourned in the land of the Philistines many days.
And it came to pass after these things, that God tempted Abraham, and said to him, Abraham: and he said, Behold, \add here\add* I \add am\add*.

And he said, Take no thy son, thy only \add son\add* Isaac, hom thou lovest, and go into the land of Moriah; and offer him there for a burnt-offering upon one of the mountains hich I ill name to thee.

And Abraham rose early in the morning, and saddled his ass, and took to of his young men ith him, and Isaac his son, and cleft the ood for the burnt-offering, and rose and ent to the place hich God had named to him.
Then on the third day Abraham lifted up his eyes, and sa the place afar off.
And Abraham said to his young men, Abide you here ith the ass, and I and the lad ill go yonder and orship, and return to you.
And Abraham took the ood of the burnt-offering, and laid \add it\add* upon Isaac his son; and he took the fire in his hand, and a knife: and they ent both of them together.
And Isaac spoke to Abraham his father, and said, My father: and he said, here \add am\add* I, my son. And he said, Behold the fire and the ood: but here \add is\add* the lamb for a burnt-offering?
And Abraham said, My son, God ill provide himself a lamb for a burnt-offering: so they ent both of them together.
And they came to the place hich God had named to him; and Abraham built an altar there, and laid the ood in order; and bound Isaac his son, and laid him on the altar upon the ood.
And Abraham stretched forth his hand, and took the knife to slay his son.
And the angel of the LORD called to him from heaven, and said, Abraham, Abraham. And he said, Here \add am\add* I.
And he said, Lay not thy hand upon the lad, neither do thou any thing to him: for no I kno that thou fearest God, seeing thou hast not ithheld from me thy son, thy only \add son\add*.

And Abraham lifted up his eyes, and looked, and behold, behind \add him\add* a ram caught in a thicket by his horns: And Abraham ent and took the ram, and offered him for a burnt-offering in the stead of his son.
And Abraham called the name of that place Jehovah-jireh: as it is said \add to\add* this day, In the mount of the LORD it ill be seen.
And the angel of the LORD called to Abraham from heaven the second time,
And said, By myself have I sorn, saith the LORD, for because thou hast done this thing, and hast not ithheld thy son, thy only \add son\add*:

That in blessing I ill bless thee, and in multiplying I ill multiply thy seed as the stars of heaven, and as the sand hich \add is\add* on the sea shore; and thy seed shall possess the gate of his enemies;
And in thy seed shall all the nations of the earth be blessed: because thou hast obeyed my voice.
So Abraham returned to his young men, and they rose and ent together to Beer-sheba; and Abraham delt at Beer-sheba.
And it came to pass after these things, that it as told to Abraham, saying, Behold, Milcah, she hath also borne children to thy brother Nahor;
Huz his first-born, and Buz his brother, and Kemuel the father of Aram,
And Chesed, and Hazo, and Pildash, and Jidlaph, and Bethuel.
And Bethuel begat Rebekah: these eight Milcah bore to Nahor Abraham’s brother.
And his concubine, hose name \add as\add* Reumah, she bore also Tebah, and Gaham, and Thahash, and Maachah.
And Sarah as a hundred and tenty-seven years old: \add these ere\add* the years of the life of Sarah.
And Sarah died in Kirjath-arba; the same \add is\add* Hebron in the land of Canaan: And Abraham came to mourn for Sarah, and to eep for her.
And Abraham stood up from before his dead, and spoke to the sons of Heth, saying,
I \add am\add* a stranger and a sojourner ith you; give me a possession of a burying-place ith you, that I may bury my dead out of my sight.
And the children of Heth ansered Abraham, saying to him,
Hear us, my lord; thou \add art\add* a mighty prince among us: in the choice of our sepulchers bury thy dead: none of us ill ithhold from thee his sepulcher, but that thou mayest bury thy dead.
And Abraham stood up and boed himself to the people of the land, to the children of Heth.
And he communed ith them, saying, If it is your mind that I should bury my dead out of my sight, hear me, and entreat for me to Ephron the son of Zohar,
That he may give me the cave of Machpelah, hich he hath, hich \add is\add* in the end of his field; for as much money as it is orth he shall give it me, for a possession of a burying-place among you.
And Ephron delt among the children of Heth. And Ephron the Hittite ansered Abraham in the audience of the children of Heth, of all that entered the gates of his city, saying,
Nay, my lord, hear me: the field give I to thee, and the cave that \add is\add* in it, I give it to thee; in the presence of the sons of my people I give it to thee: bury thy dead.
And Abraham boed himself before the people of the land.

And he spoke to Ephron in the audience of the people of the land, saying, But if thou \add ilt give it\add*, I pray thee, hear me: I ill give thee money for the field: take \add it\add* of me, and I ill bury my dead there.
And Ephron ansered Abraham, saying to him,
My lord, hearken to me: the land \add is orth\add* four hundred shekels of silver; hat \add is\add* that betixt me and thee? bury therefore thy dead.

And Abraham hearkened to Ephron; and Abraham eighed to Ephron the silver hich he had named in the audience of the sons of Heth, four hundred shekels of silver, current \add money\add* ith the merchant.

And the field of Ephron, hich \add as\add* in Machpelah, hich \add as\add* before Mamre, the field and the cave hich \add as\add* in it, and all the trees that \add ere\add* in the field, that \add ere\add* in all the borders round about, ere made sure
To Abraham for a possession in the presence of the children of Heth, before all that entered the gate of his city.
And after this, Abraham buried Sarah his ife in the cave of the field of Machpelah, before Mamre: the same \add is\add* Hebron in the land of Canaan.
And the field, and the cave that \add is\add* in it ere made sure to Abraham for a possession of a burying-place, by the sons of Heth.
And Abraham as old \add and\add* far advanced in age: and the LORD had blessed Abraham in all things.
And Abraham said to his eldest servant of his house, that ruled over all that he had, Put, I pray thee, thy hand under my thigh:
And I ill make thee sear by the LORD, the God of heaven and the God of the earth, that thou ilt not take a ife for my son of the daughters of the Canaanites among hom I dell:
But thou shalt go to my country, and to my kindred, and take a ife for my son Isaac.
And the servant said to him, It may be the oman ill not be illing to follo me to this land: must I needs bring thy son again to the land from hence thou camest?
And Abraham said to him, Beare that thou bring not my son thither again.

The LORD God of heaven, ho took me from my father’s house, and from the land of my kindred, and ho spoke to me, and ho sore to me, saying, To thy seed I ill give this land: he ill send his angel before thee, and thou shalt take a ife for my son from thence.
And if the oman shall not be illing to follo thee, then thou shalt be clear from this my oath; only bring not my son thither again.
And the servant put his hand under the thigh of Abraham his master, and sore to him concerning that matter.
And the servant took ten camels, of the camels of his master, and departed; (for all the goods of his master \add ere\add* in his hands:) and he arose, and ent to Mesopotamia, to the city of Nahor.
And he made his camels to kneel don ithout the city by a ell of ater, at the time of the evening, the time hen omen go out to dra \add ater\add*:
And he said, O LORD God of my master Abraham, I pray thee, prosper me this day, and sho kindness to my master Abraham.
Behold, I stand \add here\add* by the ell of ater; and the daughters of the men of the city come out to dra ater:

And let it come to pass, that the damsel to hom I shall say, Let don thy pitcher, I pray thee, that I may drink; and she shall say, Drink, and I ill give thy camels drink also: \add let the same be\add* she \add that\add* thou hast appointed for thy servant Isaac; and by that shall I kno that thou hast shon kindness to my master.
And it came to pass before he had done speaking, that behold, Rebekah came out, ho as born to Bethuel son of Milcah, the ife of Nahor, Abraham’s brother, ith her pitcher upon her shoulder.
And the damsel \add as\add* very fair to look upon, a virgin, neither had any man knon her: and she ent don to the ell, and filled her pitcher, and came up.
And the servant ran to meet her, and said, Let me, I pray thee, drink a little ater from thy pitcher.
And she said, Drink, my lord. And she hasted, and let don her pitcher upon her hand, and gave him drink.
And hen she had done giving him drink, she said, I ill dra \add ater\add* for thy camels also, till they have done drinking.
And she hasted, and emptied her pitcher into the trough, and ran again to the ell to dra \add ater\add*, and dre for all his camels.
And the man, ondering at her, held his peace, to kno hether the LORD had made his journey prosperous, or not.
And it came to pass as the camels had done drinking, that the man took a golden ear-ring of half a shekel eight, and to bracelets for her hands of ten \add shekels\add* eight of gold;
And said, Whose daughter \add art\add* thou? tell me, I pray thee: is there room \add in\add* thy father’s house for us to lodge in?
And she said to him, I \add am\add* the daughter of Bethuel the son of Milcah, hom she bore to Nahor.
She said moreover to him, We have both stra and provender enough, and room to lodge in.
And the man boed his head, and orshipped the LORD.

And he said, Blessed \add be\add* the LORD God of my master Abraham, ho hath not left my master destitute of his mercy and his truth: I \add being\add* in the ay, the LORD led me to the house of my master’s brethren.
And the damsel ran, and told these things to her mother’s house.
And Rebekah had a brother, and his name \add as\add* Laban: and Laban ran out to the man, to the ell.

And it came to pass hen he sa the ear-ring and bracelets upon his sister’s hands, and hen he heard the ords of Rebekah his sister, saying, Thus spoke the man to me; that he came to the man; and behold, he stood by the camels at the ell.
And he said, Come in, thou blessed of the LORD; hy standest thou ithout? for I have prepared the house, and room for the camels.
And the man came into the house: and he ungirded his camels, and gave stra and provender for the camels, and ater to ash his feet, and the men’s feet that \add ere\add* ith him.
And there as set \add food\add* before him to eat: but he said, I ill not eat, until I have told my errand. And he said, Speak on.
And he said, I \add am\add* Abraham’s servant.
And the LORD hath blessed my master greatly, and he is become great: and he hath given him flocks, and herds, and silver, and gold, and men-servants, and maid-servants, and camels, and asses.
And Sarah, my master’s ife, bore a son to my master hen she as old: and to him hath he given all that he hath.
And my master made me sear, saying, Thou shalt not take a ife for my son of the daughters of the Canaanites, in hose land I dell:
But thou shalt go to my father’s house, and to my kindred, and take a ife for my son.
And I said to my master, It may be the oman ill not follo me.
And he said to me, The LORD, before hom I alk, ill send his angel ith thee, and prosper thy ay; and thou shalt take a ife for my son of my kindred, and of my father’s house.
Then shalt thou be clear from \add this\add* my oath, hen thou comest to my kindred; and if they give not thee \add one\add*, thou shalt be clear from my oath.
And I came this day to the ell, and said, O LORD God of my master Abraham, if no thou dost prosper my ay hich I go:
Behold, I stand by the ell of ater; and it shall come to pass, that hen the virgin cometh forth to dra \add ater\add*, and I say to her, Give me, I pray thee, a little ater of thy pitcher to drink;
And she saith to me, Both drink thou, and I ill also dra for thy camels: \add let\add* the same \add be\add* the oman hom the LORD hath pointed out for my master’s son.

And before I had done speaking in my heart, behold, Rebekah came forth ith her pitcher on her shoulder; and she ent don to the ell, and dre \add ater\add*: and I said to her, Let me drink, I pray thee.
And she made haste, and let don her pitcher from her \add shoulder\add*, and said, Drink, and I ill give thy camels drink also: so I drank, and she made the camels drink also.

And I asked her, and said, Whose daughter \add art\add* thou? And she said, The daughter of Bethuel, Nahor’s son, hom Milcah bore to him: and I put the ear-ring upon her face, and the bracelets upon her hands.
And I boed my head, and orshipped the LORD, and blessed the LORD God of my master Abraham, ho had led me in the right ay to take my master’s brother’s daughter for his son.
And no if you ill deal kindly and truly ith my master, tell me; and if not, tell me; that I may turn to the right hand, or to the left.
Then Laban and Bethuel ansered, and said, The thing proceedeth from the LORD: e cannot speak to thee bad or good.
Behold, Rebekah \add is\add* before thee, take \add her\add*, and go, and let her be thy master’s son’s ife, as the LORD hath spoken.
And it came to pass, that hen Abraham’s servant heard their ords, he orshipped the LORD, \add boing himself\add* to the earth.
And the servant brought forth jeels of silver, and jeels of gold, and raiment, and gave \add them\add* to Rebekah: He gave also to her brother and to her mother precious things.
And they ate and drank, he and the men that \add ere\add* ith him, and tarried all night; and they rose in the morning, and he said, Send me aay to my master.
And her brother and her mother said, Let the damsel abide ith us \add a fe\add* days, at the least ten; after that she shall go.
And he said to them, Hinder me not, seeing the LORD hath prospered my ay: send me aay, that I may go to my master.
And they said, We ill call the damsel, and inquire at her mouth.
And they called Rebekah, and said to her, Wilt thou go ith this man? And she said, I ill go.
And they sent aay Rebekah their sister, and her nurse, and Abraham’s servant, and his men.
And they blessed Rebekah, and said to her, Thou \add art\add* our sister, be thou \add the mother\add* of thousands of millions, and let thy seed possess the gate of those ho hate them.
And Rebekah arose, and her damsels, and they rode upon the camels, and folloed the man: and the servant took Rebekah, and ent his ay.
And Isaac came from the ay of the ell Lahai-roi; for he delt in the south country.
And Isaac ent out to meditate in the field at evening: and he lifted up his eyes, and sa, and behold, the camels \add ere\add* coming.
And Rebekah lifted up her eyes, and hen she sa Isaac, she alighted from the camel.

For she \add had\add* said to the servant, What man \add is\add* this that alketh in the field to meet us? And the servant \add had\add* said, It \add is\add* my master: therefore she took a vail and covered herself.
And the servant told Isaac all things that he had done.
And Isaac brought her into his mother Sarah’s tent, and took Rebekah, and she became his ife; and he loved her: and Isaac as comforted after his mother’s \add death\add*.
Then again Abraham took a ife, and her name \add as\add* Keturah.
And she bore him Zimran, and Jokshan, and Medan, and Midian, and Ishbak, and Shuah.
And Jokshan begat Sheba, and Dedan. And the sons of Dedan ere Asshurim, and Letushim and Leummim.
And the sons of Midian; Ephah, and Epher, and Hanoch, and Abidah, and Eldaah. All these \add ere\add* the children of Keturah.
And Abraham gave all that he had to Isaac.
But to the sons of the concubines hich Abraham had, Abraham gave gifts, and sent them aay from Isaac his son (hile he yet lived) eastard, to the east country.
And these \add are\add* the days of the years of Abraham’s life hich he lived, a hundred and seventy five years.
Then Abraham expired, and died in a good old age, an old man, and full \add of years\add*; and as gathered to his people.
And his sons Isaac and Ishmael buried him in the cave of Machpelah, in the field of Ephron the son of Zohar the Hittite, hich \add is\add* before Mamre;
The field hich Abraham purchased of the sons of Heth: there as Abraham buried, and Sarah his ife.
And it came to pass after the death of Abraham, that God blessed his son Isaac: and Isaac delt by the ell Lahai-roi.
No these \add are\add* the generations of Ishmael, Abraham’s son, hom Hagar the Egyptian, Sarah’s handmaid, bore to Abraham.
And these \add are\add* the names of the sons of Ishmael, by their names, according to their generations: The first-born of Ishmael, Nebajoth; and Kedar, and Adbeel, and Mibsam,
And Mishma, and Dumah, and Massa,
Hadar, and Tema, Jetur, Naphish, and Kedemah:
These \add are\add* the sons of Ishmael, and these \add are\add* their names, by their tons, and by their castles; telve princes according to their nations.
And these \add are\add* the years of the life of Ishmael; a hundred and thirty and seven years: and he expired and died, and as gathered to his people.
And they delt from Havilah to Shur, that \add is\add* before Egypt, as thou goest toards Assyria: \add and\add* he died in the presence of all his brethren.
And these \add are\add* the generations of Isaac, Abraham’s son: Abraham begat Isaac:
And Isaac as forty years old hen he took Rebekah to ife, the daughter of Bethuel the Syrian of Padan-aram, the sister to Laban the Syrian.
And Isaac entreated the LORD for his ife, because she \add as\add* barren: and the LORD as entreated of him, and Rebekah his ife conceived.
And the children struggled together ithin her: and she said, If \add it is\add* so, hy \add am\add* I thus? And she ent to inquire of the LORD.

And the LORD said to her, To nations \add are\add* in thy omb, and to manner of people shall be separated from thy boels: and \add the one\add* people shall be stronger than \add the other\add* people; and the elder shall serve the younger.
And hen her days to be delivered ere fulfilled, behold, \add there ere\add* tins in her omb.
And the first as born red, all over like a hairy garment: and they called his name Esau.
And after that his brother as born, and his hand took hold on Esau’s heel; and his name as called Jacob: and Isaac \add as\add* sixty years old hen she bore them.
And the boys gre: and Esau as a skillful hunter, a man of the field; and Jacob \add as\add* a plain man delling in tents.
And Isaac loved Esau, because he ate of \add his\add* venison: but Rebekah loved Jacob.
And Jacob boiled pottage: and Esau came from the field, and he \add as\add* faint.
And Esau said to Jacob, Feed me, I pray thee, ith that same red \add pottage\add*; for I \add am\add* faint: therefore as his name called Edom.
And Jacob said, Sell to me this day thy birth-right.
And Esau said, Behold, I \add am\add* at the point to die: and hat profit shall this birth-right bring to me?
And Jacob said, Sear to me this day; and he sore to him: and he sold his birth-right to Jacob.
Then Jacob gave Esau bread and pottage of lentiles; and he ate and drank, and rose and ent his ay: thus Esau despised \add his\add* birth-right.
And there as a famine in the land, besides the first famine that as in the days of Abraham. And Isaac ent to Abimelech king of the Philistines to Gerar.
And the LORD appeared to him, and said, Go not don into Egypt: dell in the land hich I shall tell thee of.
Sojourn in this land, and I ill be ith thee, and ill bless thee: for to thee, and to thy seed I ill give all these countries, and I ill perform the oath hich I sore to Abraham thy father;
And I ill make thy seed to multiply as the stars of heaven, and ill give to thy seed all these countries: and in thy seed shall all the nations of the earth be blessed:
Because that Abraham obeyed my voice, and kept my charge, my commandments, my statutes, and my las.
And Isaac delt in Gerar:

And the men of the place asked \add him\add* of his ife; and he said, She \add is\add* my sister: for he feared to say, \add She is\add* my ife; lest, \add said he\add*, the men of the place should kill me for Rebekah; because she \add as\add* fair to look upon.
And it came to pass hen he had been there a long time, that Abimelech king of the Philistines looked out at a indo, and sa, and behold, Isaac \add as\add* sporting ith Rebekah his ife.
And Abimelech called Isaac, and said, Behold, surely she \add is\add* thy ife: and ho saidst thou, She \add is\add* my sister? and Isaac said to him, Because I said, Lest I should die on her account.
And Abimelech said, What \add is\add* this thou hast done to us? one of the people might lightly have lain ith thy ife, and thou ouldst have brought guiltiness upon us.
And Abimelech charged all \add his\add* people, saying, He that toucheth this man or his ife shall surely be put to death.
Then Isaac soed in that land, and received in the same year a hundred-fold: and the LORD blessed him:
And the man became great, and ent forard, and gre until he became very great:
For he had possession of flocks, and possession of herds, and very many servants: And the Philistines envied him.
For all the ells hich his father’s servants had digged in the days of Abraham his father, the Philistines had stopped them, and filled them ith earth.
And Abimelech said to Isaac, Go from us: for thou art much mightier than e.
And Isaac departed thence, and pitched his tent in the valley of Gerar, and delt there.

And Isaac digged again the ells of ater hich they had digged in the days of Abraham his father; for the Philistines had stopped them after the death of Abraham: and he called their names after the names by hich his father had called them.
And Isaac’s servants digged in the valley, and found there a ell of springing ater.
And the herdmen of Gerar contended ith Isaac’s herdmen, saying, The ater \add is\add* ours: and he called the name of the ell Esek; because they strove ith him.
And they digged another ell, and contended for that also: and he called the name of it Sitnah.

And he removed from thence, and digged another ell; and for that they did not contend: and he called the name of it Rehoboth; and he said, For no the LORD hath made room for us, and e shall be fruitful in the land.
And he ent up from thence to Beer-sheba.

And the LORD appeared to him the same night, and said, I \add am\add* the God of Abraham thy father: fear not, for I \add am\add* ith thee, and ill bless thee, and multiply thy seed for my servant Abraham’s sake.
And he built an altar there, and called upon the name of the LORD, and pitched his tent there: and there Isaac’s servants digged a ell.
Then Abimelech ent to him from Gerar, and Ahuzzath one of his friends, and Phichol the chief captain of his army.
And Isaac said to them, Why come ye to me, seeing ye hate me, and have sent me aay from you?
And they said, We sa certainly that the LORD as ith thee: and e said, Let there be no an oath betixt us, \add even\add* betixt us and thee, and let us make a covenant ith thee;
That thou ilt do us no hurt, as e have not touched thee, and as e have done to thee nothing but good, and have sent thee aay in peace: thou \add art\add* no the blessed of the LORD.
And he made them a feast, and they ate and drank.
And they rose betimes in the morning, and sore one to another: and Isaac sent them aay, and they departed from him in peace.
And it came to pass the same day, that Isaac’s servants came and told him concerning the ell hich they had digged, and said to him, We have found ater.
And he called it Shebah: therefore the name of the city \add is\add* Beer-sheba to this day.
And Esau as forty years old hen he took for a ife Judith the daughter of Beeri the Hittite, and Bashemath the daughter of Elon the Hittite:
Who ere a grief of mind to Isaac and Rebekah.
And it came to pass, that hen Isaac as old, and his eyes ere dim, so that he could not see, he called Esau his eldest son, and said to him, My son: and he said to him, Behold, \add here am\add* I.
And he said, Behold no, I am old, I kno not the day of my death:
No therefore take, I pray thee, thy eapons, thy quiver and thy bo, and go out to the field, and take me \add some\add* venison;
And make me savory meat, such as I love, and bring \add it\add* to me, that I may eat; that my soul may bless thee before I die.
And Rebekah heard hen Isaac spoke to Esau his son; and Esau ent to the field to hunt \add for\add* venison, \add and\add* to bring it.
And Rebekah spoke to Jacob her son, saying, Behold, I heard thy father speak to Esau thy brother, saying,
Bring me venison, and make me savory meat, that I may eat, and bless thee before the LORD, before my death.
No therefore, my son, obey my voice, according to that hich I command thee.
Go no to the flock, and bring me from thence to good kids of the goats; and I ill make them savory meat for thy father, such as he loveth:
And thou shalt bring \add it\add* to thy father, that he may eat, and that he may bless thee before his death.
And Jacob said to Rebekah his mother, Behold, Esau my brother \add is\add* a hairy man, and I \add am\add* a smooth man:
My father perhaps ill feel me, and I shall seem to him as a deceiver; and I shall bring a curse upon me, and not a blessing.
And his mother said to him, upon me \add be\add* thy curse, my son; only obey my voice, and go, bring them to me.
And he ent, and took, and brought \add them\add* to his mother: and his mother made savory meat, such as his father loved.
And Rebekah took goodly raiment of her eldest son Esau, hich as ith her in the house, and put it upon Jacob her younger son:
And she put the skins of the kids of the goats on his hands, and on the smooth part of his neck:
And she gave the savory meat, and the bread hich she had prepared, into the hand of her son Jacob.
And he came to his father, and said, My father: And he said, Here \add am\add* I; ho \add art\add* thou, my son?
And Jacob said to his father, I \add am\add* Esau thy first-born; I have done according as thou badest me: arise, I pray thee, sit and eat of my venison, that thy soul may bless me.
And Isaac said to his son, Ho \add is it\add* that thou hast found \add it\add* so quickly, my son? And he said, Because the LORD thy God brought \add it\add* to me.
And Isaac said to Jacob, Come near, I pray thee, that I may feel thee, my son, hether thou \add art\add* my very son Esau, or not.
And Jacob ent near to Isaac his father; and he felt him, and said, The voice \add is\add* Jacob’s voice, but the hands \add are\add* the hands of Esau.
And he discerned him not, because his hands ere hairy, as his brother Esau’s hands: So he blessed him.
And he said, \add Art\add* thou my very son Esau? And he said, I \add am\add*.
And he said, bring \add it\add* near to me, and I ill eat of my son’s venison, that my soul may bless thee. And he brought \add it\add* near to him, and he ate: and he brought him ine, and he drank.
And his father Isaac said to him, Come near no, and kiss me, my son.
And he came near, and kissed him: and he smelled the smell of his raiment, and blessed him, and said, See, the smell of my son \add is\add* as the smell of a field hich the LORD hath blessed:
Therefore God give thee of the de of heaven, and the fatness of the earth, and plenty of corn and ine:

Let people serve thee, and nations bo don to thee; be lord over thy brethren, and let thy mother’s sons bo don to thee: cursed \add be\add* every one that curseth thee, and blessed \add be\add* he that blesseth thee.
And it came to pass, as soon as Isaac had made an end of blessing Jacob, and Jacob had yet scarcely gone out from the presence of Isaac his father, that Esau his brother came in from his hunting.
And he also had made savory meat, and brought it to his father; and said to his father, Let my father arise, and eat of his son’s venison, that thy soul may bless me.
And Isaac his father said to him, Who \add art\add* thou? And he said, I \add am\add* thy son, thy first-born Esau.

And Isaac trembled exceedingly, and said, Who? here \add is\add* he that hath taken venison, and brought \add it\add* me, and I have eaten of all before thou camest, and have blessed him? yea, \add and\add* he shall be blessed.
And hen Esau heard the ords of his father, he cried ith a great and exceedingly bitter cry, and said to his father, Bless me, \add even\add* me also, O my father.

And he said, Is he not rightly named Jacob? for he hath supplanted me tice: he took aay my birth-right; and behold, no he hath taken aay my blessing. And he said, Hast thou not reserved a blessing for me?

And Isaac ansered and said to Esau, Behold, I have made him thy lord, and all his brethren have I given to him for servants; and ith corn and ine have I sustained him: and hat shall I do no to thee, my son?
And Esau said to his father, Hast thou but one blessing, my father? bless me, \add even\add* me also, O my father. And Esau lifted up his voice, and ept.
And Isaac his father ansered, and said to him, Behold, thy delling shall be the fatness of the earth, and of the de of heaven from above;
And by thy sord shalt thou live, and shalt serve thy brother: and it shall come to pass hen thou shalt have the dominion, that thou shalt break his yoke from off thy neck.
And Esau hated Jacob, because of the blessing ith hich his father blessed him: and Esau said in his heart, The days of mourning for my father are at hand; then ill I slay my brother Jacob.

And these ords of Esau her elder son ere told to Rebekah: and she sent and called Jacob her younger son, and said to him, Behold, thy brother Esau, as concerning thee, doth comfort himself, \add purposing\add* to kill thee.
No therefore, my son, obey my voice: and arise, flee thou to Laban my brother to Haran;
And tarry ith him a fe days, until thy brother’s fury shall turn aay;

Till thy brother’s anger shall turn aay from thee, and he shall forget \add that\add* hich thou hast done to him: then I ill send, and bring thee from thence. Why should I be deprived also of you both in one day?

And Rebekah said to Isaac, I am eary of my life, because of the daughters of Heth: if Jacob shall take a ife of the daughters of Heth, such as these \add ho are\add* of the daughters of the land, hat good ill my life do me?
And Isaac called Jacob, and blessed him, and charged him, and said to him, Thou shalt not take a ife of the daughters of Canaan.
Arise, go to Padan-aram, to the house of Bethuel thy mother’s father; and take thee a ife from thence of the daughters of Laban thy mother’s brother.
And God Almighty bless thee, and make thee fruitful, and multiply thee, that thou mayest be a multitude of people;
And give thee the blessing of Abraham, to thee, and to thy seed ith thee; that thou mayest inherit the land in hich thou art a stranger, hich God gave to Abraham.
And Isaac sent aay Jacob: and he ent to Padan-aram, to Laban, son of Bethuel the Syrian, the brother of Rebekah, Jacob’s and Esau’s mother.

When Esau sa that Isaac had blessed Jacob, and sent him aay to Padan-aram, to take him a ife from thence; and that as he blessed him, he gave him a charge, saying, Thou shalt not take a ife of the daughters of Canaan;
And that Jacob obeyed his father, and his mother, and as gone to Padan-aram;
And Esau seeing that the daughters of Canaan pleased not Isaac his father;
Then ent Esau to Ishmael, and took to the ives hich he had, Mahalath the daughter of Ishmael Abraham’s son, the sister of Nebajoth, to be his ife.
And Jacob ent out from Beer-sheba, and ent toards Haran.

And he lighted upon a certain place, and tarried there all night, because the sun as set: and he took of the stones of that place, and put \add them for\add* his pillos, and lay don in that place to sleep.
And he dreamed, and behold, a ladder set upon the earth, and the top of it reached to heaven: and behold, the angels of God ascending and descending on it.
And behold, the LORD stood above it, and said, I \add am\add* the LORD God of Abraham thy father, and the God of Isaac: the land on hich thou liest, to thee ill I give it, and to thy seed.

And thy seed shall be as the dust of the earth; and thou shalt spread abroad to the est, and to the east, and to the north, and to the south: and in thee and in thy seed shall all the families of the earth be blessed.

And behold, I \add am\add* ith thee, and ill keep thee in all \add places\add* hither thou goest, and ill bring thee again into this land: for I ill not leave thee, until I have done \add that\add* hich I have declared to thee.
And Jacob aaked out of his sleep, and he said, Surely the LORD is in this place; and I kne \add it\add* not.
And he as afraid, and said, Ho dreadful \add is\add* this place! this \add is\add* no other but the house of God, and this \add is\add* the gate of heaven.
And Jacob rose early in the morning, and took the stone that he had put \add for\add* his pillos, and set it up \add for\add* a pillar, and poured oil on the top of it.
And he called the name of that place Beth-el: but the name of that city \add as called\add* Luz at the first.
And Jacob voed a vo, saying, If God ill be ith me, and ill keep me in this ay that I go, and ill give me bread to eat, and raiment to put on,
So that I come again to my father’s house in peace; then shall the LORD be my God:
And this stone, hich I have set \add for\add* a pillar, shall be God’s house: and of all that thou shalt give me, I ill surely give the tenth to thee.
Then Jacob ent on his journey, and came into the land of the people of the east.

And he looked, and behold, a ell in the field, and lo, there \add ere\add* three flocks of sheep lying by it; for out of that ell they atered the flocks: and a great stone \add as\add* upon the ell’s mouth.
And thither ere all the flocks gathered: and they rolled the stone from the ell’s mouth and atered the sheep, and put the stone again upon the ell’s mouth in its place.
And Jacob said to them, My brethren, hence \add are\add* ye? And they said, We \add are\add* from Haran.
And he said to them, Kno ye Laban the son of Nahor? and they said, We kno \add him\add*.
And he said to them, \add Is\add* he ell? And they said, \add He is\add* ell: and behold, Rachel his daughter cometh ith the sheep.
And he said, Lo, \add it is\add* yet high day, neither \add is it\add* time that the cattle should be collected: ater ye the sheep, and go \add and\add* feed \add them\add*.
And they said, We cannot, until all the flocks are collected, and \add till\add* they roll the stone from the ell’s mouth; then e ater the sheep.
And hile he as yet speaking ith them, Rachel came ith her father’s sheep: for she kept them.

And it came to pass, hen Jacob sa Rachel, the daughter of Laban his mother’s brother, and the sheep of Laban his mother’s brother; that Jacob ent near, and rolled the stone from the ell’s mouth, and atered the flock of Laban his mother’s brother.
And Jacob kissed Rachel, and lifted up his voice, and ept.
And Jacob told Rachel that he \add as\add* her father’s brother, and that he \add as\add* Rebekah’s son; and she ran and told her father.
And it came to pass hen Laban heard the tidings of Jacob his sister’s son, that he ran to meet him, and embraced him, and kissed him, and brought him to his house. And he told Laban all these things.
And Laban said to him, Surely thou \add art\add* my bone and my flesh: and he abode ith him the space of a month.
And Laban said to Jacob, Because thou \add art\add* my brother, shouldest thou therefore serve me for naught? tell me, hat \add shall\add* thy ages \add be\add*?
And Laban had to daughters: the name of the elder \add as\add* Leah, and the name of the younger \add as\add* Rachel.
Leah \add as\add* tender-eyed, but Rachel as beautiful and ell-favored.
And Jacob loved Rachel; and said, I ill serve thee seven years for Rachel thy younger daughter.
And Laban said, \add It is\add* better that I give her to thee, than that I should give her to another man: abide ith me.
And Jacob served seven years for Rachel; and they seemed to him \add but\add* a fe days, for the love he had to her.
And Jacob said to Laban, Give \add me\add* my ife (for my days are fulfilled) that I may go in to her.
And Laban assembled all the men of the place, and made a feast.
And it came to pass in the evening, that he took Leah his daughter, and brought her to him; and he ent in to her.
And Laban gave to his daughter Leah, Zilpah his maid \add for\add* a handmaid.

And it came to pass, that in the morning, behold, it \add as\add* Leah: and he said to Laban, What \add is\add* this thou hast done to me? did I not serve ith thee for Rachel? hy then hast thou deceived me?
