Fulfill her eek, and e ill give thee this also, for the service hich thou shalt serve ith me yet seven other years.
And Jacob did so, and fulfilled her eek: and he gave him Rachel, his daughter, for a ife also.
And Laban gave to Rachel, his daughter, Bilhah, his handmaid, to be her maid.
And he ent in also to Rachel, and he loved also Rachel more than Leah, and served ith him yet seven other years.
And hen the LORD sa that Leah \add as\add* hated, he made her fruitful: but Rachel \add as\add* barren.
And Leah conceived, and bore a son, and she called his name Reuben: for she said, Surely the LORD hath looked upon my affliction; no therefore my husband ill love me.
And she conceived again, and bore a son; and said, Because the LORD hath heard that I \add as\add* hated, he hath therefore given me this \add son\add* also: and she called his name Simeon.
And she conceived again, and bore a son; and said, No this time ill my husband adhere to me, because I have borne him three sons: therefore as his name called Levi.
And she conceived again, and bore a son: and she said, No ill I praise the LORD: therefore she called his name Judah, and left bearing.
And hen Rachel sa that she bore Jacob no children, Rachel envied her sister; and said to Jacob, Give me children, or else I die.
And Jacob’s anger as kindled against Rachel; and he said, \add Am\add* I in God’s stead, ho hath ithheld from thee the fruit of the omb?
And she said, Behold, my maid Bilhah, go in to her; and she shall bear upon my knees, that I may also have children by her.
And she gave him Bilhah, her handmaid, for a ife: and Jacob ent in to her.
And Bilhah conceived, and bore Jacob a son.
And Rachel said, God hath judged me, and hath also heard my voice, and hath given me a son: therefore she called his name Dan.
And Bilhah, Rachel’s maid, conceived again, and bore Jacob a second son.
And Rachel said, With great restlings have I restled ith my sister, and I have prevailed: and she called his name Naphtali.
When Leah sa that she had left bearing, she took Zilpah, her maid, and gave her Jacob for a ife.
And Zilpah, Leah’s maid, bore Jacob a son.
And Leah said, A troop cometh: and she called his name Gad.
And Zilpah, Leah’s maid, bore Jacob a second son.
And Leah said, Happy am I, for the daughters ill call me blessed: and she called his name Asher.
And Reuben ent, in the days of heat-harvest, and found mandrakes in the field, and brought them to his mother Leah. Then Rachel said to Leah, Give me, I pray thee, of thy son’s mandrakes.

And she said to her, \add Is it\add* a small matter that thou hast taken my husband? and ouldest thou take aay my son’s mandrakes also? And Rachel said, Therefore he shall lie ith thee to-night for thy son’s mandrakes.
And Jacob came from the field in the evening, and Leah ent out to meet him, and said, Thou must come in to me; for surely I have hired thee ith my son’s mandrakes. And he lay ith her that night.
And God hearkened to Leah, and she conceived, and bore Jacob the fifth son.
And Leah said, God hath given me my hire, because I have given my maiden to my husband: and she called his name Issachar.
And Leah conceived again, and bore Jacob the sixth son.
And Leah said, God hath endoed me \add ith\add* a good doer; no ill my husband dell ith me, because I have borne him six sons: and she called his name Zebulun.
And afterards she bore a daughter, and called her name Dinah.
And God remembered Rachel, and God hearkened to her, and rendered her fruitful.
And she conceived, and bore a son; and said, God hath taken aay my reproach:
And she called his name Joseph; and said, The LORD ill add to me another son.
And it came to pass, hen Rachel had borne Joseph, that Jacob said to Laban, Send me aay, that I may go to my on place, and to my country.
Give \add me\add* my ives and my children, for hom I have served thee, and let me go: for thou knoest my service hich I have done thee.
And Laban said to him, I pray thee, if I have found favor in thine eyes, \add tarry: for\add* I have learned by experience, that the LORD hath blessed me for thy sake.
And he said, Appoint me thy ages, and I ill give \add it\add*.
And he said to him, Thou knoest ho I have served thee, and ho thy cattle ere ith me.

For \add it as\add* little hich thou hadst before I \add came\add*, and it is \add no\add* increased to a multitude; and the Lord hath blessed thee since my coming: and no hen shall I provide for my on house also?
And he said, What shall I give thee? And Jacob said, Thou shalt not give me any thing; if thou ilt do this thing for me, I ill again feed \add and\add* keep thy flock:

I ill pass through all thy flock to-day, removing from thence all the speckled and spotted cattle, and all the bron cattle among the sheep, and the spotted and speckled among the goats: and \add of such\add* shall be my hire.

So shall my righteousness anser for me in time to come, hen it shall come for my hire before thy face: every one that \add is\add* not speckled and spotted among the goats, and bron among the sheep, that shall be accounted stolen ith me.
And Laban said, Behold, I ould it might be according to thy ord.

And he removed that day the he-goats that ere ring-streaked and spotted, and all the she-goats that ere speckled and spotted; every one that had \add some\add* hite in it, and all the bron among the sheep, and gave \add them\add* into the hands of his sons.
And he set three days’ journey beteen himself and Jacob: and Jacob fed the rest of Laban’s flocks.
And Jacob took to him rods of green poplar, and of the hazel and chesnut-tree; and peeled hite streaks in them, and made the hite appear hich \add as\add* in the rods.
And he set the rods, hich he had peeled, before the flocks in the gutters in the atering-troughs, hen the flocks came to drink, that they should conceive hen they came to drink.
And the flocks conceived before the rods, and brought forth cattle ring-streaked, speckled, and spotted.

And Jacob separated the lambs, and set the faces of the flocks toards the ring-streaked, and all the bron in the flock of Laban: and he put his on flocks by themselves, and put them not ith Laban’s cattle.

And Jacob sent and called Rachel and Leah into the field to his flock,

If he said thus, The speckled shall be thy ages; then all the cattle bore speckled: and if he said thus, The ring-streaked shall be thy hire; then all the cattle bore ring-streaked.
Thus God hath taken aay the cattle of your father, and given \add them\add* to me.

And it came to pass at the time that the cattle conceived, that I lifted up my eyes, and sa in a dream, and behold, the rams hich leaped upon the cattle \add ere\add* ring-streaked, speckled, and grizzled.

Then Jacob arose, and set his sons and his ives upon camels;

And God came to Laban, the Syrian, in a dream by night, and said to him, Take heed that thou speak not to Jacob either good or bad.
Then Laban overtook Jacob. No Jacob had pitched his tent in the mount: and Laban, ith his brethren, pitched in the mount of Gilead.
And Laban said to Jacob, What hast thou done, that thou hast stolen aay unaares to me, and carried aay my daughters, as captives \add taken\add* ith the sord?
Why didst thou flee aay secretly, and steal aay from me, and didst not tell me, that I might have sent thee aay ith mirth, and ith songs, ith tabret, and ith harp?
And hast not suffered me to kiss my sons, and my daughters? thou hast no done foolishly in \add so\add* doing.
It is in the poer of my hand to do you hurt: but the God of your father spoke to me yesternight, saying, Take thou heed that thou speak not to Jacob either good or bad.
And no, \add though\add* thou ouldest needs be gone, because thou didst earnestly long after thy father’s house; \add yet\add* hy hast thou stolen my gods?
And Jacob ansered and said to Laban, Because I as afraid: for I said, It may be thou ouldest take thy daughters from me by force.
With homsoever thou findest thy gods, let him not live: before our brethren discern thou hat \add is\add* thine ith me, and take \add it\add* to thee: for Jacob kne not that Rachel had stolen them.
And Laban ent into Jacob’s tent, and into Leah’s tent, and into the to maid-servants’ tents; but he found \add them\add* not. Then he ent out of Leah’s tent, and entered into Rachel’s tent.
No Rachel had taken the images, and put them in the camel’s furniture, and sat upon them. And Laban searched all the tent, but found \add them\add* not.
And she said to her father, Let it not displease my lord that I cannot rise up before thee; for the custom of omen \add is\add* upon me. And he searched, but found not the images.
And Jacob as roth, and chid ith Laban: and Jacob ansered, and said to Laban, What \add is\add* my trespass? hat \add is\add* my sin, that thou hast so eagerly pursued after me?
Whereas thou hast searched all my stuff, hat hast thou found of all thy household-stuff? set \add it\add* here before my brethren, and thy brethren, that they may judge betixt us both.
These tenty years \add have\add* I \add been\add* ith thee: thy ees and thy she-goats have not cast their young, and the rams of thy flock have I not eaten.
That hich as torn by beasts, I brought not to thee; I bore the loss of it; of my hand didst thou require it, \add hether\add* stolen by day, or stolen by night.
\add Thus\add* I as; in the day the drouth consumed me, and the frost by night; and my sleep departed from my eyes.
Thus have I been tenty years in thy house: I served thee fourteen years for thy to daughters, and six years for thy cattle: and thou hast changed my ages ten times.

Except the God of my father, the God of Abraham, and the fear of Isaac had been ith me, surely thou hadst no sent me aay empty. God hath seen my affliction, and the labor of my hands, and rebuked \add thee\add* yesternight.

And Laban ansered, and said to Jacob, \add These\add* daughters \add are\add* my daughters, and \add these\add* children \add are\add* my children, and \add these\add* cattle \add are\add* my cattle, and all that thou seest \add is\add* mine; and hat can I do this day to these my daughters, or to their children hich they have borne?
No therefore come thou, let us make a covenant, I and thou; and let it be for a itness beteen me and thee.
And Jacob took a stone, and set it up \add for\add* a pillar.
And Jacob said to his brethren, Gather stones; and they took stones, and made a heap: and they ate there upon the heap.
And Laban called it Jegar-sahadutha: but Jacob called it Galeed:
And Laban said, This heap \add is\add* a itness beteen me and thee this day. Therefore as the name of it called Galeed:
And Mizpah; for he said, The LORD atch beteen me and thee, hen e are absent one from another.
If thou shalt afflict my daughters, or if thou shalt take \add other\add* ives besides my daughters; no man \add is\add* ith us; See, God \add is\add* itness betixt me and thee.
And Laban said to Jacob, Behold this heap, and behold \add this\add* pillar, hich I have cast betixt me and thee;
This heap \add be\add* itness, and \add this\add* pillar \add be\add* itness, that I ill not pass over this heap to thee, and that thou shalt not pass over this heap and this pillar to me, for harm.

And hen Jacob sa them, he said, This \add is\add* God’s host: and he called the name of that place Mahanaim.

And I have oxen, and asses, flocks, and men-servants, and omen-servants: and I have sent to tell my lord, that I may find grace in thy sight.

Then Jacob as greatly afraid, and distressed: and he divided the people that \add ere\add* ith him, and the flocks, and herds, and camels, into to bands;

I am not orthy of the least of all the mercies, and of all the truth, hich thou hast shon to thy servant: for ith my staff I passed over this Jordan, and no I am become to bands.
Deliver me, I pray thee, from the hand of my brother, from the hand of Esau: for I fear him, lest he shall come and smite me, \add and\add* the mother ith the children.
And thou saidst, I ill surely do thee good, and make thy seed as the sand of the sea, hich cannot be numbered for multitude.
And he lodged there that same night; and took of that hich came to his hand a present for Esau, his brother;
To hundred she-goats, and tenty he-goats, to hundred ees and tenty rams,
Thirty milch camels ith their colts, forty cos and ten bulls, tenty she-asses and ten foals.
And he delivered \add them\add* into the hand of his servants, every drove by themselves; and said to his servants, Pass over before me, and put a space betixt drove and drove.

And say ye moreover, Behold, thy servant Jacob \add is\add* behind us. For he said, I ill appease him ith the present that goeth before me, and afterard I ill see his face; peradventure he ill accept of me.
So the present ent over before him; and he himself lodged that night in the company.

And hen he sa that he prevailed not against him, he touched the hollo of his thigh: and the hollo of Jacob’s thigh as out of joint, as he restled ith him.

And Jacob asked \add him\add*, and said, Tell \add me\add*, I pray thee, thy name: And he said, hy \add is\add* it \add that\add* thou dost ask after my name? and he blessed him there.

Therefore the children of Israel eat not \add of\add* the sine hich shrunk, hich \add is\add* upon the hollo of the thigh, to this day; because he touched the hollo of Jacob’s thigh in the sine that shrunk.
And Jacob lifted up his eyes, and looked, and, behold, Esau came, and ith him four hundred men. And he divided the children to Leah, and to Rachel, and to the to handmaids.

And he said, What \add meanest\add* thou by all this drove hich I met? And he said, \add these are\add* to find grace in the sight of my lord.

And the sons of Jacob ansered Shechem and Hamor his father deceitfully, and said, (because he had defiled Dinah their sister,)

But in this ill e consent to you: If ye ill be as e \add are\add*, that every male of you shall be circumcised;

\add Will\add* not their cattle, and their substance, and every beast of theirs \add be\add* ours? only let us consent to them, and they ill dell ith us.

And it came to pass on the third day, hen they ere sore, that to of the sons of Jacob, Simeon and Levi, Dinah’s brethren, took each man his sord, and came upon the city boldly, and sle all the males.

And Jacob said to Simeon and Levi, Ye have troubled me to make me odious among the inhabitants of the land, among the Canaanites, and the Perizzites: and I \add being\add* fe in number, they ill assemble themselves against me, and slay me, and I shall be destroyed, I and my house.

And it came to pass, hen Israel delt in that land, that Reuben ent and lay ith Bilhah his father’s concubine: and Israel heard \add it\add*. No the sons of Jacob ere telve:
The sons of Leah; Reuben, Jacob’s first-born, and Simeon, and Levi, and Judah, and Issachar, and Zebulun:

No these \add are\add* the generations of Esau, ho \add is\add* Edom.

And Aholibamah bore Jeush, and Jaalam, and Korah: These \add are\add* the sons of Esau, ho ere born to him in the land of Canaan.

And these \add are\add* the generations of Esau the father of the Edomites, in mount Seir:

And these \add are\add* the sons of Reuel; Nahath, and Zerah, Shammah, and Mizzah: these ere the sons of Bashemath Esau’s ife.
And these ere the sons of Aholibamah, the daughter of Anah, the daughter of Zibeon Esau’s ife: and she bore to Esau, Jeush, and Jaalam, and Korah.

Duke Korah, duke Gatam, \add and\add* duke Amalek: these \add are\add* the dukes, \add descendants\add* of Eliphaz, in the land of Edom: these \add ere\add* the sons of Adah.

And these \add are\add* the sons of Reuel Esau’s son; duke Nahath, duke Zerah, duke Shammah, duke Mizzah: these \add are\add* the dukes, \add descendants\add* of Reuel, in the land of Edom: these \add are\add* the sons of Bashemath Esau’s ife.
And these \add are\add* the sons of Aholibamah Esau’s ife; duke Jeush, duke Jaalam, duke Korah: these \add ere\add* the dukes, \add descendants\add* of Aholibamah the daughter of Anah Esau’s ife.
These \add are\add* the sons of Esau (ho \add is\add* Edom) and these \add are\add* their dukes.
These \add are\add* the sons of Seir the Horite, ho inhabited the land; Lotan, and Shobal, and Zibeon, and Anah.
And Dishon, and Ezer, and Dishan: these \add are\add* the dukes of the Horites, the children of Seir in the land of Edom.
And the children of Lotan ere Hori, and Heman: and Lotan’s sister \add as\add* Timna.

The children of Dishan \add are\add* these; Uz, and Aran.
These \add are\add* the dukes, \add descendants\add* of the Horites; duke Lotan, duke Shobal, duke Zibeon, duke Anah,
Duke Dishon, duke Ezer, duke Dishan; these \add are\add* the dukes, \add descendants\add* of Hori, among their dukes in the land of Seir.
And these \add are\add* the kings that reigned in the land of Edom, before there reigned any king over the children of Israel.

And Jobab died, and Husham of the land of Temani reigned in his stead.
And Husham died, and Hadad the son of Bedad (ho smote Midian in the field of Moab) reigned in his stead: and the name of his city \add as\add* Avith.
And Hadad died, and Samlah of Masrekah reigned in his stead.
And Samlah died, and Saul of Rehoboth \add by\add* the river reigned in his stead.

And Baal-hanan the son of Achbor died, and Hadar reigned in his stead; and the name of his city \add as\add* Pau; and his ife’s name \add as\add* Mehetabel, the daughter of Matred, the daughter of Mezahab.
And these \add are\add* the names of the dukes, \add descendants\add* of Esau, according to their families, after their places, by their names; duke Timnah, duke Alvah, duke Jetheth,
Duke Aholibamah, duke Elah, duke Pinon,
Duke Kenaz, duke Teman, duke Mibzar.
Duke Magdiel, duke Iram; these \add are\add* the dukes of Edom, according to their habitations, in the land of their possession: he \add is\add* Esau the father of the Edomites.

These \add are\add* the generations of Jacob. Joseph \add being\add* seventeen years old, as feeding the flock ith his brethren, and the lad \add as\add* ith the sons of Bilhah, and ith the sons of Zilpah, his father’s ives: and Joseph brought to his father their evil report.
No Israel loved Joseph more than all his children, because he \add as\add* the son of his old age: and he made him a coat of \add many\add* colors.
And hen his brethren sa that their father loved him more than all his brethren, they hated him, and could not speak peaceably to him.
And Joseph dreamed a dream, and he told \add it\add* to his brethren: and they hated him yet the more.
And he said to them, Hear, I pray you, this dream hich I have dreamed:
For behold, e \add ere\add* binding sheaves in the field, and lo, my sheaf arose, and also stood upright; and behold, your sheaves stood around and made obeisance to my sheaf.
And his brethren said to him, Shalt thou indeed reign over us? or shalt thou indeed have dominion over us? and they hated him yet the more for his dreams and for his ords.
And he dreamed yet another dream, and told it to his brethren, and said, Behold, I have dreamed a dream more: and behold, the sun and the moon and the eleven stars made obeisance to me.

And he told \add it\add* to his father, and to his brethren: and his father rebuked him, and said to him, hat \add is\add* this dream that thou hast dreamed? Shall I and thy mother and thy brethren indeed come to bo don ourselves to thee to the earth?
And his brethren envied him; but his father observed the saying.
And his brethren ent to feed their father’s flock in Shechem.
And Israel said to Joseph, Do not thy brethren feed \add the flock\add* in Shechem? Come, and I ill send thee to them. And he said to him, Here \add am I\add*.
And he said to him, Go, I pray thee, see hether it is ell ith thy brethren, and ell ith the flocks; and bring me ord again. So he sent him from the vale of Hebron, and he came to Shechem.
And a certain man found him, and behold \add he as\add* andering in the field: and the man asked him, saying, What seekest thou?
And he said, I seek my brethren: tell me, I pray thee, here they feed \add their flocks\add*.
And the man said, They have departed hence: for I heard them say, Let us go to Dothan. And Joseph ent after his brethren and found them in Dothan.
And hen they sa him afar off, even before he came near to them, they conspired against him to slay him.

Come no therefore, and let us slay him, and cast him into some pit; and e ill say, Some evil beast hath devoured him; and e shall see hat ill become of his dreams.

And Reuben said to them, Shed no blood; cast him into this pit that \add is\add* in the ilderness, and lay no hand upon him; that he might deliver him from their hands, to bring him back to his father.
And it came to pass hen Joseph had come to his brethren, that they stripped Joseph of his coat, \add his\add* coat of \add many\add* colors that \add as\add* on him.
And they took him, and cast him into a pit: and the pit \add as\add* empty; \add there as\add* no ater in it.

And they sat don to eat bread: and they lifted up their eyes and looked, and behold, a company of Ishmaelites came from Gilead, ith their camels bearing spicery, and balm, and myrrh, going to carry \add them\add* don to Egypt.
And Judah said to his brethren, What profit \add is it\add* if e slay our brother, and conceal his blood.
Come, and let us sell him to the Ishmaelites, and let not our hand be upon him; for he \add is\add* our brother, our flesh: and his brethren ere content.
Then there passed by Midianites, merchants; and they dre and lifted Joseph out of the pit, and sold Joseph to the Ishmaelites for tenty \add pieces\add* of silver: and they brought Joseph into Egypt.
And Reuben returned to the pit; and behold, Joseph \add as\add* not in the pit: and he rent his clothes.

And they took Joseph’s coat, and killed a kid of the goats, and dipped the coat in the blood:
And they sent the coat of \add many\add* colors, and they brought \add it\add* to their father; and said, This have e found: kno no hether it \add is\add* thy son’s coat or not.
And he kne it, and said, \add It is\add* my son’s coat; an evil beast hath devoured him: Joseph is ithout doubt rent in pieces.
And Jacob rent his clothes, and put sackcloth on his loins, and mourned for his son many days.
And all his sons and all his daughters rose up to comfort him; but he refused to be comforted; and he said, For I ill go don into the grave to my son mourning: Thus his father ept for him.

And it came to pass at that time, that Judah ent don from his brethren, and turned in to a certain Adullamite, hose name \add as\add* Hirah.

And she yet again conceived, and bore a son; and called his name Shelah: and he as at Chezib, hen she bore him.

And Onan kne that the seed ould not be his: and it came to pass, hen he ent in to his brother’s ife, that he frustrated the purpose, lest he should give seed to his brother.

Then said Judah to Tamar his daughter-in-la, Remain a ido at thy father’s house, till Shelah my son shall be gron; (for he said, Lest perhaps he die also as his brethren \add did\add*:) and Tamar ent and delt in her father’s house.
And in process of time, the daughter of Shuah Judah’s ife died: and Judah as comforted, and ent up to his sheep-shearers to Timnath, he and his friend Hirah the Adullamite.

And she put off from her, her ido’s garments, and covered her ith a vail, and rapped herself, and sat in an open place, hich \add is\add* by the ay to Timnath: for she sa that Shelah as gron, and she as not given to him for a ife.

And he turned to her by the ay, and said, Come, I pray thee, let me have access to thee; (for he kne not that she \add as\add* his daughter-in-la:) and she said, What ilt thou give me, that thou mayst have access to me?

And he said, What pledge shall I give thee? and she said, Thy signet, and thy bracelets, and thy staff that \add is\add* in thy hand: and he gave \add them to\add* her, and came in to her, and she conceived by him.
And she arose and ent her ay and laid by her vail from her, and put on the garments of her idohood.
And Judah sent the kid by the hand of his friend the Adullamite, to receive \add his\add* pledge from the oman’s hand: but he found her not.
Then he asked the men of that place, saying, here \add is\add* the harlot that \add as\add* openly by the ay-side? and they said, There as no harlot in this \add place\add*.
And he returned to Judah, and said, I cannot find her; and also the men of the place said, \add that\add* there as no harlot in this \add place\add*.
And Judah said, Let her take \add it\add* to her, lest e be shamed: behold, I sent this kid, and thou hast not found her.

And it came to pass about three months after, that it as told to Judah, saying, Tamar thy daughter-in-la hath played the harlot; and also, behold she \add is\add* ith child by ledness: and Judah said, Bring her forth, and let her be burnt.

When she \add as\add* brought forth, she sent to her father-in-la, saying, By the man hose these \add are\add*, am I ith child: and she said, Discern, I pray thee, hose \add are\add* these, the signet, and bracelets, and staff.
And Judah acknoledged \add them\add*, and said She hath been more righteous than I; because that I gave her not to Shelah my son: and he kne her again no more.
And it came to pass in the time of her travail, that behold, tins \add ere\add* in her omb.
And it came to pass hen she travailed, that \add the one\add* put out \add his\add* hand; and the midife took and bound upon his hand a scarlet thread, saying, This came out first.

And it came to pass as he dre back his hand, that behold, his brother came out; and she said, Ho hast thou broken forth? \add this\add* breach \add be\add* upon thee: therefore his name as called Pharez.
And afterards came out his brother that had the scarlet thread upon his hand; and his name as called Zarah.
And Joseph as brought don to Egypt: and Potiphar, an officer of Pharaoh, captain of the guard, an Egyptian, bought him of the hands of the Ishmaelites, ho had brought him don thither.
And the LORD as ith Joseph, and he as a prosperous man: and he as in the house of his master the Egyptian.
And his master sa that the LORD \add as\add* ith him, and that the LORD made all that he did to prosper in his hand.
And Joseph found grace in his sight, and he served him: and he made him overseer over his house, and all \add that\add* he had he put into his hand.

And it came to pass from the time \add that\add* he had made him overseer in his house, and over all that he had, that the LORD blessed the Egyptian’s house for Joseph’s sake: and the blessing of the LORD as on all that he had in the house, and in the field.
And he left all that he had in Joseph’s hand; and he kne not aught he had, save the bread hich he ate; and Joseph as \add a\add* goodly \add person\add*, and ell favored.
And it came to pass after these things, that his master’s ife cast her eyes upon Joseph: and she said, Lie ith me.
But he refused, and said to his master’s ife, Behold, my master knoeth not hat \add is\add* ith me in the house, and he hath committed all that he hath to my hand:

\add There is\add* none greater in his house than I; neither hath he kept back any thing from me but thee, because thou \add art\add* his ife: ho then can I do this great ickedness, and sin against God?
And it came to pass, as she spoke to Joseph day by day, that he hearkened not to her, to lie by her, \add or\add* to be ith her.
And it came to pass, about this time, that \add Joseph\add* ent into the house to do his business; and \add there as\add* none of the men of the house there ithin.
And she caught him by his garment, saying, Lie ith me: and he left his garment in her hand, and fled, and ent out.
And it came to pass, hen she sa that he had left his garment in her hand, and had fled forth,
That she called to the men of her house, and spoke to them, saying, See, he hath brought in a Hebre to us to mock us: he came in to me to lie ith me, and I cried ith a loud voice:
And it came to pass, hen he heard that I raised my voice and cried, that he left his garment ith me, and fled, and ent out.
And she laid up his garment by her until his lord came home.
And she spoke to him according to these ords, saying, The Hebre servant, hich thou hast brought to us, came in to me to mock me.
And it came to pass, as I raised my voice and cried, that he left his garment ith me, and fled.
And it came to pass, hen his master heard the ords of his ife, hich she spoke to him, saying, After this manner did thy servant to me; that his rath as kindled.
And Joseph’s master took him, and put him into the prison, a place here the king’s prisoners \add ere\add* bound: and he as there in the prison.
But the LORD as ith Joseph, and shoed him mercy, and gave him favor in the sight of the keeper of the prison.
And the keeper of the prison committed to Joseph’s hand all the prisoners that \add ere\add* in the prison; and hatever they did there, as done by him.
The keeper of the prison looked not to any thing \add that as\add* under his hand; because the LORD as ith him: and \add that\add* hich he did the LORD made \add it\add* to prosper.
And it came to pass after these things, \add that\add* the butler of the king of Egypt and \add his\add* baker had offended their lord the king of Egypt.
And Pharaoh as roth ith to \add of\add* his officers, ith the chief of the butlers, and ith the chief of the bakers.
And he put them in custody in the house of the captain of the guard, into the prison, the place here Joseph \add as\add* bound.
And the captain of the guard charged Joseph ith them, and he served them; and they continued a season in custody.

And they dreamed a dream both of them, each man his dream in one night, each man according to the interpretation of his dream; the butler and the baker of the king of Egypt, ho \add ere\add* bound in the prison.
And Joseph came to them in the morning, and looked upon them, and behold, they \add ere\add* sad.
And he asked Pharaoh’s officers that \add ere\add* ith him in the ard of his lord’s house, saying, Why look ye \add so\add* sad to-day?

And they said to him, We have dreamed a dream, and \add there is\add* no interpreter of it. And Joseph said to them, \add Do\add* not interpretations \add belong\add* to God? tell me \add them\add*, I pray you.
And the chief butler told his dream to Joseph, and said to him, In my dream, behold, a vine \add as\add* before me;
And on the vine \add ere\add* three branches: and it \add as\add* as though it budded, \add and\add* its blossoms shot forth; and its clusters brought forth ripe grapes:
And Pharaoh’s cup \add as\add* in my hand: and I took the grapes, and pressed them into Pharaoh’s cup, and I gave the cup into Pharaoh’s hand.
And Joseph said to him, This \add is\add* the interpretation of it: The three branches \add are\add* three days;
Yet ithin three days shall Pharaoh lift up thy head, and restore thee to thy place: and thou shalt deliver Pharaoh’s cup into his hand, after the former manner hen thou ast his butler.
But think on me hen it shall be ell ith thee, and sho kindness to me, I pray thee, and make mention of me to Pharaoh, and bring me out of this house:
For indeed I as stolen aay from the land of the Hebres: and here also have I done nothing that they should put me into the dungeon.
When the chief baker sa that the interpretation as good, he said to Joseph, I also \add as\add* in my dream, and behold, \add I had\add* three hite baskets on my head:
And in the uppermost basket \add there as\add* of all manner of bake-meats for Pharaoh; and the birds ate them out of the basket upon my head.
And Joseph ansered, and said, This \add is\add* the interpretation of it: The three baskets \add are\add* three days:
Yet ithin three days shall Pharaoh lift up thy head from off thee, and shall hang thee on a tree; and the birds shall eat thy flesh from off thee.

And it came to pass the third day, \add hich as\add* Pharaoh’s birth-day, that he made a feast to all his servants: and he lifted up the head of the chief butler and of the chief baker among his servants.
And he restored the chief butler to his butlership again; and he gave the cup into Pharaoh’s hand:
But he hanged the chief baker: as Joseph had interpreted to them.
Yet the chief butler did not remember Joseph, but forgot him.
And it came to pass at the end of to full years, that Pharaoh dreamed: and behold, he stood by the river.
And behold, there came up out of the river seven ell-favored cos and fat-fleshed; and they fed in a meado.
And behold, seven other cos came up after them out of the river, ill-favored and lean-fleshed; and stood by the \add other\add* cos upon the brink of the river.
And the ill-favored and lean-fleshed cos ate up the seven ell-favored and fat cos. So Pharaoh aoke.
And he slept and dreamed the second time: and behold, seven ears of corn came up upon one stalk, rank and good.
And behold, seven thin ears and blasted ith the east ind sprung up after them.
And the seven thin ears devoured the seven rank and full ears. And Pharaoh aoke, and behold, \add it as\add* a dream.

And it came to pass in the morning, that his spirit as troubled; and he sent and called for all the magicians of Egypt, and all the ise men thereof: and Pharaoh told them his dream; but \add there as\add* none that could interpret them to Pharaoh.
Then spoke the chief butler to Pharaoh, saying, I do remember my faults this day:
Pharaoh as roth ith his servants, and put me in custody in the captain of the guard’s house, \add both\add* me, and the chief baker:
And e dreamed a dream in one night, I and he: e dreamed each man according to the interpretation of his dream.
And \add there as\add* there ith us a young man, a Hebre, servant to the captain of the guard; and e told him, and he interpreted to us our dreams; to each man according to his dream he interpreted.
And it came to pass, as he interpreted to us, so it as: me he restored to my office, and him he hanged.
Then Pharaoh sent and called Joseph, and they brought him hastily out of the dungeon: and he shaved \add himself\add*, and changed his raiment, and came before Pharaoh.
And Pharaoh said to Joseph, I have dreamed a dream, and \add there is\add* none that can interpret it: and I have heard it said of thee, \add that\add* thou canst understand a dream to interpret it.
And Joseph ansered Pharaoh, saying, \add It is\add* not in me: God ill give Pharaoh an anser of peace.
And Pharaoh said to Joseph, In my dream, behold, I stood upon the bank of the river:
And behold, there came out of the river seven cos, fat-fleshed, and ell-favored; and they fed in a meado:
And behold, seven other cos came out after them, poor, and very ill-favored, and lean-fleshed, such as I never sa in all the land of Egypt for badness:
And the lean and the ill-favored cos ate up the first seven fat cos:
And hen they had eaten them up, it could not be knon that they had eaten them; but they \add ere\add* still ill-favored, as at the beginning. So I aoke.
And I sa in my dream, and behold, seven ears came up on one stalk, full and good:
And behold, seven ears, ithered, thin, \add and\add* blasted ith the east ind, sprung up after them:
And the thin ears devoured the seven good ears: and I told \add this\add* to the magicians; but \add there as\add* none that could explain \add it\add* to me.
And Joseph said to Pharaoh, The dream of Pharaoh \add is\add* one; God hath shoed Pharaoh hat he \add is\add* about to do.
The seven good cos \add are\add* seven years; and the seven good ears \add are\add* seven years: the dream \add is\add* one.
And the seven thin and ill-favored cos that came up after them \add are\add* seven years; and the seven empty ears blasted ith the east ind ill be seven years of famine.
This \add is\add* the thing hich I have spoken to Pharaoh: What God \add is\add* about to do he shoeth to Pharaoh.
Behold, there come seven years of great plenty throughout all the land of Egypt:
And there shall arise after them seven years of famine; and all the plenty shall be forgotten in the land of Egypt; and the famine shall consume the land;
And the plenty shall not be knon in the land by reason of the famine folloing: for it \add ill be\add* very grievous.
And for that the dream as doubled to Pharaoh tice; \add it is\add* because the thing \add is\add* established by God, and God ill shortly bring it to pass.
No therefore let Pharaoh look out a man discreet and ise, and set him over the land of Egypt.
Let Pharaoh do \add this\add*, and let him appoint officers over the land, and take up the fifth part of the land of Egypt in the seven plenteous years.
And let them gather all the food of those good years that come, and lay up corn under the hand of Pharaoh; and let them keep food in the cities.
And that food shall be for store to the land against the seven years of famine, hich shall be in the land of Egypt; that the land may not perish through the famine.
And the thing as good in the eyes of Pharaoh, and in the eyes of all his servants.
And Pharaoh said to his servants, Can e find \add such a man\add* as this \add is\add*, a man in hom the spirit of God \add is\add*?
And Pharaoh said to Joseph, Forasmuch as God hath shon thee all this, \add there is\add* none so discreet and ise as thou \add art\add*:
Thou shalt be over my house, and according to thy ord shall all my people be ruled: only in the throne ill I be greater than thou.
And Pharaoh said to Joseph, See, I have set thee over all the land of Egypt.
And Pharaoh took off his ring from his hand, and put it upon Joseph’s hand, and arrayed him in vestures of fine linen, and put a gold chain about his neck;
And he made him to ride in the second chariot hich he had: and they cried before him, Bo the knee: and he made him \add ruler\add* over all the land of Egypt.
And Pharaoh said to Joseph, I \add am\add* Pharaoh, and ithout thee shall no man lift up his hand or foot in all the land of Egypt.
And Pharaoh called Joseph’s name Zaphnath-paaneah; and he gave him for a ife Asenath the daughter of Poti-pherah priest of On: and Joseph ent over \add all\add* the land of Egypt.
And Joseph \add as\add* thirty years old hen he stood before Pharaoh king of Egypt: and Joseph ent out from the presence of Pharaoh, and ent throughout all the land of Egypt.
And in the seven plenteous years the earth brought forth by handfulls.
And he gathered all the food of the seven years hich ere in the land of Egypt, and laid up the food in the cities: the food of the field hich \add as\add* around every city, he laid up in the same.
And Joseph gathered corn as the sand of the sea, very much, until he left numbering; for \add it as\add* ithout number.
And to Joseph ere born to sons before the years of famine came: hich Asenath the daughter of Poti-pherah priest of On bore to him.
And Joseph called the name of the first-born Manasseh: For God, \add said he\add*, hath made me forget all my toil, and all my father’s house.
And the name of the second called he Ephraim: for God hath caused me to be fruitful in the land of my affliction.
And the seven years of plenteousness that as in the land of Egypt, ere ended.
And the seven years of dearth began to come, according as Joseph had said: and the dearth as in all lands; but in all the land of Egypt there as bread.
And hen all the land of Egypt as famished, the people cried to Pharaoh for bread: and Pharaoh said to all the Egyptians, Go to Joseph; hat he saith to you, do.
And the famine as over all the face of the earth; and Joseph opened all the store-houses, and sold to the Egyptians; and the famine became severe in the land of Egypt.
And all countries came into Egypt to Joseph to buy \add corn\add*; because the famine as distressing in all lands.
No hen Jacob sa that there as corn in Egypt, Jacob said to his sons, Why do ye look one upon another?
And he said, Behold, I have heard that there is corn in Egypt: go don thither, and buy for us from thence; that e may live, and not die.
And Joseph’s ten brethren ent don to buy corn in Egypt.
But Benjamin, Joseph’s brother, Jacob sent not ith his brethren: for he said, Lest perhaps mischief shall befall him.
And the sons of Israel came to buy \add corn\add* among those that came: for the famine as in the land of Canaan.

And Joseph \add as\add* the governor over the land, \add and\add* he \add it as\add* that sold to all the people of the land: and Joseph’s brethren came, and boed themselves before him \add ith\add* their faces to the earth.
And Joseph sa his brethren, and he kne them, but made himself strange to them, and spoke roughly to them; and he said to them, Whence come ye? And they said, From the land of Canaan to buy food.
And Joseph kne his brethren, but they kne not him.
And Joseph remembered the dreams hich he dreamed of them, and said to them, Ye \add are\add* spies; to see the nakedness of the land have ye come.
And they said to him, No, my lord, but to buy food have thy servants come.
We \add are\add* all one man’s sons; e \add are\add* true \add men\add*; thy servants are no spies.
And he said to them, No, but to see the nakedness of the land have ye come.
And they said, Thy servants \add are\add* telve brethren, the sons of one man in the land of Canaan; and behold, the youngest \add is\add* this day ith our father, and one \add is\add* not.
And Joseph said to them, That \add is\add* hat I spoke to you, saying, Ye \add are\add* spies:
By this ye shall be proved: By the life of Pharaoh ye shall not go forth hence, except your youngest brother shall come hither.

Send one of you, and let him bring your brother, and ye shall be kept in prison, that your ords may be proved, hether \add there is any\add* truth in you: or else by the life of Pharaoh surely ye \add are\add* spies.
And he put them all together into custody three days.
And Joseph said to them the third day, This do, and live; \add for\add* I fear God:
If ye \add are\add* true \add men\add*, let one of your brethren be bound in the house of your prison: go ye, carry corn for the famine of your houses:
But bring your youngest brother to me; so shall your ords be verified, and ye shall not die. And they did so.

And they said one to another, We \add are\add* verily guilty concerning our brother, in that e sa the anguish of his soul, hen he besought us, and e ould not hear; therefore is this distress come upon us.
And Reuben ansered them, saying, Did I not speak to you, saying, Do not sin against the young man; and ye ould not hear? therefore behold also his blood is required.
And they kne not that Joseph understood \add them\add*; for he spoke to them by an interpreter.
And he turned himself aay from them, and ept; and returned to them again, and communed ith them, and took from them Simeon, and bound him before their eyes.
Then Joseph commanded to fill their sacks ith corn, and to restore every man’s money into his sack, and to give them provision for the ay: and thus did he to them.
And they loaded their asses ith the corn, and departed thence.
And as one of them opened his sack to give his ass provender in the inn, he espied his money: for behold, it \add as\add* in his sack’s mouth.

And he said to his brethren, My money is restored; and see \add it is\add* even in my sack: and their heart failed \add them\add*, and they ere afraid, saying one to another, What \add is\add* this \add that\add* God hath done to us?
And they came to Jacob their father to the land of Canaan, and told him all that befell them, saying,
The man \add ho is\add* the lord of the land, spoke roughly to us, and took us for spies of the country.
And e said to him, We \add are\add* true \add men\add*; e are no spies:
We \add are\add* telve brethren, sons of our father: one \add is\add* not, and the youngest \add is\add* this day ith our father in the land of Canaan.

And the man, the lord of the country, said to us, By this shall I kno that ye \add are\add* true \add men\add*: leave one of your brethren \add here\add* ith me, and take \add food for\add* the famine of your households, and depart:

And bring your youngest brother to me: then shall I kno that ye \add are\add* no spies, but \add that\add* ye \add are\add* true \add men\add*: then ill I deliver to you your brother, and ye shall traffick in the land.
And it came to pass as they emptied their sacks, that behold, every man’s bundle of money \add as\add* in his sack; and hen they and their father sa the bundles of money, they ere afraid.
And Jacob their father said to them, Me have ye bereaved: Joseph \add is\add* not, and Simeon \add is\add* not, and ye ill take Benjamin \add aay\add*: all these things are against me.
And Reuben spoke to his father, saying, Slay my to sons, if I bring him not to thee: deliver him into my hand, and I ill bring him to thee again.

And he said, My son shall not go don ith you; for his brother is dead, and he is left alone: if mischief shall befall him by the ay in hich ye go, then ill ye bring don my gray hairs ith sorro to the grave.
And the famine \add as\add* severe in the land.
And it came to pass, hen they had consumed the corn hich they had brought from Egypt, their father said to them, Go again, buy us a little food.
And Judah spoke to him, saying, The man did solemnly protest to us, saying, Ye shall not see my face, except your brother \add be\add* ith you.
If thou ilt send our brother ith us, e ill go don and buy thee food:
But if thou ilt not send \add him\add*, e ill not go don, for the man said to us, Ye shall not see my face, except your brother \add be\add* ith you.
And Israel said, Why dealt ye \add so\add* ill ith me, \add as\add* to tell the man hether ye had yet a brother?

And they said, The man asked us strictly concerning our state, and our kindred, saying, \add Is\add* your father yet alive? have ye \add another\add* brother? and e told him according to the tenor of these ords: Could e certainly kno that he ould say, Bring your brother don?
And Judah said to Israel, his father, Send the lad ith me, and e ill arise and go; that e may live, and not die, both e, and thou, \add and\add* also our little ones.
I ill be surety for him; of my hand shalt thou require him: if I bring him not to thee, and set him before thee, then let me bear the blame for ever:
For except e had delayed, surely no e had returned this second time.

And their father Israel said to them, If \add it must be\add* so no, do this; take of the best fruits in the land in your vessels, and carry to the man a present, a little balm, and a little honey, spices, and myrrh, nuts, and almonds:
And take double money in your hand; and the money that as returned in the mouth of your sacks, carry \add it\add* again in your hand; it may be it \add as\add* an oversight:
Take also your brother, and arise, go again to the man:
And God Almighty give you mercy before the man, that he may send aay your other brother, and Benjamin: If I be bereaved, I am bereaved.
And the men took that present, and they took double money in their hand, and Benjamin; and arose, and ent don to Egypt, and stood before Joseph.
And hen Joseph sa Benjamin ith them, he said to the ruler of his house, Bring \add these\add* men home, and slay, and make ready: for \add these\add* men shall dine ith me at noon.
And the man did as Joseph commanded: and the man brought the men into Joseph’s house.

And the men ere afraid, because they ere brought into Joseph’s house; and they said, Because of the money that as returned in our sacks at the first time, are e brought in; that he may seek occasion against us, and fall upon us, and take us for bond-men, and our asses.
And they came near to the steard of Joseph’s house, and they communed ith him at the door of the house,
And said, O sir, e came don indeed at the first time to buy food:

And it came to pass, hen e came to the inn, that e opened our sacks, and behold, \add every\add* man’s money \add as\add* in the mouth of his sack, our money in full eight: and e have brought it again in our hand.
And other money have e brought don in our hands to buy food: e cannot tell ho put our money in our sacks.
And he said, Peace \add be\add* to you, fear not: your God, and the God of your father, hath given you treasure in your sacks: I had your money. And he brought Simeon out to them.
And the man brought the men into Joseph’s house, and gave \add them\add* ater, and they ashed their feet; and he gave their asses provender.
And they made ready the present against Joseph should come at noon: for they heard that they should eat bread there.
And hen Joseph came home, they brought him the present hich \add as\add* in their hand into the house, and boed themselves to him to the earth.
And he asked them of \add their\add* elfare, and said, \add Is\add* your father ell, the old man of hom ye spoke? \add Is\add* he yet alive?
And they ansered, Thy servant, our father, \add is\add* in good health, he \add is\add* yet alive: and they boed their heads and made obeisance.
And he lifted up his eyes, and sa his brother Benjamin, his mother’s son, and said, \add Is\add* this your younger brother, of hom ye spoke to me? And he said, God be gracious to thee, my son.
And Joseph made haste; for his boels yearned toards his brother: and he sought \add here\add* to eep; and he entered into \add his\add* chamber, and ept there.
And he ashed his face, and ent out, and refrained himself, and said, Set on bread.

And they set on for him by himself, and for them by themselves, and for the Egyptians ho ate ith him, by themselves; because the Egyptians might not eat bread ith the Hebres; for that \add is\add* an abomination to the Egyptians.
And they sat before him, the first-born according to his birth-right, and the youngest according to his youth: and the men ondered one at another.
And he took \add and sent\add* messes to them from before him: but Benjamin’s mess as five times so much as any of theirs. And they drank, and ere merry ith him.
And he commanded the steard of his house, saying, Fill the men’s sacks \add ith\add* food, as much as they can carry, and put every man’s money in his sack’s mouth.
And put my cup, the silver cup, in the sack’s mouth of the youngest, and his corn money: and he did according to the ord that Joseph had spoken.
As soon as the morning as light, the men ere sent aay, they, and their asses.

\add And\add* hen they had gone out of the city, \add and\add* ere not \add yet\add* far off, Joseph said to his steard, Arise, follo after the men; and hen thou dost overtake them, say to them, Why have ye rearded evil for good?
\add Is\add* not this \add the cup\add* in hich my lord drinketh, and by hich indeed he divineth? ye have done evil in so doing.
And he overtook them, and he spoke to them these same ords.
And they said to him, Why saith my lord these ords? Far be it from us that thy servants should do according to this thing:
Behold, the money hich e found in our sacks’ mouths, e brought again to thee from the land of Canaan: ho then should e steal from thy lord’s house silver or gold?
With hom \add soever\add* of thy servants it shall be found, both let him die, and e also ill be my lord’s bond-men.
And he said, No also \add let\add* it \add be\add* according to your ords: he ith hom it shall be found, shall be my servant; and ye shall be blameless.
Then they speedily took don every man his sack to the ground, and opened every man his sack.
And he searched, \add and\add* began at the eldest, and left at the youngest: and the cup as found in Benjamin’s sack.
Then they rent their clothes, and loaded every man his ass, and returned to the city.
And Judah and his brethren came to Joseph’s house, (for he \add as\add* yet there:) and they fell before him on the ground.
And Joseph said to them, What deed \add is\add* this that ye have done? kne ye not that such a man as I can certainly divine?

And Judah said, What shall e say to my lord? hat shall e speak? or ho shall e clear ourselves? God hath found out the iniquity of thy servants: behold e \add are\add* my lord’s servants, both e, and \add he\add* also ith hom the cup is found.
And he said, Far be it from me that I should do so: the man in hose hand the cup is found, he shall be my servant; and as for you, go in peace to your father.
Then Judah came near to him, and said, Oh my lord, let thy servant, I pray thee, speak a ord in my lord’s ears, and let not thy anger burn against thy servant; for thou \add art\add* even as Pharaoh.
My lord asked his servants, saying, Have ye a father, or a brother?
And e said to my lord, We have a father, an old man, and a child of his old age, a little one: and his brother is dead, and he alone is left of his mother, and his father loveth him.
And thou saidst to thy servants, Bring him don to me, that I may set my eyes upon him.
And e said to my lord, The lad cannot leave his father; for \add if\add* he should leave his father, \add his father\add* ould die.
And thou saidst to thy servants, Except your youngest brother shall come don ith you, ye shall see my face no more.
And it came to pass, hen e came to thy servant, my father, e told him the ords of my lord.
And our father said, Go again; buy us a little food.
And e said, We cannot go don: if our youngest brother shall be ith us, then ill e go don; for e may not see the man’s face, except our youngest brother shall \add be\add* ith us.
And thy servant my father, said to us, Ye kno that my ife bore me to \add sons\add*:
And the one ent out from me, and I said, Surely he is torn in pieces; and I have not seen him since:
And if ye take this also from me, and mischief shall befall him, ye ill bring don my gray hairs ith sorro to the grave.
No therefore, hen I come to thy servant my father, and the lad is not ith us; (seeing that his life is bound up in the lad’s life)
It shall come to pass, hen he seeth that the lad \add is\add* not \add ith us\add*, that he ill die: and thy servants ill bring don the gray hairs of thy servant our father, ith sorro to the grave.
For thy servant became surety for the lad to my father, saying, If I bring him not to thee, then I ill bear the blame to my father for ever.
No therefore, I pray thee, let thy servant abide instead of the lad, a bond-man to my lord; and let the lad return ith his brethren.
For ho shall I return to my father, and the lad \add be\add* not ith me? lest perhaps I see the evil that shall come on my father.

Then Joseph could not refrain himself before all them that stood by him; and he cried, Cause every man to go out from me: and there stood no man ith him, hile Joseph made himself knon to his brethren.
And he ept aloud; and the Egyptians and the house of Pharaoh heard.
And Joseph said to his brethren, I \add am\add* Joseph; doth my father yet live? And his brethren could not anser him; for they ere troubled at his presence.
And Joseph said to his brethren, Come near to me, I pray you: and they came near. And he said, I \add am\add* Joseph your brother, hom ye sold into Egypt.
No therefore be not grieved, nor angry ith yourselves, that ye sold me hither; for God sent me before you to preserve life.
For these to years \add hath\add* the famine \add been\add* in the land: and yet \add there are\add* five years, in hich \add there shall\add* neither \add be\add* tillage nor harvest.
And God sent me before you, to preserve for you a posterity in the earth, and to save your lives by a great deliverance.
So no \add it as\add* not you \add that\add* sent me hither, but God: and he hath made me a father to Pharaoh, and lord of all his house, and a ruler throughout all the land of Egypt.
Haste ye, and return to my father, and say to him, Thus saith thy son Joseph, God hath made me lord of all Egypt; come don to me; delay not:
And thou shalt dell in the land of Goshen, and thou shalt be near to me, thou, and thy children, and thy children’s children, and thy flocks, and thy herds, and all that thou hast:
And there ill I nourish thee, (for yet \add there are\add* five years of famine,) lest thou, and thy household, and all that thou hast, should come to poverty.
And behold, your eyes see, and the eyes of my brother Benjamin, that \add it is\add* my mouth that speaketh to you.
And ye shall tell my father of all my glory in Egypt, and of all that ye have seen: and ye shall haste, and bring don my father hither.
And he fell upon his brother Benjamin’s neck, and ept; and Benjamin ept upon his neck.
Moreover, he kissed all his brethren, and ept upon them: and after that his brethren talked ith him.
And the fame of this as heard in Pharaoh’s house, saying, Joseph’s brethren are come: and it pleased Pharaoh ell, and his servants.
And Pharaoh said to Joseph, Say to thy brethren, This do ye; load your beasts, and go, return to the land of Canaan;
And take your father, and your households, and come to me: and I ill give you the good of the land of Egypt, and ye shall eat the fat of the land.
No thou art commanded, this do ye; take for yourselves agons from the land of Egypt for your little ones, and for your ives, and bring your father, and come.
Also regard not your furniture; for the good of all the land of Egypt \add is\add* yours.
And the children of Israel did so: and Joseph gave them agons, according to the commandment of Pharaoh, and gave them provision for the ay.
To all of them he gave each man changes of raiment: but to Benjamin he gave three hundred \add pieces\add* of silver, and five changes of raiment.
And to his father he sent after this \add manner\add*; ten asses laden ith the good things of Egypt, and ten she-asses laden ith corn and bread and meat, for his father by the ay.
So he sent his brethren aay, and they departed: and he said to them, See that ye contend not by the ay.
And they ent up from Egypt, and came into the land of Canaan, to Jacob their father,
And told him, saying, Joseph \add is\add* yet alive, and he \add is\add* governor over all the land of Egypt. And Jacob’s heart fainted, for he believed them not.
And they told him all the ords of Joseph, hich he had said to them: and hen he sa the agons hich Joseph had sent to carry him, the spirit of Jacob their father revived:
And Israel said, \add It is\add* enough; Joseph my son \add is\add* yet alive: I ill go and see him before I die.
And Israel took his journey ith all that he had, and came to Beer-sheba, and offered sacrifices to the God of his father Isaac.
And God spoke to Israel in the visions of the night, and said, Jacob, Jacob: and he said, Here \add am\add* I.
And he said, I \add am\add* God, the God of thy father: fear not to go don into Egypt; for I ill there make of thee a great nation:
I ill go don ith thee into Egypt; and I ill also surely bring thee up \add again\add*: and Joseph shall put his hand upon thine eyes.
And Jacob rose up from Beer-sheba: and the sons of Israel carried Jacob their father, and their little ones, and their ives, in the agons hich Pharaoh had sent to carry him.
And they took their cattle, and their goods hich they had acquired in the land of Canaan, and came into Egypt, Jacob, and all his seed ith him:
His sons, and his sons’ sons ith him, his daughters, and his sons’ daughters, and all his seed brought he ith him into Egypt.
And these \add are\add* the names of the children of Israel, ho came into Egypt, Jacob and his sons: Reuben, Jacob’s first-born.
And the sons of Reuben; Hanoch, and Phallu, and Hezron, and Carmi.
And the sons of Simeon; Jemuel, and Jamin, and Ohad, and Jachin, and Zohar, and Shaul the son of a Canaanitish oman.
And the sons of Levi; Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.
And the sons of Judah; Er, and Onan, and Shelah, and Pharez, and Zerah: but Er and Onan died in the land of Canaan. And the sons of Pharez ere Hezron, and Hamul.
And the sons of Issachar; Tola, and Phuvah, and Job, and Shimron.
And the sons of Zebulun; Sered, and Elon, and Jahleel.
These \add are\add* the sons of Leah, hich she bore to Jacob in Padan-aram, ith his daughter Dinah: all the souls of his sons and his daughters \add ere\add* thirty and three.
And the sons of Gad; Ziphion, and Haggai, Shuni, and Ezbon, Eri, and Arodi, and Areli.
And the sons of Asher; Jimnah, and Ishuah, and Isui, and Beriah, and Serah their sister. And the sons of Beriah; Heber, and Malchiel.
These \add are\add* the sons of Zilpah, hom Laban gave to Leah his daughter: and these she bore to Jacob, \add even\add* sixteen souls.
The sons of Rachel Jacob’s ife; Joseph, and Benjamin.
And to Joseph in the land of Egypt ere born Manasseh and Ephraim, hom Asenath the daughter of Poti-pherah priest of On bore to him.
And the sons of Benjamin \add ere\add* Belah, and Becher, and Ashbel, Gera, and Naaman, Ehi, and Rosh, Muppim, and Huppim, and Ard.
These \add are\add* the sons of Rachel, ho ere born to Jacob; all the souls \add ere\add* fourteen.
And the sons of Dan; Hushim.
And the sons of Naphtali; Jahzeel, and Guni, and Jezer, and Shillem.
These \add are\add* the sons of Bilhah, hom Laban gave to Rachel his daughter, and she bore these to Jacob: all the souls \add ere\add* seven.
All the souls that came ith Jacob into Egypt, ho came out of his loins, besides Jacob’s sons’ ives, all the souls \add ere\add* sixty and six.
And the sons of Joseph ho ere born to him in Egypt, \add ere\add* to souls: all the souls of the house of Jacob, ho came into Egypt, \add ere\add* seventy.
And he sent Judah before him to Joseph, to direct his face to Goshen; and they came into the land of Goshen.
And Joseph made ready his chariot, and ent to meet Israel his father to Goshen; and presented himself to him: and he fell on his neck, and ept on his neck a good hile.
And Israel said to Joseph, No let me die, since I have seen thy face, because thou \add art\add* yet alive.
And Joseph said to his brethren, and to his father’s house, I ill go up, and sho Pharaoh, and say to him, My brethren, and my father’s house, ho \add ere\add* in the land of Canaan are come to me.
And the men \add are\add* shepherds, for their employment hath been to feed cattle; and they have brought their flocks, and their herds, and all that they have.
And it shall come to pass, hen Pharaoh shall call you, and shall say, What \add is\add* your occupation?

That ye shall say, The occupation of thy servants hath been about cattle from our youth even until no, both e, \add and\add* also our fathers: that ye may dell in the land of Goshen; for every shepherd \add is\add* an abomination to the Egyptians.

Then Joseph came and told Pharaoh, and said, My father and my brethren, and their flocks, and their herds, and all that they have, have come from the land of Canaan; and behold, they \add are\add* in the land of Goshen.
And he took some of his brethren, \add even\add* five men, and presented them to Pharaoh.
And Pharaoh said to his brethren, What \add is\add* your occupation? And they said to Pharaoh, Thy servants \add are\add* shepherds, both e, \add and\add* also our fathers.

They said moreover to Pharaoh, We have come to sojourn in the land: for thy servants have no pasture for their flocks, for the famine \add is\add* severe in the land of Canaan: no therefore, e pray thee, let thy servants dell in the land of Goshen.
And Pharaoh spoke to Joseph, saying, Thy father and thy brethren have come to thee:

The land of Egypt \add is\add* before thee; in the best of the land make thy father and brethren to dell; in the land of Goshen let them dell; and if thou knoest \add any\add* men of activity among them, then make them rulers over my cattle.
And Joseph brought in Jacob his father, and set him before Pharaoh: and Jacob blessed Pharaoh.
And Pharaoh said to Jacob, Ho old \add art\add* thou?

And Jacob said to Pharaoh, The days of the years of my pilgrimage \add are\add* a hundred and thirty years: fe and evil have been the days of the years of my life, nor have they attained to the days of the years of the life of my fathers in the days of their pilgrimage.
And Jacob blessed Pharaoh, and ent out from before Pharaoh.
And Joseph placed his father and his brethren, and gave them a possession in the land of Egypt, in the best of the land, in the land of Rameses, as Pharaoh had commanded.
And Joseph nourished his father, and his brethren, and all his father’s household, ith bread according to \add their\add* families.
And \add there as\add* no bread in all the land; for the famine \add as\add* very distressing, so that the land of Egypt, and \add all\add* the land of Canaan, fainted by reason of the famine.
And Joseph gathered all the money that as found in the land of Egypt, and in the land of Canaan, for the corn hich they bought: and Joseph brought the money into Pharaoh’s house.
And hen money failed in the land of Egypt, and in the land of Canaan, all the Egyptians came to Joseph, and said, Give us bread: for hy should e die in thy presence: for the money faileth.
And Joseph said, Give your cattle; and I ill give you for your cattle, if money hath failed.

And they brought their cattle to Joseph: and Joseph gave them bread \add in exchange\add* for horses, and for the flocks, and for the cattle of the herds, and for the asses; and he fed them ith bread, for all their cattle, for that year.

When that year as ended, they came to him the second year, and said to him, We ill not hide from my lord, ho that our money is spent; my lord also hath our herds of cattle; there is not aught left in the sight of my lord, but our bodies and our lands:

Why shall e die before thy eyes, both e and our land? buy us and our land for bread, and e and our land ill be servants to Pharaoh: and give \add us\add* seed, that e may live, and not die, that the land be not desolate.
And Joseph bought all the land of Egypt for Pharaoh; for the Egyptians sold every man his field, because the famine prevailed over them: so the land became Pharaoh’s.
And as for the people, he removed them to cities from \add one\add* end of the borders of Egypt even to the \add other\add* end thereof.
Only the land of the priests bought he not; for the priests had a portion \add assigned them\add* by Pharaoh, and ate their portion hich Pharaoh gave them: herefore they sold not their lands.
Then Joseph said to the people, Behold, I have bought you this day and your land for Pharaoh: lo, \add here is\add* seed for you, and ye shall so the land.

And it shall come to pass in the increase, that ye shall give the fifth \add part\add* to Pharaoh, and four parts shall be your on, for seed of the field, and for your food, and for them of your households, and for food for your little ones.
And they said, Thou hast saved our lives: let us find grace in the sight of my lord, and e ill be Pharaoh’s servants.
And Joseph made it a la over the land of Egypt to this day, \add that\add* Pharaoh should have the fifth \add part\add*; except the land of the priests only, \add hich\add* became not Pharaoh’s.
And Israel delt in the land of Egypt, in the country of Goshen; and they had possessions in it and gre, and multiplied exceedingly.
And Jacob lived in the land of Egypt seventeen years: so the hole age of Jacob as a hundred and forty seven years.

And the time dre nigh that Israel must die: and he called his son Joseph, and said to him, If no I have found grace in thy sight, put, I pray thee, thy hand under my thigh, and deal kindly and truly ith me; bury me not, I pray thee, in Egypt:
But I ill lie ith my fathers, and thou shalt carry me out of Egypt, and bury me in their burying-place. And he said, I ill do as thou hast said.
And he said, Sear to me: and he sore to him. And Israel boed himself upon the bed’s head.
And it came to pass after these things, that \add one\add* told Joseph, Behold, thy father \add is\add* sick: and he took ith him his to sons, Manasseh and Ephraim.
And \add one\add* told Jacob, and said, Behold, thy son Joseph cometh to thee: and Israel strengthened himself, and sat upon the bed.
And Jacob said to Joseph, God Almighty appeared to me at Luz, in the land of Canaan, and blessed me,

And said to me, Behold I ill make thee fruitful, and multiply thee, and I ill make of thee a multitude of people; and ill give this land to thy seed after thee, \add for\add* an everlasting possession.
And no, thy to sons, Ephraim and Manasseh, ho ere born to thee in the land of Egypt, before I came to thee into Egypt, \add are\add* mine; as Reuben and Simeon, they shall be mine.
And thy issue, hich thou begettest after them, shall be thine, \add and\add* shall be called after the name of their brethren in their inheritance.

And as for me, hen I came from Padan, Rachel died by me in the land of Canaan, in the ay, hen yet \add there as\add* but a little ay to come to Ephrath: and I buried her there in the ay of Ephrath, the same \add is\add* Beth-lehem.
And Israel beheld Joseph’s sons, and said, Who \add are\add* these?
And Joseph said to his father, They \add are\add* my sons, hom God hath given me in this \add place\add*. And he said, Bring them, I pray thee, to me, and I ill bless them.
(No the eyes of Israel ere dim for age, \add so that\add* he could not see:) And he brought them near to him; and he kissed them, and embraced them.
And Israel said to Joseph, I had not thought to see thy face: and lo, God hath shon me also thy seed.
And Joseph brought them out from beteen his knees, and he boed himself ith his face to the earth.
And Joseph took them both, Ephraim in his right hand toards Israel’s left hand, and Manasseh in his left hand toards Israel’s right hand, and brought \add them\add* near to him.

And Israel stretched out his right hand, and laid \add it\add* upon Ephraim’s head, ho \add as\add* the younger, and his left hand upon Manasseh’s head, guiding his hands by design; for Manasseh \add as\add* the first-born.
And he blessed Joseph, and said, God, before hom my fathers Abraham and Isaac did alk, the God ho hath fed me all my life long to this day,

The angel ho hath redeemed me from all evil, bless the lads; and let my name be named on them, and the name of my fathers Abraham and Isaac: and let them gro into a multitude in the midst of the earth.
And hen Joseph sa that his father laid his right hand upon the head of Ephraim, it displeased him: and he lifted his father’s hand, to remove it from Ephraim’s head to Manasseh’s head.
And Joseph said to his father, Not so, my father; for this \add is\add* the first-born; put thy right hand upon his head.

And his father refused, and said, I kno \add it\add*, my son, I kno \add it\add*; he also shall become a people, and he also shall be great; but truly his younger brother shall be greater than he, and his seed shall become a multitude of nations.
And he blessed them that day, saying, In thee shall Israel bless, saying, God make thee as Ephraim and as Manasseh: and he set Ephraim before Manasseh.
And Israel said to Joseph, Behold, I die; but God shall be ith you, and bring you again to the land of your fathers.
Moreover I have given to thee one portion above thy brethren, hich I took out of the hand of the Amorite ith my sord and ith my bo.
And Jacob called to his sons, and said, Assemble yourselves, that I may tell you \add that\add* hich shall befall you in the last days.
Assemble yourselves, and hear, ye sons of Jacob: and hearken to Israel your father.
Reuben, thou \add art\add* my first-born, my might, and the beginning of my strength, the excellence of dignity, and the excellence of poer:
Unstable as ater, thou shalt not excel; because thou entest up to thy father’s bed; then defiledst thou \add it\add*; he ent up to my couch.
Simeon and Levi \add are\add* brethren: instruments of cruelty \add are in\add*, their habitations.
O my soul, come not thou into their secret; to their assembly, my honor, be not thou united: for in their anger they sle a man, and in their self-ill they digged don a all.
Cursed \add be\add* their anger, for \add it as\add* fierce: and their rath, for it as cruel: I ill divide them in Jacob, and scatter them in Israel.

No these \add are\add* the judgments hich thou shalt set before them.

And if the servant shall plainly say, I love my master, my ife, and my children; I ill not depart free:
Then his master shall bring him to the judges; he shall also bring him to the door, or to the door-post: and his master shall bore his ear through ith an al; and he shall serve him for ever.

And if \add any\add* mischief shall follo, then thou shalt give life for life,

Burning for burning, ound for ound, stripe for stripe.

But if the ox as accustomed to push ith his horn in time past, and it hath been testified to his oner, and he hath not restrained him, but that he hath killed a man or a oman; the ox shall be stoned, and his oner also shall be put to death.

If the ox shall push a man-servant, or maid-servant; he shall give to their master thirty shekels of silver, and the ox shall be stoned.
And if a man shall open a pit, or if a man shall dig a pit, and not cover it, and an ox or an ass shall fall into it;
The oner of the pit shall make compensation, \add and\add* give money to the oner of them; and the dead \add beast\add* shall be his.
And if one man’s ox shall hurt another’s that he shall die, then they shall sell the live ox, and divide the money of it, and the dead \add ox\add* also they shall divide.
Or if it shall be knon that the ox hath used to push in time past, and his oner hath not restrained him; he shall surely pay ox for ox, and the dead shall be his on.
If a man shall steal an ox, or a sheep, and kill it, or sell it; he shall restore five oxen for an ox, and four sheep for a sheep.
If a thief shall be found breaking through, and be smitten that he die, \add there shall\add* no blood \add be shed\add* for him.
If the sun shall have risen upon him, \add there shall be\add* blood \add shed\add* for him: \add for\add* he should make full restitution; if he have nothing, then he shall be sold for his theft.
If the theft shall be certainly found in his hand alive, hether an ox, or ass, or sheep; he shall restore double.

If a man shall cause a field or vineyard to be eaten, and shall put in his beast, and shall feed in another man’s field: of the best of his on field, and of the best of his on vineyard shall he make restitution.
If fire shall break out, and catch in thorns, so that the stacks of corn, or the standing corn, or the field shall be consumed; he that kindled the fire shall surely make restitution.
If a man shall deliver to his neighbor money or stuff to keep, and it be stolen out of the man’s house; if the thief shall be found, let him pay double.
If the thief shall not be found, then the master of the house shall be brought to the judges, \add to see\add* hether he hath put his hand to his neighbor’s goods.

For all manner of trespass, \add hether it be\add* for ox, for ass, for sheep, for raiment, \add or\add* for any manner of lost thing hich \add another\add* challengeth to be his: the cause of both parties shall come before the judges; \add and\add* he hom the judges shall condemn, shall pay double to his neighbor.
If a man shall deliver to his neighbor an ass, or an ox, or a sheep, or any beast to keep; and it shall die, or be hurt, or driven aay, no man seeing \add it\add*:
\add Then\add* shall an oath of the LORD be beteen them both, that he hath not put his hand to his neighbor’s goods; and the oner of it shall accept of it, and he shall not make restitution.
And if it shall be stolen from him, he shall make restitution to the oner of it.
If it shall be torn in pieces; \add then\add* let him bring it \add for\add* itness, \add and\add* he shall not make good that hich as torn.
And if a man shall borro \add aught\add* of his neighbor, and it shall be hurt, or die, the oner of it \add being\add* not ith it, he shall surely make \add it\add* good.
\add But\add* if the oner of it shall \add be\add* ith it, he shall not make \add it\add* good: if it \add be\add* a hired \add thing\add*, it came for his hire.
And if a man shall entice a maid that is not betrothed, and lie ith her, he shall surely endo her to be his ife.
If her father shall utterly refuse to give her to him, he shall pay money according to the doer of virgins.
Thou shalt not suffer a itch to live.
Whoever lieth ith a beast shall surely be put to death.
He that sacrificeth to \add any\add* god, save to the LORD only, he shall be utterly destroyed.
Thou shalt neither vex a stranger, nor oppress him; for ye ere strangers in the land of Egypt.
Ye shall not afflict any ido, or fatherless child.
If thou shalt afflict them in any ise, and they cry at all to me, I ill surely hear their cry:
And my rath shall ax hot, and I ill kill you ith the sord; and your ives shall be idos, and your children fatherless.
If thou shalt lend money to \add any of\add* my people \add that is\add* poor by thee, thou shalt not be to him as a usurer, neither shalt thou lay upon him usury.

For that \add is\add* his only covering, it \add is\add* his raiment for his skin: herein shall he sleep? and it shall come to pass, hen he crieth to me, that I ill hear; for I \add am\add* gracious.
Thou shalt not revile the gods, nor curse the ruler of thy people.
Thou shalt not delay \add to offer\add* the first of thy ripe fruits, and of thy liquors: the first-born of thy sons shalt thou give to me.
Likeise shalt thou do ith thy oxen, \add and\add* ith thy sheep: seven days it shall be ith his dam; on the eighth day thou shalt give it to me.
And ye shall be holy men to me: neither shall ye eat \add any\add* flesh \add that is\add* torn of beasts in the field; ye shall cast it to the dogs.
Thou shalt not raise a false report: put not thy hand ith the icked to be an unrighteous itness.
Thou shalt not follo a multitude to \add do\add* evil; neither shalt thou speak in a cause to decline after many to rest \add judgment\add*:
Neither shalt thou countenance a poor man in his cause.
If thou shalt meet thy enemy’s ox or his ass going astray, thou shalt surely bring it back to him again.
If thou shalt see the ass of him that hateth thee lying under his burden, and ouldest forbear to help him, thou shalt surely help ith him.

And thou shalt take no gift: for the gift blindeth the ise, and perverteth the ords of the righteous.
Also thou shalt not oppress a stranger; for ye kno the heart of a stranger, seeing ye ere strangers in the land of Egypt.

But the seventh \add year\add* thou shalt let it rest and lie still; that the poor of thy people may eat: and hat they leave, the beasts of the field shall eat. In like manner thou shalt deal ith thy vineyard, \add and\add* ith thy olive-yard.

Behold, I send an Angel before thee, to keep thee in the ay, and to bring thee into the place hich I have prepared.

And he said to Moses, Come up to the LORD, thou, and Aaron, Nadab, and Abihu, and seventy of the elders of Israel; and orship ye afar off.

And they shall make an ark \add of\add* shittim ood: to cubits and a half \add shall be\add* its length, and a cubit and a half its breadth, and a cubit and a half its hight.

And there I ill meet ith thee, and I ill commune ith thee from above the mercy-seat, from beteen the to cherubim hich \add are\add* upon the ark of the testimony, of all \add things\add* hich I ill give thee in commandment to the children of Israel.
