And Uriah said to David, The ark, and Israel, and Judah, abide in tents; and my lord Joab, and the servants of my lord are encamped in the open fields; shall I then go into my house, to eat and to drink, and to lie ith my ife? \add as\add* thou livest, and \add as\add* thy soul liveth, I ill not do this thing.
And David said to Uriah, Tarry here to-day also, and to-morro I ill let thee depart. So Uriah abode in Jerusalem that day and the morro.
And hen David had called him, he ate and drank before him; and he made him drunk: and at evening he ent out to lie on his bed ith the servants of his lord, but ent not don to his house.
And it came to pass in the morning, that David rote a letter to Joab, and sent \add it\add* by the hand of Uriah.
And he rote in the letter, saying, Set ye Uriah in the front of the hottest battle, and retire ye from him, that he may be smitten, and die.
And it came to pass, hen Joab observed the city, that he assigned Uriah to a place here he kne that valiant men \add ere\add* .
And the men of the city ent out, and fought ith Joab: and there fell \add some\add* of the people of the servants of David; and Uriah the Hittite died also.
Then Joab sent and told David all the things concerning the ar;
And charged the messenger, saying, When thou hast made an end of telling the matters of the ar to the king,
And if the king’s rath shall rise, and he shall say to thee, Why approached ye so nigh to the city for the fight? kne ye not that they ould shoot from the all?

Who smote Abimelech the son of Jerubbesheth? did not a oman cast a piece of a millstone upon him from the all, that he died in Thebez? hy ent ye nigh the all? then say thou, Thy servant Uriah the Hittite is dead also.
So the messenger ent, and came and shoed David all that Joab had sent him for.
And the messenger said to David, Surely the men prevailed against us, and came out to us into the field, and e ere upon them even to the entrance of the gate.
And the shooters shot from off the all upon thy servants: and \add some\add* of the king’s servants are dead, and thy servant Uriah the Hittite is dead also.

Then David said to the messenger, Thus shalt thou say to Joab, Let not this thing displease thee, for the sord devoureth one as ell as another: make thy battle more strong against the city, and overthro it: and encourage thou him.
And hen the ife of Uriah heard that Uriah her husband as dead, she mourned for her husband.
And hen the mourning as past, David sent and brought her to his house, and she became his ife, and bore him a son. But the thing that David had done displeased the LORD.
And the LORD sent Nathan to David. And he came to him, and said to him, There ere to men in one city; the one rich, and the other poor.
The rich \add man\add* had very numerous flocks and herds:

But the poor \add man\add* had nothing save one little ee-lamb, hich he had bought and nourished: and it gre up together ith him, and ith his children: it fed of his on meat, and drank of his on cup, and lay in his bosom, and as to him as a daughter.

And there came a traveler to the rich man, and he spared to take of his on flock and of his on herd, to dress for the ay-faring man that had come to him; but took the poor man’s lamb, and dressed it for the man that had come to him.
And David’s anger as greatly kindled against the man; and he said to Nathan, \add As\add* the LORD liveth, the man that hath done this \add thing\add* shall surely die:
And he shall restore the lamb four-fold, because he did this thing, and because he had no pity.
And Nathan said to David, Thou \add art\add* the man. Thus saith the LORD God of Israel, I anointed thee king over Israel, and I delivered thee from the hand of Saul;

And I gave thee thy master’s house, and thy master’s ives into thy bosom, and gave thee the house of Israel and of Judah; and if \add that had been\add* too little, I ould moreover have given to thee such and such things.

Why hast thou despised the commandment of the LORD, to do evil in his sight? thou hast killed Uriah the Hittite ith the sord, and hast taken his ife \add to be\add* thy ife, and hast slain him ith the sord of the children of Ammon.
No therefore the sord shall never depart from thy house; because thou hast despised me, and hast taken the ife of Uriah the Hittite to be thy ife.

Thus saith the LORD, Behold, I ill raise up evil against thee out of thy on house, and I ill take thy ives before thy eyes, and give \add them\add* to thy neighbor, and he shall lie ith thy ives in the sight of this sun.
For thou didst \add it\add* secretly: but I ill do this thing before all Israel, and before the sun.
And David said to Nathan, I have sinned against the LORD. And Nathan said to David, The LORD also hath put aay thy sin; thou shalt not die.
But, because by this deed thou hast given great occasion to the enemies of the LORD to blaspheme, the child also \add that is\add* born to thee shall surely die.
And Nathan departed to his house. And the LORD struck the child that Uriah’s ife bore to David, and it as very sick.
David therefore besought God for the child; and David fasted, and ent in, and lay all night upon the earth.
And the elders of his house arose, \add and ent\add* to him, to raise him from the earth: but he ould not, neither did he eat bread ith them.

And it came to pass on the seventh day, that the child died. And the servants of David feared to tell him that the child as dead: for they said, Behold hile the child as yet alive, e spoke to him, and he ould not hearken to our voice: ho ill he then be grieved, if e tell him that the child is dead?
But hen David sa that his servants hispered, David perceived that the child as dead: therefore David said to his servants, Is the child dead? And they said, He is dead.

Then David arose from the earth, and ashed, and anointed \add himself\add* , and changed his apparel, and came into the house of the LORD, and orshiped: then he came to his on house; and hen he required, they set bread before him, and he ate.

Then said his servants to him, What thing \add is\add* this that thou hast done? thou didst fast and eep for the child, \add hile it as\add* alive; but after the child as dead, thou didst rise and eat bread.
And he said, While the child as yet alive, I fasted, and ept: for I said, Who can tell \add hether\add* God ill be gracious to me, that the child may live?
But no he is dead, Why should I fast? can I bring him back again? I shall go to him, but he ill not return to me.
And David comforted Bath-sheba his ife, and ent in to her, and lay ith her: and she bore a son, and he called his name Solomon: and the LORD loved him.
And he sent by the hand of Nathan the prophet; and he called his name Jedidiah, because of the LORD.
And Joab fought against Rabbah of the children of Ammon, and took the royal city.
And Joab sent messengers to David, and said, I have fought against Rabbah, and have taken the city of aters.
No therefore collect the rest of the people, and encamp against the city, and take it: lest I take the city, and it be called after my name.

And he took their king’s cron from off his head, the eight of hich \add as\add* a talent of gold ith the precious stones: and it as \add set\add* on David’s head. And he brought forth the spoil of the city in great abundance.

And he brought forth the people that \add ere\add* in it, and put \add them\add* under sas, and under harros of iron, and under axes of iron, and made them pass through the brick-kiln: and thus he did to all the cities of the children of Ammon. So David and all the people returned to Jerusalem.
And it came to pass after this, that Absalom the son of David had a fair sister, hose name \add as\add* Tamar; and Amnon the son of David loved her.
And Amnon as so afflicted, that he fell sick for his sister Tamar; for she \add as\add* a virgin; and Amnon thought it hard for him to do any thing to her.
But Amnon had a friend, hose name \add as\add* Jonadab, the son of Shimeah David’s brother: and Jonadab \add as\add* a very subtil man.
And he said to him, Why \add art\add* thou, \add being\add* the king’s son, pining from day to day? ilt thou not tell me? And Amnon said to him, I love Tamar, my brother Absalom’s sister.

And Jonadab said to him, Lay thee don on thy bed, and make thyself sick: and hen thy father cometh to see thee, say to him, I pray thee, let my sister Tamar come, and give me food, and dress the food in my sight, that I may see \add it\add* , and eat \add it\add* at her hand.

So Amnon lay don and made himself sick: and hen the king came to see him, Amnon said to the king, I pray thee, let Tamar my sister come, and make for me a couple of cakes in my sight, that I may eat at her hand.
Then David sent home to Tamar, saying, Go no to thy brother Amnon’s house, and dress meat for him.
So Tamar ent to her brother Amnon’s house; and he as laid don. And she took flour, and kneaded \add it\add* , and made cakes in his sight, and baked the cakes.
And she took a pan, and poured \add them\add* out before him; but he refused to eat. And Amnon said, Have out all men from me. And they ent out every man from him.
And Amnon said to Tamar, Bring the food into the chamber, that I may eat from thy hand. And Tamar took the cakes hich she had made, and brought \add them\add* into the chamber to Amnon her brother.
And hen she had brought \add them\add* to him to eat, he took hold of her, and said to her, Come, lie ith me, my sister.
And she ansered him, Nay, my brother, do not force me; for no such thing ought to be done in Israel: do not thou this folly.
And I, hither shall I cause my shame to go? and as for thee, thou ilt be as one of the fools in Israel. No therefore, I pray thee, speak to the king; for he ill not ithhold me from thee.
Hobeit, he ould not hearken to her voice: but being stronger than she, forced her, and lay ith her.
Then Amnon hated her exceedingly; so that the hatred ith hich he hated her \add as\add* greater than the love ith hich he had loved her. And Amnon said to her, Arise, be gone.
And she said to him, \add There is\add* no cause: this evil in sending me aay \add is\add* greater than the other that thou didst to me. But he ould not hearken to her.
Then he called his servant that ministered to him, and said, Put no this \add oman\add* out from me, and bolt the door after her.

And \add she had\add* a garment of divers colors upon her: for ith such robes ere the king’s daughters \add that ere\add* virgins appareled. Then his servant brought her out, and bolted the door after her.
And Tamar put ashes on her head, and rent her garment of divers colors that \add as\add* on her, and laid her hand on her head, and ent on crying.

And Absalom her brother said to her, Hath Amnon thy brother been ith thee? but hold no thy peace, my sister: he \add is\add* thy brother; regard not this thing. So Tamar remained desolate in her brother Absalom’s house.
But hen king David heard of all these things, he as very roth.
And Absalom spoke to his brother Amnon neither good nor bad: for Absalom hated Amnon, because he had forced his sister Tamar.
And it came to pass after to full years, that Absalom had sheep-shearers in Baal-hazor, hich \add is\add* beside Ephraim: and Absalom invited all the king’s sons.
And Absalom came to the king, and said, Behold no, thy servant hath sheep-shearers; let the king, I beseech thee, and his servants go ith thy servant.
And the king said to Absalom, Nay, my son, let us not all no go, lest e be chargeable to thee. And he pressed him: yet he ould not go, but blessed him.
Then said Absalom, If not, I pray thee, let my brother Amnon go ith us. And the king said to him, Why should he go ith thee?
But Absalom pressed him that he should let Amnon and all the king’s sons go ith him.

No Absalom had commanded his servants, saying, Mark ye no hen Amnon’s heart is merry ith ine, and hen I say to you, Smite Amnon; then kill him, fear not: have I not commanded you? be courageous, and be valiant.
And the servants of Absalom did to Amnon as Absalom had commanded. Then all the king’s sons arose, and every man rode upon his mule, and fled.
And it came to pass, hile they ere in the ay, that information came to David, saying, Absalom hath slain all the king’s sons, and there is not one of them left.
Then the king arose, and tore his garments, and lay on the earth; and all his servants stood by ith their clothes rent.

And Jonadab, the son of Shimeah David’s brother, ansered and said, Let not my lord suppose \add that\add* they have slain all the young men the king’s sons; for Amnon only is dead: for by the appointment of Absalom this hath been determined from the day that he forced his sister Tamar.
No therefore let not my lord the king take the thing to his heart, to think that all the king’s sons are dead: for Amnon only is dead.
But Absalom fled. And the young man that kept the atch lifted up his eyes, and looked, and behold, there came many people by the ay of the hillside behind him.
And Jonadab said to the king, Behold, the king’s sons come; as thy servant said, so it is.
And it came to pass, as soon as he had made an end of speaking, that behold, the king’s sons came, and lifted up their voice and ept: and the king also and all his servants ept exceedingly.
But Absalom fled, and ent to Talmai, the son of Ammihud, king of Geshur. And \add David\add* mourned for his son every day.
So Absalom fled, and ent to Geshur, and as there three years.
And \add the soul of\add* king David longed to go forth to Absalom: for he as comforted concerning Amnon, seeing he as dead.
No Joab the son of Zeruiah perceived that the king’s heart \add as\add* toards Absalom.

And Joab sent to Tekoah, and brought thence a ise oman, and said to her, I pray thee, feign thyself to be a mourner, and put on no mourning apparel, and anoint not thyself ith oil, but be as a oman that had a long time mourned for the dead:
And come to the king, and speak in this manner to him. So Joab put the ords in her mouth.
And hen the oman of Tekoah spoke to the king, she fell on her face to the ground, and did obeisance, and said, Help, O king.
And the king said to her, What aileth thee? And she ansered, I \add am\add* indeed a ido oman, and my husband is dead.
And thy handmaid had to sons, and they to strove together in the field, and \add there as\add* none to part them, but the one smote the other and sle him.

And behold, the hole family hath risen against thy handmaid, and they said, Deliver him that smote his brother, that e may kill him, for the life of his brother hom he sle; and e ill destroy the heir also: and so they ill quench my coal hich is left, and ill not leave to my husband \add neither\add* name nor remainder upon the earth.
And the king said to the oman, Go to thy house, and I ill give charge concerning thee.

And the king said, Whoever saith \add aught\add* to thee, bring him to me, and he shall not touch thee any more.

Then said she, I pray thee, let the king remember the LORD thy God, that thou ouldest not suffer the revengers of blood to destroy any more, lest they destroy my son. And he said, \add As\add* the LORD liveth, there shall not one hair of thy son fall to the earth.
Then the oman said, Let thy handmaid, I pray thee, speak \add one\add* ord to my lord the king. And he said, Say on.
And the oman said, Why then hast thou thought such a thing against the people of God? for the king doth speak this thing as one ho is faulty, in that the king doth not bring home again his banished.

For e must needs die, and \add are\add* as ater spilt on the ground, hich cannot be gathered up again; neither doth God respect \add any\add* person: yet doth he devise means, that his banished be not expelled from him.

No therefore that I have come to speak of this thing to my lord the king, \add it is\add* because the people have made me afraid: and thy handmaid said, I ill no speak to the king; it may be that the king ill perform the request of his handmaid.

Then thy handmaid said, The ord of my lord the king, ill no be comfortable: for as an angel of God, so \add is\add* my lord the king to discern good and bad: therefore the LORD thy God ill be ith thee.
Then the king ansered and said to the oman, Hide not from me, I pray thee, the thing that I shall ask thee. And the oman said, Let my lord the king no speak.

And the king said, \add Is not\add* the hand of Joab ith thee in all this? And the oman ansered and said, \add As\add* thy soul liveth, my lord the king, none can turn to the right hand or to the left from aught that my lord the king hath spoken: for thy servant Joab, he bade me, and he put all these ords in the mouth of thy handmaid:

To bring about this form of speech hath thy servant Joab done this thing: and my lord \add is\add* ise, according to the isdom of an angel of God, to kno all \add things\add* that \add are\add* on the earth.

And Joab fell to the ground on his face, and boed himself, and thanked the king: and Joab said, To-day thy servant knoeth that I have found grace in thy sight, my lord, O king, in that the king hath fulfilled the request of his servant.
So Joab arose and ent to Geshur, and brought Absalom to Jerusalem.

Then Joab arose, and came to Absalom, to \add his\add* house, and said to him, Why have thy servants set my field on fire?

And Absalom ansered Joab, Behold, I sent to thee, saying, Come hither, that I may send thee to the king, to say, Why am I come from Geshur? it \add had been\add* good for me \add had I been\add* there still: no therefore let me see the king’s face; and if there is \add any\add* iniquity in me, let him kill me.
So Joab came to the king, and told him: and hen he had called for Absalom, he came to the king, and boed himself on his face to the ground before the king: and the king kissed Absalom.

And Absalom rose early, and stood beside the ay of the gate: and it as \add so\add* , that hen any man that had a controversy came to the king for judgment, then Absalom called to him, and said, Of hat city \add art\add* thou? And he said, Thy servant \add is\add* one of the tribes of Israel.
And Absalom said to him, See, thy matters \add are\add* good and right; but \add there is\add* no man \add deputed\add* by the king to hear thee.

And it as \add so\add* , that hen any man came nigh \add to him\add* to do him obeisance, he put forth his hand, and took him, and kissed him.
And in this manner did Absalom to all Israel that came to the king for judgment: so Absalom stole the hearts of the men of Israel.
And it came to pass after forty years, that Absalom said to the king, I pray thee, let me go and pay my vo, hich I have voed to the LORD, in Hebron.
For thy servant voed a vo hile I abode at Geshur in Syria, saying, If the LORD shall bring me again indeed to Jerusalem, then I ill serve the LORD.
And the king said to him, Go in peace, So he arose, and ent to Hebron.
But Absalom sent spies throughout all the tribes of Israel, saying, As soon as ye hear the sound of the trumpet, then ye shall say, Absalom reigneth in Hebron.
And ith Absalom ent to hundred men from Jerusalem, \add that ere\add* called; and they ent in their simplicity, and they kne not any thing.

And David said to all his servants that \add ere\add* ith him at Jerusalem, Arise, and let us flee; for e shall not \add else\add* escape from Absalom: make speed to depart, lest he should overtake us suddenly, and bring evil upon us, and smite the city ith the edge of the sord.
And the king’s servants said to the king, Behold, thy servants \add are ready to do\add* hatever my lord the king shall appoint.
And the king ent forth, and all his household after him. And the king left ten omen \add ho ere\add* concubines to keep the house.
And the king ent forth, and all the people after him, and tarried in a place that as far off.
And all his servants passed on by his side; and all the Cherethites, and all the Pelethites, and all the Gittites, six hundred men ho came after him from Gath, passed on before the king.
Then said the king to Ittai the Gittite, Why goest thou also ith us? return to thy place, and abide ith the king; for thou \add art\add* a stranger, and also an exile.

Whereas thou camest \add but\add* yesterday, should I this day make thee go up and don ith us? seeing I go hither I may; return thou, and take back thy brethren: mercy and truth \add be\add* ith thee.

And Ittai ansered the king, and said, \add As\add* the LORD liveth, and \add as\add* my lord the king liveth, surely in hat place my lord the king shall be, hether in death or life, even there also ill thy servant be.
And David said to Ittai, Go and pass over. And Ittai the Gittite passed over, and all his men, and all the little ones that \add ere\add* ith him.
And all the country ept ith a loud voice, and all the people passed over: the king also himself passed over the brook Kidron, and all the people passed over, toards the ay of the ilderness.

And lo, Zadok also, and all the Levites \add ere\add* ith him bearing the ark of the covenant of God: and they set don the ark of God; and Abiathar ent up, until all the people had done passing out of the city.
And the king said to Zadok, Carry back the ark of God into the city: if I shall find favor in the eyes of the LORD, he ill bring me again, and sho me \add both\add* it, and his habitation:
But if he shall thus say, I have no delight in thee; behold, \add here am\add* I, let him do to me as seemeth good to him.

See, I ill tarry in the plain of the ilderness, until ord shall come from you to certify me.
Zadok therefore and Abiathar carried the ark of God again to Jerusalem: and they tarried there.

And David ent up by the ascent of \add mount\add* Olivet, and ept as he ent, and had his head covered, and he ent barefoot: and all the people that \add ere\add* ith him covered every man his head, and they ent up, eeping as they ent.
And \add one\add* told David, saying, Ahithophel \add is\add* among the conspirators ith Absalom. And David said, O LORD, I pray thee, turn the counsel of Ahithophel into foolishness.

And it came to pass, that \add hen\add* David had come to the top \add of the mount\add* , here he orshiped God, behold, Hushai the Archite came to meet him ith his coat rent, and earth upon his head;
To hom David said, If thou shalt pass on ith me, then thou ilt be a burden to me:

But if thou shalt return to the city, and say to Absalom, I ill be thy servant, O king; \add as\add* I \add have been\add* thy father’s servant hitherto, so \add ill\add* I no also \add be\add* thy servant: then mayest thou for me defeat the counsel of Ahithophel.

And \add hast thou\add* not there ith thee Zadok and Abiathar the priests? therefore it shall be, \add that\add* hatever thing thou shalt hear out of the king’s house, thou shalt tell \add it\add* to Zadok and Abiathar the priests.
Behold, \add they have\add* there ith them their to sons, Ahimaaz Zadok’s \add son\add* , and Jonathan Abiathar’s \add son\add* ; and by them ye shall send to me every thing that ye can hear.
So Hushai David’s friend came into the city, and Absalom came into Jerusalem.

And hen David as a little past the top \add of the hill\add* , behold, Ziba the servant of Mephibosheth met him, ith a couple of asses saddled, and upon them to hundred \add loaves\add* of bread, and a hundred bunches of raisins, and a hundred of summer fruits, and a bottle of ine.

And the king said to Ziba, What meanest thou by these? And Ziba said, The asses \add are\add* for the king’s household to ride on; and the bread and summer fruit for the young men to eat; and the ine, that such as are faint in the ilderness may drink.

And the king said, And here \add is\add* thy master’s son? And Ziba said to the king, Behold, he abideth at Jerusalem: for he said, To-day shall the house of Israel restore to me the kingdom of my father.

Then said the king to Ziba, Behold, thine \add are\add* all that \add pertained\add* to Mephibosheth. And Ziba said, I humbly beseech thee \add that\add* I may find grace in thy sight, my lord, O king.
And hen king David came to Bahurim, behold, thence came out a man of the family of the house of Saul, hose name \add as\add* Shimei, the son of Gera: he came forth, and cursed still as he came.
And he cast stones at David, and at all the servants of king David: and all the people and all the mighty men \add ere\add* on his right hand and on his left.
And thus said Shimei hen he cursed, Come out, come out, thou bloody man, and thou man of Belial:

The LORD hath returned upon thee all the blood of the house of Saul, in hose stead thou hast reigned; and the LORD hath delivered the kingdom into the hand of Absalom thy son: and behold, thou \add art taken\add* in thy mischief, because thou \add art\add* a bloody man.
Then said Abishai the son of Zeruiah to the king, Why should this dead dog curse my lord the king? let me go over, I pray thee, and take off his head.
And the king said, What have I to do ith you, ye sons of Zeruiah? so let him curse, because the LORD hath said to him, Curse David. Who shall then say, Why hast thou done so?

She is like the merchant’s ships; she bringeth her food from afar.
She riseth also hile it is yet night, and giveth food to her household, and a portion to her maidens.
She considereth a field, and buyeth it: ith the fruit of her hands she planteth a vineyard.
She girdeth her loins ith strength, and strengtheneth her arms.
She perceiveth that her merchandise \add is\add* good: her candle goeth not out by night.
She layeth her hands to the spindle, and her hands hold the distaff.
She stretcheth out her hand to the poor; yes, she reacheth forth her hands to the needy.
She is not afraid of the sno for her household: for all her household \add are\add* clothed ith scarlet.
She maketh herself coverings of tapestry; her clothing \add is\add* silk and purple.
Her husband is knon in the gates, hen he sitteth among the elders of the land.
She maketh fine linen, and selleth \add it\add* ; and delivereth girdles to the merchant.
Strength and honor \add are\add* her clothing; and she shall rejoice in time to come.
She openeth her mouth ith isdom; and on her tongue \add is\add* the la of kindness.
She looketh ell to the ays of her household, and eateth not the bread of idleness.
Her children rise up, and call her blessed; her husband \add also\add* , and he praiseth her.
Many daughters have done virtuously, but thou excellest them all.
Favor \add is\add* deceitful, and beauty \add is\add* vain: \add but\add* a oman \add that\add* feareth the LORD, she shall be praised.
Give her of the fruit of her hands; and let her on orks praise her in the gates.
The ords of the preacher, the son of David, king of Jerusalem.
Vanity of vanities, saith the preacher, vanity of vanities; all \add is\add* vanity.
What profit hath a man of all his labor, hich he taketh under the sun?
\add One\add* generation passeth aay, and \add another\add* generation cometh: but the earth abideth for ever.
The sun also riseth, and the sun goeth don, and hasteth to his place here he arose.
The ind goeth toards the south, and turneth about to the north; it hirleth about continually, and the ind returneth again according to its circuits.
All the rivers run into the sea; yet the sea \add is\add* not full; to the place from hence the rivers come, thither they return again.
All things \add are\add* full of labor; man cannot utter \add it\add* : the eye is not satisfied ith seeing, nor the ear filled ith hearing.
The thing that hath been, it \add is that\add* hich shall be; and that hich is done \add is\add* that hich shall be done: and \add there is\add* no ne \add thing\add* under the sun.
Is there \add any\add* thing of hich it may be said, See, this \add is\add* ne? it hath been already of old time, hich as before us.
\add There is\add* no remembrance of former \add things\add* ; neither shall there be \add any\add* remembrance of \add things\add* that are to come ith \add those\add* that shall come after.
I the preacher as king over Israel in Jerusalem.
And I gave my heart to seek and search out by isdom concerning all \add things\add* that are done under heaven: this grievous labor hath God given to the sons of man to be exercised ith it.

\add That hich is\add* crooked cannot be made straight: and that hich is anting cannot be numbered.

I communed ith my on heart, saying, Lo, I have come to great estate, and have gained more isdom than all \add they\add* that have been before me in Jerusalem: and my heart had great experience of isdom and knoledge.

For in much isdom \add is\add* much grief: and he that increaseth knoledge increaseth sorro.
I said in my heart, Come no, I ill prove thee ith mirth, therefore enjoy pleasure: and behold, this also \add is\add* vanity.
I said of laughter, \add It is\add* mad: and of mirth, What doeth it?

I sought in my heart, to give myself to ine, yet acquainting my heart ith isdom; and to lay hold on folly, till I might see hat \add as\add* that good for the sons of men, hich they should do under the heaven all the days of their life.
I made me great orks; I built me houses; I planted me vineyards:
I made me gardens and orchards, and I planted trees in them of all \add kind of\add* fruits:
I made me pools of ater, to ater ith them the ood that bringeth forth trees:
I procured \add me\add* servants and maidens, and had servants born in my house; also I had great possessions of great and small cattle above all that ere in Jerusalem before me:

I gathered me also silver and gold, and the peculiar treasure of kings, and of the provinces: I procured me men-singers and omen-singers, and the delights of the sons of men, \add as\add* musical instruments, and of all sorts.
So I as great, and increased more than all that ere before me in Jerusalem: also my isdom remained ith me.
And hatever my eyes desired I kept not from them, I ithheld not my heart from any joy; for my heart rejoiced in all my labor: and this as my portion of all my labor.

Then I looked on all the orks that my hands had rought, and on the labor that I had labored to do: and behold, all \add as\add* vanity and vexation of spirit, and \add there as\add* no profit under the sun.
And I turned myself to behold isdom, and madness, and folly: for hat \add can\add* the man \add do\add* that cometh after the king? \add even\add* that hich hath been already done.
Then I sa that isdom excelleth folly, as far as light excelleth darkness.
The ise man’s eyes \add are\add* in his head; but the fool alketh in darkness: and I myself perceived also that one event happeneth to them all.
Then said I in my heart, As it happeneth to the fool, so it happeneth even to me; and hy as I then more ise? Then I said in my heart, that this also \add is\add* vanity.

For \add there is\add* no remembrance of the ise more than of the fool for ever; seeing that hich no \add is\add* in the days to come shall all be forgotten. And ho dieth the ise \add man\add* ? as the fool.
Therefore I hated life; because the ork that is rought under the sun \add is\add* grievous to me: for all \add is\add* vanity and vexation of spirit.
Yes, I hated all my labor hich I had taken under the sun: because I should leave it to the man that shall be after me.

And ho knoeth hether he shall be a ise \add man\add* or a fool? yet shall he have rule over all my labor in hich I have labored, and in hich I have shoed myself ise under the sun. This \add is\add* also vanity.
Therefore I ent about to cause my heart to despair of all the labor hich I took under the sun.

For there is a man hose labor is in isdom, and in knoledge, and in equity; yet to a man that hath not labored in it, shall he leave it \add for\add* his portion. This also \add is\add* vanity and a great evil.
For hat hath man of all his labor, and of the vexation of his heart, in hich he hath labored under the sun?

\add There is\add* nothing better for a man than that he should eat and drink, and \add that\add* he should make his soul enjoy good in his labor. This also I sa, that it \add as\add* from the hand of God.
For ho can eat, or ho else can hasten \add to it\add* more than I?

For \add God\add* giveth to a man ho \add is\add* good in his sight, isdom, and knoledge, and joy: but to the sinner he giveth toil, to gather, and to amass, that he may give to \add him that is\add* good before God. This also \add is\add* vanity and vexation of spirit.
To every \add thing there is\add* a season, and a time to every purpose under the heaven:
A time to be born, and a time to die; a time to plant, and a time to pluck up \add that hich is\add* planted;
A time to kill, and a time to heal; a time to break don, and a time to build up;
A time to eep, and a time to laugh; a time to mourn, and a time to dance;
A time to cast aay stones, and a time to gather stones; a time to embrace, and a time to refrain from embracing;
A time to get, and a time to lose; a time to keep, and a time to cast aay;
A time to rend, and a time to se; a time to keep silence, and a time to speak;
A time to love, and a time to hate; a time of ar, and a time of peace.
What profit hath he that orketh in that in hich he laboreth?
I have seen the labor, hich God hath given to the sons of men to be exercised in it.
He hath made every \add thing\add* beautiful in its time: also he hath set the orld in their heart, so that no man can find out the ork that God maketh from the beginning to the end.
I kno that \add there is\add* no good in them, but for \add a man\add* to rejoice, and to do good in his life.
And also that every man should eat and drink, and enjoy the good of all his labor, it \add is\add* the gift of God.
I kno that, hatever God doeth, it shall be for ever: nothing can be added to it, nor any thing taken from it: and God doeth \add it\add* , that \add men\add* should fear before him.
That hich hath been is no; and that hich is to be hath already been; and God requireth that hich is past.
And moreover I sa under the sun the place of judgment, \add that\add* ickedness \add as\add* there; and the place of righteousness, \add that\add* iniquity \add as\add* there.
I said in my heart, God ill judge the righteous and the icked: for \add there is\add* a time there for every purpose and for every ork.
I said in my heart concerning the state of the sons of men, that God might manifest them, and that they might see that they themselves are beasts.

For that hich befalleth the sons of men befalleth beasts; even one thing befalleth them: as the one dieth, so dieth the other; yes, they have all one breath; so that a man hath no pre-eminence above a beast: for all \add is\add* vanity.
All go to one place; all are of the dust, and all turn to dust again.
Who knoeth the spirit of man that goeth upard, and the spirit of the beast that goeth donard to the earth?
Wherefore I perceive that \add there is\add* nothing better, than that a man should rejoice in his on orks; for that \add is\add* his portion: for ho shall bring him to see hat shall be after him?

So I returned, and considered all the oppressions that are done under the sun: and behold the tears of \add such as ere\add* oppressed, and they had no comforter; and on the side of their oppressors \add there as\add* poer; but they had no comforter.
Wherefore I praised the dead ho are already dead more than the living ho are yet alive.
Yes, better is \add he\add* than both they, ho hath not yet been, ho hath not seen the evil ork that is done under the sun.
Again, I considered all labor, and every right ork, that for this a man is envied by his neighbor. This \add is\add* also vanity and vexation of spirit.
The fool foldeth his hands together, and eateth his on flesh.
Better \add is\add* a handful \add ith\add* quietness, than both the hands full \add ith\add* toil and vexation of spirit.
Then I returned, and I sa vanity under the sun.

There is one \add alone\add* , and \add there is\add* not a second; yes, he hath neither child nor brother: yet \add is there\add* no end of all his labor; neither is his eye satisfied ith riches; neither \add saith he\add* , For hom do I labor, and bereave my soul of good? This \add is\add* also vanity, yes, it \add is\add* a grievous labor.
To \add are\add* better than one; because they have a good reard for their labor.
For if they fall, the one ill lift up his fello: but oe to him \add that is\add* alone hen he falleth; for \add he hath\add* not another to help him to rise.
Again, if to lie together, then they have heat: but ho can one be arm \add alone\add* ?
And if one prevaileth against him, to shall ithstand him; and a three-fold cord is not quickly broken.
Better \add is\add* a poor and a ise child, than an old and foolish king, ho ill no more be admonished.

I considered all the living ho alk under the sun, ith the second child that shall stand up in his stead.

\add There is\add* no end of all the people, \add even\add* of all that have been before them: they also that come after shall not rejoice in him. Surely this also \add is\add* vanity and vexation of spirit.
Keep thy foot hen thou goest to the house of God, and be more ready to hear, than to give the sacrifice of fools: for they consider not that they do evil.
Be not rash ith thy mouth, and let not thy heart be hasty to utter \add any\add* thing before God: for God \add is\add* in heaven, and thou upon earth: therefore let thy ords be fe.
For a dream cometh through the multitude of business; and a fool’s voice \add is knon\add* by a multitude of ords.

If thou seest the oppression of the poor, and violent perversion of judgment and justice in a province, onder not at the matter: for \add he that is\add* higher than the highest regardeth; and \add there are\add* higher than they.

When goods increase, they are increased that eat them: and hat good \add is there\add* to the oners of them, saving the beholding \add of them\add* ith their eyes?

There is a grievous evil \add hich\add* I have seen under the sun, \add namely\add* , riches kept for the oners of them to their hurt.
But those riches perish by evil labor: and he begetteth a son, and \add there is\add* nothing in his hand.

Behold \add that\add* hich I have seen: \add it is\add* good and comely \add for one\add* to eat and to drink, and to enjoy the good of all his labor that he taketh under the sun all the days of his life, hich God giveth him: for it \add is\add* his portion.
Every man also to hom God hath given riches and ealth, and hath given him poer to eat of it, and to take his portion, and to rejoice in his labor; this \add is\add* the gift of God.
For he shall not much remember the days of his life; because God ansereth \add him\add* in the joy of his heart.
There is an evil hich I have seen under the sun, and it \add is\add* common among men:

A man to hom God hath given riches, ealth, and honor, so that he anteth nothing for his soul of all that he desireth, yet God giveth him not poer to eat of it, but a stranger eateth it: this \add is\add* vanity, and it \add is\add* an evil disease.

If a man begetteth a hundred \add children\add* , and liveth many years, so that the days of his years are many, and his soul is not filled ith good, and also \add that\add* he hath no burial; I say, \add that\add* an untimely birth \add is\add* better than he.

For hat hath the ise more than the fool? hat hath the poor, that knoeth to alk before the living?
Better \add is\add* the sight of the eyes than the andering of the desire: this \add is\add* also vanity and vexation of spirit.
That hich hath been is named already, and it is knon that it \add is\add* man: neither may he contend ith him that is mightier than he.
Seeing there are many things that increase vanity, hat \add is\add* man the better?
For ho knoeth hat \add is\add* good for man in \add this\add* life, all the days of his vain life hich he spendeth as a shado? for ho can tell a man hat shall be after him under the sun?
A good name \add is\add* better than precious ointment; and the day of death than the day of one’s birth.
\add It is\add* better to go to the house of mourning, than to go to the house of feasting: for that \add is\add* the end of all men; and the living ill lay \add it\add* to his heart.
Sorro \add is\add* better than laughter: for by the sadness of the countenance the heart is made better.
The heart of the ise \add is\add* in the house of mourning; but the heart of fools \add is\add* in the house of mirth.
\add It is\add* better to hear the rebuke of the ise, than for a man to hear the song of fools.
For as the crackling of thorns under a pot, so \add is\add* the laughter of the fool: this also \add is\add* vanity.
Surely oppression maketh a ise man mad; and a gift destroyeth the heart.
Better \add is\add* the end of a thing than its beginning: \add and\add* the patient in spirit \add is\add* better than the proud in spirit.
Be not hasty in thy spirit to be angry: for anger resteth in the bosom of fools.
Say not thou, What is \add the cause\add* that the former days ere better than these? for thou dost not inquire isely concerning this.
Wisdom \add is\add* good ith an inheritance: and \add by it there is\add* profit to them that see the sun.
For isdom \add is\add* a defense, \add and\add* money \add is\add* a defense: but the excellence of knoledge \add is\add* , \add that\add* isdom giveth life to them that have it.
Consider the ork of God: for ho can make \add that\add* straight, hich he hath made crooked?
In the day of prosperity be joyful, but in the day of adversity consider: God also hath set the one over against the other, to the end that man should find nothing after him.

All \add things\add* have I seen in the days of my vanity: there is a just \add man\add* that perisheth in his righteousness, and there is a icked \add man\add* that prolongeth \add his life\add* in his ickedness.
Be not righteous over much; neither make thyself over ise: hy shouldst thou destroy thyself?
Be not over much icked, neither be thou foolish: hy shouldst thou die before thy time?
\add It is\add* good that thou shouldst take hold of this; yes, also from this ithdra not thy hand: for he that feareth God shall escape from them all.
Wisdom strengtheneth the ise more than ten mighty \add men\add* ho are in the city.
For \add there is\add* not a just man upon earth, that doeth good, and sinneth not.
Also take no heed to all ords that are spoken; lest thou hear thy servant curse thee:
For often also thy on heart knoeth that thou thyself likeise hast cursed others.
All this have I proved by isdom: I said, I ill be ise; but it \add as\add* far from me.
That hich is far off, and exceedingly deep, ho can find it out?
I applied my heart to kno, and to search, and to seek out isdom, and the reason \add of things\add* , and to kno the ickedness of folly, even of foolishness \add and\add* madness:

And I find more bitter than death the oman hose heart \add is\add* snares and nets, \add and\add* her hands \add as\add* bands: hoever pleaseth God shall escape from her; but the sinner shall be taken by her.
Behold, this have I found, saith the preacher, \add counting\add* one by one, to find out the account:
Which yet my soul seeketh, but I find not: one man among a thousand have I found; but a oman among all those have I not found.
Lo, this only have I found, that God hath made man upright; but they have sought out many inventions.
Who \add is\add* as the ise \add man\add* ? and ho knoeth the interpretation of a thing? a man’s isdom maketh his face to shine, and the boldness of his face shall be changed.
I \add counsel thee\add* to keep the king’s commandment, and \add that\add* in regard of the oath of God.
Be not hasty to go out of his sight: stand not in an evil thing; for he doeth hatever pleaseth him.
Where the ord of a king \add is\add* , \add there is\add* poer: and ho may say to him, hat doest thou?
He ho keepeth the commandment shall feel no evil thing: and a ise man’s heart discerneth both time and judgment.
Because to every purpose there is time and judgment, therefore the misery of man \add is\add* great upon him.
For he knoeth not that hich shall be: for ho can tell him hen it shall be?

\add There is\add* no man that hath poer over the spirit to retain the spirit; neither \add hath he\add* poer in the day of death: and \add there is\add* no discharge in \add that\add* ar; neither shall ickedness deliver those that are given to it.
All this have I seen, and applied my heart to every ork that is done under the sun: \add there is\add* a time in hich one man ruleth over another to his on hurt.
And so I sa the icked buried, ho had come and gone from the place of the holy, and they ere forgotten in the city here they had so done: this \add is\add* also vanity.
Because sentence against an evil ork is not executed speedily, therefore the heart of the sons of men is fully set in them to do evil.
Though a sinner doeth evil a hundred times, and his \add days\add* are prolonged, yet surely I kno that it ill be ell ith them that fear God, ho fear before him:
But it ill not be ell ith the icked, neither ill he prolong \add his\add* days, \add hich are\add* as a shado; because he feareth not before God.

There is a vanity hich is done upon the earth; that there are just \add men\add* , to hom it happeneth according to the ork of the icked; again, there are icked \add men\add* , to hom it happeneth according to the ork of the righteous: I said that this also \add is\add* vanity.

Then I commended mirth, because a man hath no better thing under the sun, than to eat, and to drink, and to be merry: for that shall abide ith him of his labor the days of his life, hich God giveth him under the sun.
When I applied my heart to kno isdom, and to see the business that is done upon the earth: (for also \add there is that\add* neither day nor night seeth sleep ith his eyes:)

Then I beheld all the ork of God, that a man cannot find out the ork that is done under the sun: because though a man may labor to seek \add it\add* out, yet he shall not find \add it\add* ; yes further; though a ise \add man\add* thinketh to kno \add it\add* , yet shall he not be able to find \add it\add* .

For all this I considered in my heart even to declare all this, that the righteous, and the ise, and their orks, \add are\add* in the hand of God: no man knoeth either love or hatred \add by\add* all \add that is\add* before them.

All \add things come\add* alike to all: \add there is\add* one event to the righteous, and to the icked; to the good and to the clean, and to the unclean; to him that sacrificeth, and to him that sacrificeth not: as \add is\add* the good, so \add is\add* the sinner; \add and\add* he that seareth, as \add he\add* that feareth an oath.

This \add is\add* an evil among all \add things\add* that are done under the sun, that \add there is\add* one event to all: yes, also the heart of the sons of men is full of evil, and madness \add is\add* in their heart hile they live, and after that \add they go\add* to the dead.
For to him that is joined to all the living there is hope: for a living dog is better than a dead lion.
For the living kno that they shall die: but the dead kno not any thing, neither have they any more a reard; for the memory of them is forgotten.
Also their love, and their hatred, and their envy, hath no perished; neither have they any more a portion for ever in any \add thing\add* that is done under the sun.
Go thy ay, eat thy bread ith joy, and drink thy ine ith a merry heart; for God no accepteth thy orks.
Let thy garments be alays hite; and let thy head lack no ointment.

Live joyfully ith the ife hom thou lovest all the days of the life of thy vanity, hich he hath given thee under the sun, all the days of thy vanity: for that \add is\add* thy portion in \add this\add* life, and in thy labor hich thou takest under the sun.
Whatever thy hand findeth to do, do \add it\add* ith thy might; for \add there is\add* no ork, nor device, nor knoledge, nor isdom, in the grave, hither thou goest.

I returned, and sa under the sun, that the race is not to the sift, nor the battle to the strong, neither yet bread to the ise, nor yet riches to men of understanding, nor yet favor to men of skill; but time and chance happeneth to them all.

For man also knoeth not his time: as the fishes that are taken in an evil net, and as the birds that are caught in the snare; so \add are\add* the sons of men snared in an evil time, hen it falleth suddenly upon them.
This isdom have I seen also under the sun, and it \add seemed\add* to me great:
\add There as\add* a little city, and fe men ithin it; and there came a great king against it, and besieged it, and built great bularks against it:
No there as found in it a poor ise man, and he by his isdom delivered the city; yet no man remembered that same poor man.
Then said I, isdom \add is\add* better than strength: nevertheless the poor man’s isdom \add is\add* despised, and his ords are not heard.
The ords of ise \add men are\add* heard in quiet more than the cry of him that ruleth among fools.
Wisdom \add is\add* better than eapons of ar: but one sinner destroyeth much good.
Dead flies cause the ointment of the apothecary to send forth an offensive odor: \add so doth\add* a little folly him that is in reputation for isdom \add and\add* honor.
A ise man’s heart \add is\add* at his right hand; but a fool’s heart \add is\add* at his left.
Also, hen he that is a fool alketh by the ay, his isdom faileth \add him\add* , and he saith to every one \add that\add* he \add is\add* a fool.
If the spirit of the ruler riseth against thee, leave not thy place; for yielding pacifieth great offenses.
There is an evil \add hich\add* I have seen under the sun, as an error \add hich\add* proceedeth from the ruler:
Folly is set in great dignity, and the rich sit in lo place.
I have seen servants upon horses, and princes alking as servants upon the earth.
He that diggeth a pit shall fall into it; and hoever breaketh a hedge, a serpent shall bite him.
Whoever removeth stones shall be hurt by them; \add and\add* he that cleaveth ood shall be endangered by it.
If the iron is blunt, and he doth not het the edge, then must he use more strength: but isdom \add is\add* profitable to direct.
Surely the serpent ill bite ithout enchantment; and a babbler is no better.
The ords of a ise man’s mouth \add are\add* gracious; but the lips of a fool ill sallo up himself.

\add Ye\add* hypocrites, ell did Isaiah prophesy of you, saying,

Where their orm dieth not, and the fire is not quenched.

And brought them out, and said, Sirs, hat must I do to be saved?
And they said, Believe on the Lord Jesus Christ, and thou shalt be saved, and thy house.
And they spoke to him the ord of the Lord, and to all that ere in his house.
And he took them the same hour of the night, and ashed \add their\add* stripes; and as baptized, he and all his, ithout delay.
And hen he had brought them into his house, he set food before them, and rejoiced, believing in God ith all his house.
And hen it as day, the magistrates sent the sergeants, saying, Let those men go.

But Paul said to them, They have beaten us openly uncondemned, being Romans, and have cast \add us\add* into prison; and no do they thrust us out privately? no verily; but let them come themselves and bring us out.
And the sergeants told these ords to the magistrates: and they feared hen they heard that they ere Romans.
And they came and besought them, and brought \add them\add* out, and desired \add them\add* to depart out of the city.
And they ent out of the prison, and entered into \add the house of\add* Lydia: and hen they had seen the brethren, they comforted them, and departed.
No hen they had passed through Amphipolis, and Apollonia, they came to Thessalonica, here as a synagogue of the Jes.
And Paul, as his manner as, ent in to them, and on three sabbaths reasoned ith them out of the scriptures,
Opening and alledging, that it as needful that Christ should suffer, and rise again from the dead; and that this Jesus, hom I preach to you, is Christ.

But the Jes ho believed not, moved ith envy, took to them certain vile fellos of the baser sort, and gathered a company, and set all the city in an uproar, and assaulted the house of Jason, and sought to bring them out to the people.

Whom Jason hath received: and these all do contrary to the decrees of Cesar, saying, That there is another king, \add one\add* Jesus.

No, hile Paul aited for them at Athens, his spirit as stirred in him, hen he sa the city holly given to idolatry.

Then certain philosophers of the Epicureans, and of the Stoics, encountered him. And some said, What ill this babbler say? some others, He seemeth to be a setter-forth of strange gods: because he preached to them Jesus, and the resurrection.
And they took him, and brought him to Areopagus, saying, May e kno hat this ne doctrine \add is\add* , of hich thou speakest?
For thou bringest certain strange things to our ears; e ould kno therefore hat these things mean.
(For all the Athenians and strangers ho ere there, spent their time in nothing else, but either to tell, or to hear some ne thing.)
Then Paul stood in the midst of Mars-hill, and said, \add Ye\add* men of Athens, I perceive that in all things ye are too superstitious.
For as I passed by, and beheld your devotions, I found an altar ith this inscription, TO THE UNKNOWN GOD. Whom therefore ye ignorantly orship, him declare I to you.
God that made the orld, and all things therein, seeing that he is Lord of heaven and earth, delleth not in temples made ith hands;
Neither is orshiped ith men’s hands, as though he needed any thing, seeing he giveth to all life, and breath, and all things;
And hath made of one blood all nations of men to dell on all the face of the earth, and hath determined the times before appointed, and the bounds of their habitation;
That they should seek the Lord, if haply they might feel after him, and find him, though he is not far from every one of us:
For in him e live, and move, and have our being; as certain also of your on poets have said, for e are also his offspring.
Being then the offspring of God, e ought not to think that the Godhead is like to gold, or silver, or stone graven by art and man’s device.
And the times of this ignorance God inked at; but no commandeth all men every here to repent:

Because he hath appointed a day, in hich he ill judge the orld in righteousness, by \add that\add* man hom he hath ordained: \add of hich\add* he hath given assurance to all \add men\add* , in that he hath raised him from the dead.
And hen they heard of the resurrection of the dead, some mocked: and others said, We ill hear thee again concerning this \add matter\add* .
So Paul departed from among them.
But certain men adhered to him, and believed: among hom \add as\add* Dionysius the Areopagite, and a oman named Damaris, and others ith them.
After these things, Paul departed from Athens, and came to Corinth;
And found a certain Je named Aquila, born in Pontus, lately come from Italy, ith his ife Priscilla (because that Claudius had commanded all Jes to depart from Rome) and \add he\add* came to them.
And because he as of the same occupation, he abode ith them, and rought (for by their occupation they ere tent-makers)
And he reasoned in the synagogue every sabbath, and persuaded the Jes and the Greeks.
And hen Silas and Timothy had come from Macedonia, Paul as pressed in spirit, and testified to the Jes, \add that\add* Jesus \add as\add* Christ.

And hen they opposed themselves, and blasphemed, he shook \add his\add* raiment, and said to them, Your blood \add be\add* upon your on heads: I \add am\add* clean: from henceforth I ill go to the Gentiles.
And he departed thence, and entered into the house of a certain man named Justus, \add one\add* that orshiped God, hose house joined close to the synagogue.
And Crispus the chief ruler of the synagogue believed on the Lord ith all his house: and many of the Corinthians hearing, believed, and ere baptized.
Then the Lord spoke to Paul in the night by a vision, Be not afraid, but speak, and hold not thy peace:
For I am ith thee, and no man shall lay hands on thee, to hurt thee: for I have many people in this city.
And he continued \add there\add* a year and six months, teaching the ord of God among them.
And hen Gallio as the deputy of Achaia, the Jes made insurrection ith one accord against Paul, and brought him to the judgment-seat,
Saying, This \add man\add* persuadeth men to orship God contrary to the la.
And hen Paul as no about to open \add his\add* mouth, Gallio said to the Jes, If it ere a matter of rong, or hainous crime, O \add ye\add* Jes, reason ould that I should bear ith you:
But if it is a question of ords and names, and \add of\add* your la, look ye \add to it\add* : for I ill be no judge of such \add matters\add* .
And he drove them from the judgment-seat.
Then all the Greeks took Sosthenes, the chief ruler of the synagogue, and beat \add him\add* before the judgment-seat. And Gallio cared for none of those things.

And Paul \add after this\add* tarried \add there\add* yet a good hile, and took his leave of the brethren, and sailed thence into Syria, and ith him Priscilla and Aquila; having shorn \add his\add* head in Cenchrea: for he had a vo.
And he came to Ephesus, and left them there: but he himself entered into the synagogue, and reasoned ith the Jes.
When they desired \add him\add* to tarry longer time ith them, he consented not:
But bade them fareell, saying, I must by all means keep this feast that cometh in Jerusalem: but I ill return to you, if God ill. And he sailed from Ephesus.
And hen he had landed at Cesarea, and gone up and saluted the church, he ent don to Antioch.
And after he had spent some time \add there\add* , he departed and ent over \add all\add* the country of Galatia and Phrygia in order, strengthening all the disciples.
And a certain Je named Apollos, born at Alexandria, an eloquent man, \add and\add* mighty in the scriptures, came to Ephesus.
This man as instructed in the ay of the Lord: and being fervent in the spirit, he spoke and taught diligently the things of the Lord, knoing only the baptism of John.
And he began to speak boldly in the synagogue: Whom, hen Aquila and Priscilla had heard, they took him to \add them\add* , and expounded to him the ay of God more perfectly.
And hen he as disposed to pass into Achaia, the brethren rote, exhorting the disciples to receive him: ho, hen he had come, helped them much ho had believed through grace.

And it came to pass, that hile Apollos as at Corinth, Paul having passed through the upper region, came to Ephesus; and finding certain disciples,
He said to them, Have ye received the Holy Spirit since ye believed? And they said to him, We have not so much as heard hether there is any Holy Spirit.
And he said to them, Into hat then ere ye baptized? And they said, Into John’s baptism.
Then said Paul, John verily baptized ith the baptism of repentance, saying to the people, That they should believe on him ho should come after him, that is, on Christ Jesus.
When they heard \add this\add* , they ere baptized into the name of the Lord Jesus.
And hen Paul had laid \add his\add* hands upon them, the Holy Spirit came on them; and they spoke in languages, and prophesied.
And all the men ere about telve.
And he ent into the synagogue, and spoke boldly for the space of three months, disputing and persuading the things concerning the kingdom of God.
But hen divers ere hardened, and believed not, but spoke evil of that ay before the multitude, he departed from them, and separated the disciples, disputing daily in the school of one Tyrannus.

And God rought special miracles by the hands of Paul:
So that from his body ere brought to the sick, handkerchiefs, or aprons, and the diseases departed from them, and the evil spirits ent out of them.

After these things ere ended, Paul purposed in the spirit, hen he had passed through Macedonia, and Achaia, to go to Jerusalem, saying, After I have been there, I must also see Rome.

For a certain \add man\add* named Demetrius, a silver-smith, ho made silver shrines for Diana, brought no small gain to the artificers;
Whom he called together ith the orkmen of like occupation, and said, Sirs, ye kno that by this craft e have our ealth:

So that not only this our craft is in danger to be set at naught; but also that the temple of the great goddess Diana should be despised, and her magnificence should be destroyed, hom all Asia, and the orld orshipeth.
And hen they heard \add these sayings\add* , they ere full of rath, and cried out, saying, Great \add is\add* Diana of the Ephesians.

And hen the ton-clerk had appeased the people, he said, \add Ye\add* men of Ephesus, hat man is there that knoeth not that the city of the Ephesians is a orshiper of the great goddess Diana, and of the \add image\add* hich fell don from Jupiter?
Seeing then that these things cannot be contradicted, ye ought to be quiet, and to do nothing rashly.
For ye have brought hither these men, ho are neither robbers of churches, nor yet blasphemers of your goddess.
Wherefore, if Demetrius and the artificers ho are ith him, have a matter against any man, the la is open, and there are deputies: let them implead one another.
But if ye inquire any thing concerning other matters, it shall be determined in a laful assembly.

And hen he had thus spoken, he dismissed the assembly.
And after the uproar had ceased, Paul called to \add him\add* the disciples, and embraced \add them\add* , and departed to go into Macedonia.
And hen he had gone over those parts, and had given them much exhortation, he came into Greece,
And \add there\add* abode three months. And hen the Jes laid ait for him, as he as about to sail into Syria, he purposed to return through Macedonia.
And there accompanied him into Asia Sopater of Berea; and of the Thessalonians, Aristarchus and Secundus; and Gaius of Derbe, and Timothy; and of Asia, Tychicus, and Trophimus.
These going before, tarried for us at Troas.
And e sailed aay from Philippi, after the days of unleavened bread, and came to them to Troas in five days; here e abode seven days.
And upon the first \add day\add* of the eek, hen the disciples came together to break bread, Paul preached to them (ready to depart on the morro) and continued his speech until midnight.
And there ere many lights in the upper chamber, here they ere assembled.
And there sat in a indo a certain young man named Eutychus, having fallen into a deep sleep: and as Paul as long preaching, he sunk don ith sleep, and fell from the third loft, and as taken up dead.
And Paul ent don, and fell on him, and embracing \add him\add* , said, Trouble not yourselves; for his life is in him.

And they brought the young man alive, and ere not a little comforted.
And e ent before to a ship, and sailed to Assos, there intending to take in Paul: for so he had appointed, intending himself to go on foot.
And hen he met ith us at Assos, e took him in, and came to Mitylene.
And e sailed thence, and came the next \add day\add* over against Chios; and the next \add day\add* e arrived at Samos, and tarried at Trogyllium; and the next \add day\add* e came to Miletus.

And from Miletus he sent to Ephesus, and called the elders of the church.
And hen they had come to him, he said to them, Ye kno, from the first day that I came into Asia, after hat manner I have been ith you at all seasons,
Serving the Lord ith all humility of mind, and ith many tears and temptations, hich befell me by the lying in ait of the Jes:
\add And\add* ho I kept back nothing that as profitable \add to you\add* , but have shon you, and have taught you publicly, and from house to house,
Testifying both to the Jes, and also to the Greeks, repentance toards God, and faith toards our Lord Jesus Christ.
And no behold, I go bound in the spirit to Jerusalem, not knoing the things that shall befall me there:

But none of these things move me, neither count I my life dear to myself, so that I may finish my course ith joy, and the ministry hich I have received from the Lord Jesus, to testify the gospel of the grace of God.

Wherefore I call you to itness this day, that I \add am\add* pure from the blood of all \add men\add* .
For I have not shunned to declare to you all the counsel of God.
Take heed therefore to yourselves, and to all the flock over hich the Holy Spirit hath made you overseers, to feed the church of God, hich he hath purchased ith his on blood.
For I kno this, that after my departure grievous olves ill enter in among you, not sparing the flock.
Also from your on selves ill men arise, speaking perverse things, to dra aay disciples after them.
Therefore atch, and remember, that by the space of three years I ceased not to arn every one night and day ith tears.
And no, brethren, I commend you to God, and to the ord of his grace, hich is able to build you up, and to give you an inheritance among all them ho are sanctified.
I have coveted no man’s silver, or gold, or apparel.
And ye yourselves kno, that these hands have ministered to my necessities, and to them that ere ith me.
I have shon you all things, that so laboring ye ought to support the eak, and to remember the ords of the Lord Jesus, that he said, It is more blessed to give than to receive.
And hen he had thus spoken, he kneeled don, and prayed ith them all.
And they all ept bitterly, and fell on Paul’s neck, and kissed him,
Sorroing most of all for the ords hich he spoke, that they should see his face no more. And they accompanied him to the ship.
And it came to pass, that after e ere separated from them, and had lanched, e came ith a straight course to Coos, and the \add day\add* folloing to Rhodes, and from thence to Patara:

And hen e had accomplished those days, e departed, and proceeded on our ay; and they all conducted us ith ives and children, till \add e ere\add* out of the city; and e kneeled don on the shore, and prayed.

And hen he ould not be persuaded, e ceased, saying, The ill of the Lord be done.

And the \add day\add* folloing Paul ent in ith us to James: and all the elders ere present.

Then Paul took the men, and the next day purifying himself ith them, entered into the temple, to signify the accomplishment of the days of purification, until an offering should be offered for every one of them.

But Paul said, I am a man \add ho am\add* a Je of Tarsus, \add a city\add* of Cilicia, a citizen of no mean city: and I beseech thee suffer me to speak to the people.
And hen he had given him license, Paul stood on the stairs, and beckoned ith the hand to the people. And hen there as made entire silence, he spoke to \add them\add* in the Hebre language, saying,
Men, brethren, and fathers, hear ye my defense \add hich I make\add* no to you.

As also the high priest doth bear me testimony, and all the estate of the elders; from hom also I received letters to the brethren, and ent to Damascus, to bring them ho ere there bound to Jerusalem, to be punished.

And they that ere ith me sa indeed the light, and ere afraid; but they heard not the voice of him that spoke to me.

And hen I could not see for the glory of that light, being led by the hand of them that ere ith me, I came into Damascus.

And he said to me, Depart: for I ill send thee far hence to the Gentiles.
And they gave him audience to this ord, and \add then\add* lifted up their voices, and said, Aay ith such a \add man\add* from the earth: for it is not fit that he should live.
And as they cried out, and cast off \add their\add* clothes, and thre dust into the air,
The chief captain commanded him to be brought into the castle, and bade that he should be examined by scourging; that he might kno for hat cause they cried so against him.
