All that are ith me salute thee. Greet them that love us in the faith. Grace \add be\add* ith you all. Amen.
Paul, a prisoner of Jesus Christ, and Timothy \add our\add* brother, to Philemon our dearly beloved, and fello-laborer,
And to \add our\add* beloved Apphia, and Archippus our fello-soldier, and to the church in thy house:
Grace to you, and peace, from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
I thank my God, making mention of thee alays in my prayers,
Hearing of thy love and faith, hich thou hast toards the Lord Jesus, and toards all saints;
That the communication of thy faith may become effectual by the acknoledging of every good thing hich is in you in Christ Jesus.
For e have great joy and consolation in thy love, because the boels of the saints are refreshed by thee, brother.
Wherefore, though I might be very bold in Christ to enjoin thee that hich is convenient.
Yet for love’s sake I rather beseech \add thee\add* , being such one as Paul the aged, and no also a prisoner of Jesus Christ.
I beseech thee for my son Onesimus, hom I have begotten in my bonds:
Who in time past as to thee unprofitable, but no profitable to thee and to me:
Whom I have sent again: thou therefore receive him, that is, my on boels:
Whom I ould have retained ith me, that in thy stead he might have ministered to me in the bonds of the gospel:
But ithout thy mind I ould do nothing; that thy benefit should not be as it ere of necessity, but illingly.
For perhaps he therefore departed for a season, that thou shouldst receive him for ever;
Not no as a servant, but above a servant, a brother beloved, specially to me, but ho much more to thee, both in the flesh, and in the Lord?
If thou accountest me therefore a partner, receive him as myself.
If he hath ronged thee, or oeth \add thee\add* aught, put that on my account;
I Paul have ritten \add it\add* ith my on hand, I ill repay \add it\add* : although I do not say to thee that thou oest to me even thy on self besides.
Yes, brother, let me have joy of thee in the Lord: refresh my boels in the Lord.
Having confidence in thy obedience I rote to thee, knoing that thou ilt also do more than I say.
But at the same time prepare me also a lodging; for I trust that through your prayers I shall be given to you.
There salute thee Epaphras, my fello-prisoner in Christ Jesus;
Marcus, Aristarchus, Demas, Lucas, my fello-laborers.
The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ \add be\add* ith your spirit. Amen.
God, ho at sundry times and in divers manners spoke in time past to the fathers by the prophets,
Hath in these last days spoken to us by \add his\add* Son, hom he hath appointed heir of all things, by hom also he made the orlds;

Who being the brightness of \add his\add* glory, and the express image of his person, and upholding all things by the ord of his poer, hen he had by himself made purification of our sins, sat don on the right hand of the Majesty on high;
Being made so much better than the angels, as he hath by inheritance obtained a more excellent name than they.
For to hich of the angels said he at any time, Thou art my Son, this day have I begotten thee? And again, I ill be to him a Father, and he shall be to me a Son?
And again, hen he bringeth in the first-begotten into the orld, he saith, And let all the angels of God orship him.
And of the angels he saith, Who maketh his angels spirits, and his ministers a flame of fire.
But to the Son, \add he saith\add* , Thy throne, O God, \add is\add* for ever and ever: a scepter of righteousness \add is\add* the scepter of thy kingdom.
Thou hast loved righteousness, and hated iniquity; therefore God, \add even\add* thy God, hath anointed thee ith the oil of gladness above thy fellos.
And, Thou, Lord, in the beginning hast laid the foundation of the earth: and the heavens are the orks of thy hands.
They shall perish; but thou remainest: and they all shall become old as doth a garment;
And as a vesture ilt thou fold them up, and they shall be changed; but thou art the same, and thy years shall not fail.
But to hich of the angels said he at any time, Sit on my right hand, until I make thy enemies thy footstool?
Are they not all ministering spirits, sent forth to minister for them ho shall inherit salvation?
Therefore e ought to give the more earnest heed to the things hich e have heard, lest at any time e should let \add them\add* slip.
For if the ord spoken by angels as steadfast, and every transgression and disobedience received a just recompense of reard;
Ho shall e escape, if e neglect so great salvation; hich at the first began to be spoken by the Lord, and as confirmed to us by them that heard \add him\add* ;
God also bearing \add them\add* testimony, both ith signs and onders, and ith divers miracles, and gifts of the Holy Spirit, according to his on ill?
For to the angels he hath not put in subjection the orld to come, concerning hich e speak.
But one in a certain place testified, saying, What is man, that thou art mindful of him? or the son of man, that thou visitest him?
Thou madest him a little loer than the angels; thou cronedst him ith glory and honor, and didst set him over the orks of thy hands:

Thou hast put all things in subjection under his feet. For in that he put all in subjection under him, he left nothing \add that is\add* not made subject to him. But no e see not yet all things subjected to him.
But e see Jesus, ho as made a little loer than the angels for the suffering of death, croned ith glory and honor; that he by the grace of God should taste death for every man.
For it became him, for hom \add are\add* all things, and by hom \add are\add* all things, in bringing many sons to glory, to make the Captain of their salvation perfect through sufferings.
For both he that sanctifieth, and they ho are sanctified, \add are\add* all of one: for hich cause he is not ashamed to call them brethren,
Saying, I ill declare thy name to my brethren, in the midst of the church ill I sing praise to thee.
And again, I ill put my trust in him. And again, Behold, I, and the children hich God hath given me.
Since then the children are partakers of flesh and blood, he also himself likeise took part of the same; that through death he might destroy him that had the poer of death, that is, the devil;
And deliver them, ho, through fear of death, ere all their life-time subject to bondage.
For verily he took not on \add him the nature of\add* angels; but he took on \add him\add* the seed of Abraham.

Wherefore in all things it behooved him to be made like \add his\add* brethren; that he might be a merciful and faithful High Priest in things \add pertaining\add* to God, to make reconciliation for the sins of the people.
For in that he himself hath suffered, being tempted, he is able to succor them that are tempted.
Wherefore, holy brethren, partakers of the heavenly calling, consider the Apostle and High Priest of our profession, Christ Jesus;
Who as faithful to him that appointed him, as also Moses \add as faithful\add* in all his house.
For this \add man\add* as counted orthy of more glory than Moses, inasmuch as he ho hath built the house, hath more honor than the house.
For every house is built by some \add man\add* ; but he that built all things \add is\add* God.
And Moses verily \add as\add* faithful in all his house, as a servant, for a testimony of those things hich ere \add afterards\add* to be spoken.
But Christ as a son over his on house: hose house are e, if e hold fast the confidence, and the rejoicing of the hope firm to the end.
Wherefore (as the Holy Spirit saith, To-day if ye ill hear his voice,
Harden not your hearts, as in the provocation, in the day of temptation in the ilderness:
When your fathers tempted me, proved me, and sa my orks forty years.
Wherefore I as grieved ith that generation, and said, They do alays err in \add their\add* heart; and they have not knon my ays.
So I sore in my rath, They shall not enter into my rest.)
Take heed, brethren, lest there be in any of you an evil heart of unbelief, in departing from the living God.
But exhort one another daily, hile it is called To-day; lest any of you be hardened through the deceitfulness of sin.
For e are made partakers of Christ, if e hold the beginning of our confidence steadfast to the end;
While it is said, To-day if ye ill hear his voice, harden not your hearts, as in the provocation.
For some, hen they had heard, did provoke: yet, not all that came out of Egypt by Moses.
But ith hom as he grieved forty years? \add as it\add* not ith them that had sinned, hose carcasses fell in the ilderness?
And to hom did he sear that they should not enter into his rest, but to them that believed not?
So e see that they could not enter in because of unbelief.
Let us therefore fear, lest a promise being left \add us\add* of entering into his rest, any of you should seem to come short of it.
For to us as the gospel preached, as ell as to them: but the ord hich they heard did not profit them, not being mixed ith faith in them that heard \add it\add* .
For e ho have believed do enter into rest, as he said, As I have sorn in my rath, if they shall enter into my rest: although the orks ere finished from the foundation of the orld.
For he spoke in a certain place of the seventh \add day\add* on this ise, And God rested the seventh day from all his orks.
And in this \add place\add* again, If they shall enter into my rest.
Seeing therefore it remaineth that some must enter into it, and they to hom it as first preached entered not because of unbelief:
(Again, he limiteth a certain day, saying in David, To-day, after so long a time; as it is said, To-day, if ye ill hear his voice, harden not your hearts.
For if Jesus had given them rest, then he ould not afterard have spoken of another day.
There remaineth therefore a rest to the people of God.
For he that hath entered into his rest, he also hath ceased from his on orks, as God \add did\add* from his.)
Let us labor therefore to enter into that rest, lest any man fall after the same example of unbelief.

For the ord of God \add is\add* living, and poerful, and sharper than any to-edged sord, piercing even to the dividing asunder of soul and spirit, and of the joints and marro, and \add is\add* a discerner of the thoughts and intents of the heart.
Neither is there any creature that is not manifest in his sight: but all things \add are\add* naked and opened to the eyes of him ith hom e have to do.
Seeing then that e have a great High Priest, that hath passed into the heavens, Jesus the Son of God, let us hold fast \add our\add* profession.
For e have not a high priest ho cannot be touched ith the feeling of our infirmities; but ho as in all points tempted as \add e are\add* , \add yet\add* ithout sin.
Let us therefore come boldly to the throne of grace, that e may obtain mercy, and find grace to help in time of need.
For every high priest taken from among men, is ordained for men in things \add pertaining\add* to God, that he may offer both gifts and sacrifices for sins:
Who can have compassion on the ignorant, and on them that are out of the ay; for that he himself also is compassed ith infirmity.
And by reason of this he ought, as for the people, so also for himself, to offer for sins.
And no man taketh this honor to himself, but he that is called by God, as \add as\add* Aaron:
So also Christ glorified not himself to be made a high priest; but he that said to him, Thou art my Son, to-day have I begotten thee.
As he saith also in another \add place\add* , Thou \add art\add* a priest for ever after the order of Melchisedec.
Who in the days of his flesh, hen he had offered up prayers and supplications ith strong crying and tears to him that as able to save him from death, and as heard, in that he feared;
Though he as a Son, yet he learned obedience by the things hich he suffered;
And being made perfect, he became the author of eternal salvation to all them that obey him;
Called by God a high priest after the order of Melchisedec.
Of hom e have many things to say, and hard to be uttered, seeing ye are dull of hearing.

For hen for the time ye ought to be teachers, ye have need of one to teach you again hich \add are\add* the first principles of the oracles of God; and are become such as have need of milk, and not of strong food.
For every one that useth milk, \add is\add* unskillful in the ord of righteousness: for he is a babe.
But strong food belongeth to them that are of full age, \add even\add* those ho by reason of use have their senses exercised to discern both good and evil.
Therefore leaving the principles of the doctrine of Christ, let us go on to perfection; not laying again the foundation of repentance from dead orks, and of faith toards God,
Of the doctrine of baptisms, and of laying on of hands, and of the resurrection of the dead, and of eternal judgment.
And this ill e do, if God permit.
For \add it is\add* impossible for those ho have been once enlightened, and have tasted the heavenly gift, and have been made partakers of the Holy Spirit.
And have tasted the good ord of God, and the poers of the orld to come,
If they shall fall aay, to rene them again to repentance; seeing they crucify to themselves the Son of God afresh, and put \add him\add* to an open shame.
For the earth hich drinketh in the rain that cometh often upon it, and bringeth forth herbs fit for them by hom it is dressed, receiveth blessing from God:
But that hich beareth thorns and briers \add is\add* rejected, and \add is\add* nigh to cursing; hose end \add is\add* to be burned.
But, beloved, e are persuaded better things of you, and things that accompany salvation, though e thus speak.
For God \add is\add* not unrighteous to forget your ork and labor of love, hich ye have shon toards his name, in that ye have ministered to the saints, and do minister.
And e desire every one of you to sho the same diligence to the full assurance of hope to the end:
That ye be not slothful, but folloers of them ho through faith and patience inherit the promises.
For hen God made promise to Abraham, because he could sear by no greater, he sore by himself,
Saying, Surely blessing I ill bless thee, and multiplying I ill multiply thee.
And so, after he had patiently endured, he obtained the promise.
For men verily sear by the greater: and an oath for confirmation \add is\add* to them an end of all contradiction.
Wherein God, illing more abundantly to sho to the heirs of promise the immutability of his counsel, confirmed \add it\add* by an oath:
That by to immutable things, in hich \add it as\add* impossible for God to lie, e might have a strong consolation, ho have fled for refuge to lay hold upon the hope set before us:
Which \add hope\add* e have as an anchor of the soul, both sure and steadfast, and hich entereth into that ithin the vail;
Whither the forerunner hath for us entered, \add even\add* Jesus, made a high priest for ever after the order of Melchisedec.
For this Melchisedec, king of Salem, priest of the most high God, ho met Abraham returning from the slaughter of the kings, and blessed him;
To hom also Abraham gave a tenth part of all; first being by interpretation King of righteousness, and after that also King of Salem, hich is, King of peace;
Without father, ithout mother, ithout descent, having neither beginning of days, nor end of life; but made like to the Son of God; abideth a priest continually.
No consider ho great this man \add as\add* , to hom even the patriarch Abraham gave the tenth of the spoils.

And verily they that are of the sons of Levi, ho receive the office of the priesthood, have a commandment to take tithes from the people according to the la, that is, from their brethren, though they come from the loins of Abraham:
But he hose descent is not counted from them received tithes from Abraham, and blessed him that had the promises.
And ithout all contradiction the less is blessed by the better.
And here men that die receive tithes; but there he \add receiveth them\add* , of hom it is testified that he liveth.
And as I may say, Levi also, ho receiveth tithes, payed tithes in Abraham.
For he as yet in the loins of his father, hen Melchisedec met him.

If therefore perfection ere by the Levitical priesthood (for under it the people received the la) hat further need \add as there\add* that another priest should rise after the order of Melchisedec, and not be called after the order of Aaron?
For the priesthood being changed, there is made of necessity a change also of the la.
For he of hom these things are spoken pertaineth to another tribe, of hich no man gave attendance at the altar.
For \add it is\add* evident that our Lord sprang from Judah; of hich tribe Moses spoke nothing concerning priesthood.
And it is yet far more evident: for that after the similitude of Melchisedec there ariseth another priest,
Who is made, not after the la of a carnal commandment, but after the poer of an endless life.
For he testifieth, Thou \add art\add* a priest for ever after the order of Melchisedec.
For there is verily a disannulling of the preceding commandment on account of its eakness and unprofitableness.
For the la made nothing perfect, but the introduction of a better hope \add did\add* ; by hich e dra nigh to God.
And inasmuch as not ithout an oath \add he as made priest\add* :
(For those priests ere made ithout an oath; but this ith an oath, by him that said to him, The Lord sore, and ill not repent, Thou \add art\add* a priest for ever after the order of Melchisedec:)
By so much as Jesus made a surety of a better testament.

Wherefore he is able also to save them to the uttermost that come to God by him, seeing he ever liveth to make intercession for them.
For such a high priest became us, \add ho is\add* holy, harmless, undefiled, separate from sinners, and made higher than the heavens;

No of the things hich e have spoken \add this is\add* the sum: We have such a high priest, ho is set on the right hand of the throne of the Majesty in the heavens;

For every high priest is ordained to offer gifts and sacrifices: herefore \add it is\add* of necessity that this man should have somehat also to offer.
For if he ere on earth, he ould not be a priest, seeing there are priests that offer gifts according to the la:

Who serve to the example and shado of heavenly things, as Moses as admonished by God hen he as about to make the tabernacle: for, See (saith he) \add that\add* thou make all things according to the pattern shon to thee in the mount.
But no hath he obtained a more excellent ministry, by ho much also he is the mediator of a better covenant, hich as established upon better promises.
For if that first \add covenant\add* had been faultless, then ould no place have been sought for the second.
For finding fault ith them, he saith, Behold, the days come, saith the Lord, hen I ill make a ne covenant ith the house of Israel and ith the house of Judah:

Not according to the covenant that I made ith their fathers, in the day hen I took them by the hand to lead them out of the land of Egypt; because they continued not in my covenant, and I regarded them not, saith the Lord.

For this \add is\add* the covenant that I ill make ith the house of Israel after those days, saith the Lord; I ill put my las into their mind, and rite them in their hearts: and I ill be to them a God, and they shall be to me a people:

For I ill be merciful to their unrighteousness, and their sins and their iniquities ill I remember no more.
In that he saith, A ne \add covenant\add* , he hath made the first old. No that hich decayeth and groeth old \add is\add* ready to vanish aay.

For there as a tabernacle made; the first, in hich \add as\add* the candlestick, and the table, and the sho-bread; hich is called the sanctuary.
And after the second vail, the tabernacle hich is called the Holiest of all;
Which had the golden censer, and the ark of the covenant overlaid around ith gold, in hich \add as\add* the golden pot that had manna, and Aaron’s rod that budded, and the tables of the covenant;
And over it the cherubim of glory shadoing the mercy-seat; of hich e cannot no speak particularly.
No hen these things ere thus ordained, the priests ent alays into the first tabernacle, accomplishing the service \add of God\add* :
But into the second \add ent\add* the high priest alone once every year, not ithout blood, hich he offered for himself, and \add for\add* the errors of the people:
The Holy Spirit this signifying, that the ay into the holiest of all as not yet made manifest, hile the first tabernacle as yet standing:
Which \add as\add* a figure for the time then present, in hich ere offered both gifts and sacrifices, that could not make him that did the service perfect, as pertaining to the conscience;
\add Which stood\add* only in meats and drinks, and divers ashings, and carnal ordinances, imposed \add on them\add* until the time of reformation.
But Christ being come a high priest of good things to come, by a greater and more perfect tabernacle, not made ith hands, that is to say, not of this building;
Neither by the blood of goats and calves, but by his on blood; he entered in once into the holy place, having obtained eternal redemption \add for us\add* .
For if the blood of bulls and of goats, and the ashes of a heifer sprinkling the unclean, sanctify to the purifying of the flesh:
Ho much more shall the blood of Christ, ho through the eternal Spirit offered himself ithout spot to God, cleanse your conscience from dead orks to serve the living God?

And for this cause he is the mediator of the ne testament, that by means of death, for the redemption of the transgressions \add that ere\add* under the first testament, they ho are called may receive the promise of eternal inheritance.
For here a testament \add is\add* , there must also of necessity be the death of the testator.
For a testament \add is\add* of force after men are dead: otherise it is of no strength at all hile the testator liveth.
Hence even the first \add testament\add* as not dedicated ithout blood.

For hen Moses had spoken every precept to all the people according to the la, he took the blood of calves and of goats, ith ater, and scarlet ool, and hyssop, and sprinkled both the book and all the people,
Saying, This \add is\add* the blood of the testament hich God hath enjoined to you.
Moreover, he sprinkled likeise ith blood both the tabernacle, and all the vessels of the ministry.
And almost all things are by the la cleansed ith blood; and ithout shedding of blood is no remission.
\add It as\add* therefore necessary that the patterns of things in the heavens should be purified ith these; but the heavenly things themselves ith better sacrifices than these.
For Christ hath not entered into the holy places made ith hands, \add hich are\add* the figures of the true; but into heaven itself, no to appear in the presence of God for us:
Nor yet that he should offer himself often, as the high priest entereth into the holy place every year ith blood of others;
For then must he often have suffered since the foundation of the orld: but no once in the end of the orld hath he appeared to put aay sin by the sacrifice of himself.
And as it is appointed to men once to die, but after this the judgment:
So Christ as once offered to bear the sins of many; and to them that look for him he ill appear the second time ithout sin to salvation.

For the la having a shado of good things to come, \add and\add* not the very image of the things, can never ith those sacrifices hich they offered year by year continually make the comers to \add them\add* perfect.
For then ould they not have ceased to be offered? because that the orshipers once cleansed, ould have had no more conscience of sins.
But in those \add sacrifices there is\add* a remembrance again \add made\add* of sins every year.
For \add it is\add* not possible that the blood of bulls and of goats should take aay sins.
Wherefore, hen he cometh into the orld, he saith, Sacrifice and offering thou ouldst not, but a body hast thou prepared me:
In burnt-offerings and \add sacrifices\add* for sin thou hast had no pleasure.
Then said I, Lo, I come (in the volume of the book it is ritten concerning me,) to do thy ill, O God.
Above, hen he said, Sacrifice and offering and burnt-offerings and \add offering\add* for sin thou ouldst not, neither hadst pleasure \add in them\add* ; hich are offered by the la;
Then said he, Lo, I come to do thy ill, O God. He taketh aay the first, that he may establish the second.
By hich ill e are sanctified through the offering of the body of Jesus Christ once \add for all\add* .
And every priest standeth daily ministering and offering often the same sacrifices, hich can never take aay sins:
But this man, after he had offered one sacrifice for sins, for ever sat don on the right hand of God;
From henceforth aiting till his enemies are made his footstool.
For by one offering he hath perfected for ever them that are sanctified.
\add Of this\add* the Holy Spirit also is a itness to us: for after that he had said before,
This \add is\add* the covenant that I ill make ith them after those days, saith the Lord, I ill put my las into their hearts, and in their minds ill I rite them;
And their sins and iniquities ill I remember no more.
No here remission of these \add is\add* , \add there is\add* no more offering for sin.
Having therefore, brethren, boldness to enter into the holiest by the blood of Jesus,
By a ne and living ay, hich he hath consecrated for us, through the vail, that is to say, his flesh;
And \add having\add* a high priest over the house of God;
Let us dra near ith a true heart in full assurance of faith, having our hearts sprinkled from an evil conscience, and our bodies ashed ith pure ater.
Let us hold fast the profession of \add our\add* faith ithout avering; for he \add is\add* faithful that promised:
And let us consider one another to excite to love and to good orks:
Not forsaking the assembling of ourselves, as the manner of some \add is\add* ; but exhorting \add one another\add* : and so much the more, as ye see the day approaching.
For if e sin illfully after e have received the knoledge of the truth, there remaineth no more sacrifice for sins,
But a certain fearful apprehension of judgment and fiery indignation, hich shall devour the adversaries.
He that despised Moses’ la, died ithout mercy under to or three itnesses:

Of ho much more severe punishment, suppose ye, shall he be thought orthy, ho hath trodden under foot the Son of God, and hath counted the blood of the covenant, by hich he as sanctified, an unholy thing, and hath done despite to the Spirit of grace?
For e kno him that hath said, Vengeance \add belongeth\add* to me, I ill recompense, saith the Lord. And again, The Lord ill judge his people.
\add It is\add* a fearful thing to fall into the hands of the living God.
But call to remembrance the former days, in hich, after ye ere illuminated, ye endured a great fight of afflictions;
Partly, hile ye ere made a gazing-stock both by reproaches and afflictions; and partly, hile ye became companions of them that ere so used.
For ye had compassion of me in my bonds, and took joyfully the seizing of your goods, knoing in yourselves that ye have in heaven a better and an enduring substance.
Cast not aay therefore your confidence, hich hath great recompense of reard.
For ye have need of patience, that, after ye have done the ill of God, ye may receive the promise.
For yet a little hile, and he that is coming ill come, and ill not tarry.
No the just shall live by faith: but if \add any man\add* shall dra back, my soul shall have no pleasure in him.
But e are not of them ho dra back to perdition; but of them that believe to the saving of the soul.
No faith is the substance of things hoped for, the evidence of things not seen.
For by it the elders obtained a good report.
Through faith e understand that the orlds ere framed by the ord of God, so that things hich are seen ere not made of things hich appeared.
By faith Abel offered to God a more excellent sacrifice than Cain, by hich he obtained testimony that he as righteous, God testifying of his gifts: and by it he being dead yet speaketh.
By faith Enoch as translated, that he should not see death; and as not found, because God had translated him: for before his translation he had this testimony, that he pleased God.
But ithout faith \add it is\add* impossible to please \add him\add* : for he that cometh to God must believe that he is, and \add that\add* he is a rearder of them that diligently seek him.

By faith Noah, being arned by God of things not seen as yet, moved ith fear, prepared an ark to the saving of his house; by hich he condemned the orld, and became heir of the righteousness hich is by faith.
